title: rc dev list reads only cwd-relative state file — drifts from live AWS, hides billing boxes
description:
DevHostService.list_hosts() returns ONLY the local .rc/dev-hosts.yml state, which is a CWD-RELATIVE path. Consequences: (1) run 'rc dev list' from a different directory than where the box was launched -> 'No dev hosts' while t4g.large boxes silently BILL; (2) the state file drifts from AWS (partial-failure leaks, out-of-band stops/destroys, stale status); (3) status shown is frozen in the file, not live.

LIVE INCIDENT (2026-06-11): 'rc dev list' showed 'No dev hosts' while 2 t4g.large boxes (alice2, e2e-timeout-2026-06-10) + 2 triage-* boxes were RUNNING + billing in us-west-1. Earlier leak (rc-xiq) noted 13 boxes + 7 EIPs leaked over 24h.

Instances ARE tagged ManagedBy=rc-dev + DevHost=<name>, so AWS is the real source of truth. Fix: rc dev list must reconcile against live AWS (describe_instances Filter tag:ManagedBy=rc-dev), independent of cwd, and flag boxes that exist in AWS but not in local state (untracked leaks) + boxes in state but gone from AWS (stale). Add --all-regions to sweep every region (leaks hide in unexpected regions). Consider moving the state file to a per-user location (~/.rc) so it stops being cwd-relative.
design: TDD. RED: DevHostService.reconcile_live(region->client map or factory) merges describe_instances(tag:ManagedBy=rc-dev) with _load_state, returns records tagged tracked/untracked/stale + live status. Mock ec2.describe_instances. BUILD + wire rc dev list (--region/--all-regions). Relates to rc-xiq (leak).
acceptance_criteria: rc dev list reflects live AWS (tag ManagedBy=rc-dev) regardless of cwd; shows live status/type/ip/launch-time; flags untracked (AWS-only) and stale (state-only) boxes; --all-regions sweeps all regions; existing behavior preserved when AWS unreachable (falls back to state w/ a warning).

title: ignore_task_definition_changes must also ignore aws_ecs_service.task_definition (terraform reverts reconcile pointer -> roll churn)
description:
ignore_task_definition_changes emits lifecycle ignore_changes=[container_definitions] on the TASK DEFINITION, but the aws_ecs_service still hardcodes task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.<svc>.arn with NO ignore_changes. So when a reconcile script (or rc force-roll) registers a NEW task def revision and points the service at it, the next terraform apply REVERTS the service pointer back to terraform's own (old) revision -> the service rolls to the stripped-env revision (roll #1), then reconcile re-points it (roll #2).

LIVE INCIDENT (browser-mgr prod 2026-06-11, run 27376376534): terraform plan reverted EVERY service: postgres :17->:5, django :14->:1, celeryworker :4->:1, celerybeat :15->:1, browserworker :20->:6. postgres (single-task EFS, min_healthy=0) rolled -> Cloud Map DNS gap -> [Errno -2] on dependents + the deploy's browser-session gate FAILED. The point of ignore_task_definition_changes (let reconcile own the task def) is defeated because terraform still owns the service's pointer.

FIX: when ignore_task_definition_changes=true, also emit lifecycle { ignore_changes = [task_definition] } on aws_ecs_service. Then terraform creates the service initially but never reverts the out-of-band pointer; reconcile/force-roll own task-def updates. Opt-in + additive (default path unchanged).
design: TDD: extend test_ignore_task_def_changes.py — RED: assert 'ignore_changes = [task_definition]' present on the service when flag on; absent by default. BUILD: add lifecycle block to aws_ecs_service in services.tf.j2 gated on ignore_task_definition_changes. GREEN: tests + golden byte-identical. Relates to [[rc-7ga]] (deploy churn) + [[rc-uky]] (field-level ownership).
acceptance_criteria: With ignore_task_definition_changes=true, services.tf emits ignore_changes=[task_definition] on aws_ecs_service; a terraform apply does NOT revert a reconcile-applied task def pointer (no roll for unchanged services); default path byte-identical (golden green). browser-mgr deploy stops rolling postgres + dependents.
close_reason: Fixed: ignore_task_definition_changes now also emits ignore_changes=[task_definition] on aws_ecs_service (commit 00f1fd6). VERIFIED in prod (browser-mgr run 27377391766): terraform plan no longer reverts service pointers, postgres did NOT roll (startedAt unchanged), session gate passed. TDD red->green, 363 tests incl golden byte-identical.

title: Determine browser topology: what must rc deploy vs external SaaS
description: Resolve the key unknown before designing: where do browsers + VNC actually run in prod? (a) inside the celery-browser worker via local Xvfb/Chromium, (b) a self-hosted 'browser-mgr' service (which repo/deploy?), or (c) browserless SaaS (BROWSERLESS_API_KEY). Inspect backend/browser_sessions/* + browser-mgr client code + live ECS. Output: the exact set of services rc must deploy for the browser stack. GATES the rest of this epic.
close_reason: Topology answered: browsers+VNC live in separate debugg-ai/browser-mgr (migrates to rc later, rc-z0k). sentinal celery-browser is just a worker connecting out.

title: celery-browser worker on rc (sentinal blocker — worker only)
description: BLOCKER for the sentinal Copilot->rc migration (see sentinal beads epic sentinal-vmj6). DebuggAI's core E2E workload is a browser-automation stack that must deploy via rc before sentinal can cut over. Today under Copilot: celery-browser = Worker Service (4 vCPU/8GB, image debugg-ai-web/backend-celery-browser, browser-use over CDP, DISPLAY=:99 + Xvfb + x11vnc + VNC_PASSWORD). The Dockerfile header says it 'controls REMOTE browsers via CDP, with local Playwright fallback for local dev' — and the app reads vnc_url from a SEPARATE 'browser-mgr' service (bmgr_session.vnc_url = ws://host/vnc/{id}/websockify) used by the frontend for live browser view. So browsers+VNC live in browser-mgr, NOT the worker. WHERE browser-mgr runs (this repo? another repo? browserless SaaS via BROWSERLESS_API_KEY?) is the key unknown. rc ALREADY supports: per-service cpu/memory (4096/8192), ECS execute-command, Service Connect/Cloud Map, non-ALB extra_ports. LIKELY GAPS: WebSocket/VNC ingress with per-session path routing (ws://.../vnc/{id}/websockify) on the ALB, Chromium-on-Fargate /dev/shm sizing, and validating the existing browser image runs unmodified under rc.
design: Phase 1 = determine topology (what must rc deploy vs what's external SaaS). Phase 2 = celery-browser worker on rc (verify, likely small gaps). Phase 3 = the hard part: browser-mgr/VNC ingress — ALB WebSocket listener + per-session path routing to /websockify, or NLB; plus Chromium /dev/shm + ephemeral storage. Phase 4 = e2e validation incl frontend live-view.
acceptance_criteria: rc can deploy the full browser-automation stack faithfully: the celery-browser worker (4vCPU/8GB, exec, Service Connect, full secrets) AND whatever provides browsers+VNC (browser-mgr or browserless), with frontend-reachable VNC live-view (ws://.../websockify). Validated end-to-end on a dev rc stack: a real browser session runs and its vnc_url renders live in the frontend.

title: [bug] v1_migrate translator import addresses don't match v2 ECSProvider's actual emitted resources
description: Phase 4.1 translators emit imports targeting module.efs.aws_efs_file_system.this etc. But the v2 ECSProvider emits flat resources: aws_lb.main, aws_acm_certificate.main, aws_subnet.public[count.index], aws_security_group.alb, aws_ecs_cluster.main, etc. Running terraform apply with current imports would either fail or recreate resources — defeats zero-data-loss premise. Also need to audit shape mismatches: 5 prod SGs vs 2 v2-emitted, 2 prod subnets vs public/private split, 7 EFS APs vs unknown v2 emission shape.
close_reason: Pivoted from terraform-import to boto3-only cutover. v1 prod is imperatively-deployed (no terraform state to import into), and v2 ECSProvider templates are greenfield-shaped. The actual migration is an ECS task-def shape change: read existing v1 task def via boto3, replace secrets[]= with ARN-by-key refs from plan.secret_arn_map, drop env keys colliding with secrets, register new revision, update_service to roll. EFS/ALB/SM/cert/DNS untouched. Tested against moto sandbox: 3 services rolled, all secrets ARN'd, env collisions dropped, image+mounts preserved, tripwire confirms zero mutation of stateful resources. 95 v1_migrate tests green (+6 net), 1483 unit+contract regression green. Terraform phases (emit/import) kept as opt-in --phase for future BYO-existing v2 ECSProvider work.

title: (EPIC) rc-only acceptance — start-simpli deploys + workers green via pure rc commands
description: If rc deploys real Django + celery systems require ANY out-of-band tooling — manual /tmp/docker-compose.ecs-test.yml, hand-written nginx.conf, sed-fixed resolver IPs, manual aws ecs commands to inspect state, curl -H Host: header tricks, etc. — then rc does not work. The 2026-04-26 start-simpli loop demonstrates this: shipping a working stack required ~6 hours of out-of-band work (hand-writing compose/ecs/nginx/{Dockerfile,nginx.conf}, copying compose files to /tmp with sed-rewritten paths, manual rc secrets push, manual aws ecs describe-services to find stuck task defs, manual celery worker reconciliation). Most of those individual gaps now have fixes (.44.18/.19, .44.20, .44.21, .44.22, .44.24, .45.11) but the FULL chain has never been re-run end-to-end with the fixes in place. THIS bead is the rc-product acceptance test: from a clean state (rc destroy --all-ephemeral), running ONLY rc commands, we ship a fully-green start-simpli stack. Every gap discovered during this run becomes a child bead under this epic. Until this bead closes green, rc does not work for production Django systems — it works for synthetic demo apps.
acceptance_criteria: From a clean machine state with /tmp/rc.local.yml deleted + all rc-test-startsimpli AWS resources destroyed: a SCRIPTED bash trace using ONLY rc commands (no aws cli, no docker compose, no sed, no editing files outside the user's project tree, no manual /tmp/docker-compose.ecs-test.yml, no curl -H Host:) brings up a fully-green start-simpli stack. Specifically: (1) 'rc up --from-compose /Users/qosha/Repos/start-simpli/start-simpli-api/docker-compose.local.yml --aws-profile default --region us-west-1 --ttl 4h -c /tmp/rc.local.yml' starts from no rc.yml + ends with a printed ALB URL; (2) After the deploy, 'rc status' shows ALL 6 services (django, celery-worker, celery-beat, nginx, postgres, redis) at running=desired with health=healthy + no STALE markers; (3) plain 'curl http://<ALB-URL>/api/v1/health/' (no Host header rewrite) returns HTTP 200 with body containing '"celery":"healthy"' (real workers responding to ping, not 'no_workers'); (4) 'rc destroy --yes' tears it down clean leaving zero resources tagged Project=rc-test-startsimpli. Trace lives in scripts/test-startsimpli-end-to-end.sh and is invoked WITHOUT arguments from the remote-compose repo root. Failures during the run get filed as child beads under this epic.
close_reason: ALL acceptance criteria met. Verified 2026-04-27 with scripts/test-startsimpli-end-to-end.sh exiting clean 7/7 against real us-west-1: rc up --from-compose deploys start-simpli end-to-end (django+celery-worker+celery-beat+nginx+postgres+redis all healthy), ALB serves 200 with celery:healthy in body, rc destroy cleans up + unregisters from ephemeral registry. Children all closed: .46.1-.46.11 + rc-3q9 (auto_on_deploy hook deferral). Plus .47 (framework presets), .46.7 (rc up --domain) shipped on top.

title: e5u.44.3: 'rc init' must default to v2 schema (currently emits v1, breaking 'rc plan')
description: Verified 2026-04-25: 'rc init' writes RC_TEMPLATE from cli.py which uses top-level cluster:/region:/compose_file:/project_name: (v1). README and the rest of the v2 code path expect version: 2 / project: / provider: ecs / provider_config: ecs:. Running 'rc plan' against a fresh init bombs with 'rc plan requires a rc.yml v2 config. Run rc migrate first.' Default 'rc init' to v2; gate v1 behind --v1 for legacy. Drop the 'yourusername/django-remote-compose' placeholder URL in the template comments.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh 'rc init' followed by 'rc plan -c rc.yml' does NOT print the 'requires a rc.yml v2 config' error. Generated rc.yml has 'version: 2' as the first non-comment key. 'rc init --v1' continues to emit the legacy template.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-25. Renamed RC_TEMPLATE -> RC_TEMPLATE_V1 (no other refs), added RC_TEMPLATE_V2 with the v2 schema (version:2, project:, provider:ecs, provider_config: ecs:, terraform: backend, services:, optional secrets/backup/compose blocks). 'rc init' uses v2 by default; 'rc init --v1' opts in to legacy. Acceptance run in /tmp/rc-init-test against /tmp/rc-verify-venv/bin/rc: (1) Fresh 'rc init' + 'rc -c rc.yml plan' prints 'Remote Compose v2 — provider=ecs project=my-project'; the 'requires a rc.yml v2' string appears 0 times. The only error is unrelated FileNotFoundError on terraform binary (covered by .44.4). (2) Generated rc.yml first non-comment key is 'version: 2'. (3) 'rc init --v1' produces a file whose first non-comment key is 'cluster: my-cluster' (legacy schema). Files: cli.py lines 23-100 (templates), 821-840 (init command).

title: e5u.44.1: declare [ecs] extra in pyproject.toml so pip install -e ".[ecs]" actually installs the v2 deps
description: Verified 2026-04-25: pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] only declares 'celery' and 'dev'. README documents 'pip install -e ".[ecs]"' as the install command for the v2/ECS path. pip emits 'WARNING: django-remote-compose 0.1.0 does not provide the extra ecs' and silently installs base deps only. Result: click is missing, python -m remote_compose.cli fails with ModuleNotFoundError. Bundle: click, python-hcl2, jinja2, boto3 (already in base), pyyaml (already in base). Mirror to setup.py extras_require for symmetry.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh venv: pip install -e ".[ecs]" prints no extras-not-found warning; python -m remote_compose.cli --help runs and lists commands; python -c "import click, hcl2, jinja2" exits 0.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-25. Added click>=8.0 to base dependencies (any CLI use needs it, not just ECS) and created [ecs] extra with python-hcl2>=4.3 and jinja2>=3.1. Mirrored to setup.py. Acceptance run on fresh /tmp/rc-verify-venv: 'pip install -e ".[ecs]"' completed with no extras-not-found warning; 'python -c "import click, hcl2, jinja2"' exits 0 (click 8.3.3, hcl2 ok, jinja2 3.1.6); 'python -m remote_compose.cli --help' renders the full command list. Files: pyproject.toml lines 28-39, setup.py lines 14-26.

title: e5u.44.2: add [project.scripts] entry point so 'rc' lands on PATH after pip install
description: Verified 2026-04-25: 'which rc' returns nothing after pip install -e .; pyproject.toml has no [project.scripts] block and setup.py has no entry_points kwarg. README quick-start (rc init, rc plan, rc deploy, rc destroy) is aspirational — every example tells the user to run 'rc' but the package does not install a 'rc' shim. Add [project.scripts] rc = "remote_compose.cli:cli" so the click root command (cli.py) becomes the binary.
acceptance_criteria: After pip install -e ".[ecs]" in a fresh venv, 'which rc' returns the venv's bin path; 'rc --help' produces identical output to 'python -m remote_compose.cli --help'.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-25. Added [project.scripts] rc = "remote_compose.cli:cli" to pyproject.toml; mirrored entry_points={'console_scripts': ['rc=remote_compose.cli:cli']} to setup.py. Acceptance run on fresh /tmp/rc-verify-venv: 'pip install -e ".[ecs]"' creates /tmp/rc-verify-venv/bin/rc; 'rc --help' renders the full command list. The output diff vs 'python -m remote_compose.cli --help' is exactly one line — the 'Usage:' program name ('rc' vs 'python -m remote_compose.cli') — which click derives from argv[0] and is unavoidable. Substantively identical otherwise. Files: pyproject.toml lines 53-54, setup.py lines 22-26.

title: (EPIC) rc copilot import — migrate ANY AWS Copilot app to rc.yml v2 (Copilot is EOS)
description: AWS Copilot has been declared end-of-service. Every team running on Copilot needs a path off it before AWS deprecates the tooling. 'rc copilot import' is THE migration: read /copilot/ (services, environments, addons, pipelines) on any repo, emit a working rc.yml v2 + docker-compose.yml. Sentinal (15 services, 4 service types, 3 envs) is the reference fixture but the tool must work on any Copilot app — not hand-rolled to sentinal's quirks. Test corpus expanded to include the official Copilot examples repo so we cover Backend / LBWS / Worker / Request-Driven / Static Site at minimum. P0 because the alternative is teams hand-translating CFN-derived YAML to terraform, which kills adoption.
close_reason: All 11 children shipped (.43.1-.43.11). rc copilot import translates copilot/ tree → rc.yml v2 + docker-compose.yml + IMPORT_SUMMARY.md, with addon CFN-template detection + per-AWS-resource-type guidance (.43.8 final). Tested against sentinal (15 services) + aws-cli corpus (LBWS, app-with-domain, static-site) + external community apps. CFN-tolerant YAML loader handles !Ref/!Sub/!GetAtt intrinsics.

title: NEXT AGENT — Start here: portable-deploy branch status + priority order
description: Orientation for the next agent picking up this work. Read this first. Branch: portable-deploy (2 commits ahead of main, pushed to origin). Main branch untouched so production start-simpli-api deploys keep working through the legacy v1 pipeline. What is DONE and verified end-to-end against real AWS (us-east-1, topmarq-web-staging account 319712925602): Provider ABC + FakeProvider + contract test suite (rc-e5u.1-6); rc.yml v2 schema + rc migrate CLI (rc-e5u.9); full ECS provider — emit_terraform + deploy + destroy + plan + redeploy + status + logs + exec + rollback + EC2 launch type + EFS volumes + secrets integration + domain/ACM/Route53 + contract registration (rc-e5u.7, 12-17); ECS validation tooling — golden-file snapshots, HCL structural tests, moto-backed boto3 integration (rc-e5u.18); rc doctor / rc install for dependency preflight (rc-e5u.21); Sample demo app (URL shortener, FastAPI + worker + postgres + redis) that deploys end-to-end on real AWS — 9 smoke iterations to green (rc-e5u.22); CLI dispatch for rc.yml v2 → Provider methods (rc-e5u.23); Image build + ECR push + forceNewDeployment in provider.deploy (rc-e5u.24); E2E test scaffolding with isolation via rc-test-* tag + reap script (rc-e5u.19-20).
design: READ THESE DOCS FIRST: ARCHITECTURE.md (root) — full system design, 9-rung validation ladder, demo app runbook; examples/demo-app/README.md — reference app with local + cloud smoke commands; .beads/issues.jsonl — canonical bead state (bd bootstrap after cloning or switching branches).  LOCAL BASELINE: rc doctor should show all green on any supported Mac/Linux box; pytest tests/unit/ tests/contract/ → 486 passed, 4 skipped; pytest tests/integration/ → 6 passed if terraform binary works; RC_E2E=1 pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/ → 4 passed against real AWS in ~25min / </bin/zsh.10.  PRIORITY ORDER FOR REMAINING WORK: P1 — (a) rc-e5u.28 migrate start-simpli-api from v1 to v2 rc.yml + cut over prod deploy to the new provider (biggest user-facing win). P2 — (b) rc-e5u.8 Kubernetes provider (proves 'multi-cloud' claim); (c) rc-e5u.25 private-subnet + NAT option for EC2 workers (currently Fargate in public subnets for cost); (d) rc-e5u.26 EFS encryption on fresh accounts (KMS key creation). P3 — (e) rc-e5u.27 Postgres-on-EFS uid; (f) rc-e5u.10 deprecate legacy imperative services once start-simpli is on v2.  KNOWN LIMITATIONS documented in ARCHITECTURE.md: private-subnet routing not yet wired; db persistence on ECS/EFS has postgres uid issue (production users should use RDS); custom domain requires pre-existing Route 53 zone; no --json CLI output; Service Connect vs plain Cloud Map split not fully evaluated.  COMMITS OF NOTE: 5c67f30 foundation, eedb780 demo app + CLI dispatch + image build.
acceptance_criteria: Next agent reads this bead, ARCHITECTURE.md, and examples/demo-app/README.md, runs 'rc doctor' + the unit/contract suite as a local baseline, then picks an item from bd ready and ships it.

title: Secrets Manager ARN uses literal REGION/ACCOUNT placeholders
description: compose_converter.py:803-804 generates ARN 'arn:aws:secretsmanager:REGION:ACCOUNT:secret:{name}' with literal strings REGION and ACCOUNT never replaced. Task definitions will contain invalid ARNs. Fix: accept region/account_id as parameters (available from cluster) or raise ComposeConversionError.
close_reason: Real ARNs in valueFrom: arn:aws:secretsmanager:<region>:<account>:secret:<name>. Constructor takes account_id; _convert_secrets takes region per-call (sourced from cluster.aws_region). Missing account_id with secrets present raises ComposeConversionError. 9 tests + converter regression suite green.

title: assignPublicIp ENABLED hardcoded for all Fargate tasks
description: ecs_service.py:753 hardcodes assignPublicIp='ENABLED' for every Fargate task including those in private subnets. Exposes containers to internet unnecessarily. Fix: make configurable, default to DISABLED when cluster has private subnets. Model field exists (ecs.py has AssignPublicIp choices) but is not wired through.
close_reason: assignPublicIp now inferred from cluster.has_public_subnets (when present), else describe_subnets boto3 fallback, else True for back-compat. Both call sites (ECSService.run_task + ECSService model service_def) updated. 8 new unit tests + 251 service regression suite green.

title: EFS defaults to root UID/GID 0 with 0777 permissions
description: efs_service.py:40-43 sets DEFAULT_UID=0, DEFAULT_GID=0, DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS='0777'. All access points get root+world-writable by default. Docstring at line 498-499 LIES claiming defaults are 1000/1000/0755. Fix: default to 1000/1000/0755, fix docstring, offer permissive settings only as named constants for specific use cases.
close_reason: EFS access-point defaults flipped from 0/0/0777 (root + world-writable) to 1000/1000/0755 (matches docstring + v2 ECS provider). Permissive 0/0/0777 retained as opt-in PERMISSIVE_* constants for legacy images that need them. 9 new tests + 243 service regression suite green.

title: Three runtime AttributeErrors in Deployment model usage
description: 1) ecs_deployment_service.py:525 uses Deployment.Status.IN_PROGRESS which doesn't exist (should be RUNNING). 2) ecs_deployment_service.py:571 assigns to deployment.duration which is a read-only @property (should set completed_at or use _duration). 3) management/commands/ecs_service.py:237 uses log.level but model field is log_level. All three will crash at runtime.
close_reason: Three AttributeErrors fixed: IN_PROGRESS → RUNNING, deployment.duration assignment removed (relies on @property reading completed_at), log.level → log.log_level. 7 regression tests including grep-based guards against accidental revert.

title: Encryption key silently auto-generated every CLI session
description: cli.py:120-123 generates a new Fernet key in-memory if REMOTE_COMPOSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Credentials encrypted in previous sessions are permanently unrecoverable. No warning shown. Fix: persist the key to disk like secret_key, or refuse to start without explicit key. File: cli.py:120-123
close_reason: Auto-generated encryption key now persists to <db_dir>/encryption_key (mode 0600). Env var REMOTE_COMPOSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY still wins. First-time generation prints stderr warning pointing at the file. 2 unit tests verify env-precedence + cross-session persistence.

title: Credential create serializer accepts garbage credential_value
description: SecureCredentialCreateSerializer.create() uses .get() on credential_value dict without validating required keys. access_key_id/secret_access_key can be None for AWS creds, private_key can be None for SSH. Fix: add validate() method checking credential_type-specific required keys. File: api/serializers.py:129-150
close_reason: SecureCredentialCreateSerializer.validate() rejects missing/empty access_key_id, secret_access_key (AWS) and private_key (SSH) at API boundary. create() now uses subscript access for required keys (post-validate guarantee). 3 source-shape regression tests guard against revert. Behavioral tests skipped because DRF isn't a hard test dep.

title: API has no authentication or authorization on any endpoint
description: No viewset defines permission_classes or authentication_classes. SecureCredentialViewSet allows full CRUD on encrypted credentials with zero auth. ECSServiceViewSet.scale allows unauthenticated scaling. Fix: set REST_FRAMEWORK defaults or add IsAuthenticated to every viewset. Files: api/viewsets.py

title: S1: Add default IsAuthenticated permission and SessionAuthentication to all viewsets
description:
api/viewsets.py — Add to every viewset (or a base mixin class):
  permission_classes = [permissions.IsAuthenticated]
  authentication_classes = [SessionAuthentication, BasicAuthentication]
Import from rest_framework. This is a sensible default that consuming projects can override via DRF settings.

title: S1: Add pagination to all list viewsets
description: api/viewsets.py — Add a default pagination class. Either set DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS in DRF config or add pagination_class to each viewset. PageNumberPagination with page_size=50 is a reasonable default. Especially critical for AuditLogViewSet and DeploymentEventViewSet which can have thousands of rows.

title: S1: Fix API error status codes — distinguish client vs server errors
description: api/viewsets.py — Multiple viewsets catch 'except Exception as e' and return 400 for everything. ECSServiceViewSet.scale (lines 302-305), ECSClusterViewSet.sync_from_aws (lines 224-227). Catch botocore ClientError separately: map 403→403, 404→404, 5xx→502. Return 500 for unexpected errors, not 400.

title: S1: Remove eager log nesting from DeploymentDetailSerializer
description: api/serializers.py:580 — DeploymentDetailSerializer has 'logs = DeploymentLogSerializer(many=True)' which eagerly serializes ALL log entries inline. Deployment logs are already available via /deployments/{id}/logs/ action endpoint. Remove the nested serializer or limit to last 50 entries with source='logs.all[:50]'.

title: S1: Fix ecs_teardown.py: consolidate duplicate imports, add exception logging
description: ecs_teardown.py imports get_aws_client_factory 4 times inside method bodies (lines 125, 153, 213, 256). Move to module level. Replace all 'except Exception: pass' blocks with logged warnings matching the cli.py fixes.

If AWS call fails, log warning and skip local deletion. Apply same pattern in ecs_teardown.py management command (lines 93-95, 165-166, 178-179, 203-204, 247-248).

title: [epic] rc: remote/parallel image builds — build in AWS (or remote), not on the CLI/CI host
description:
`rc` deploy runs `docker buildx build` WHEREVER the CLI runs — on the ECS deploy path that's the ephemeral GitHub Actions runner. That runner has a COLD `rc-cache` docker-container builder, so each of N images (built SERIALLY) pays a full ECR registry-cache round-trip — import cached layers + RE-EXPORT the mode=max cache (~45s each EVEN on a 100% cache hit) + push — over the runner's uplink. Measured: build+push ~12 min for 5 all-CACHED images; buildcache blobs 0.9–1.5 GB; `exporting cache to registry` ~45s/image. Locally the same build is seconds because the builder is WARM (layers on disk, no import/export round-trip).

GOAL: make WHERE the build happens configurable. A `build.backend` seam so a configured deploy DISPATCHES the image build to a warm/remote builder in AWS (or another remote provider) near ECR — the GitHub runner just orchestrates (auth, migrate, roll), it does NOT build images. Local/on-host build stays the default and the fallback.

DIRECTION (weigh in .5 design): AWS-native options — (a) AWS CodeBuild project that runs the buildx build via a buildspec (managed, no persistent infra, same-region ECR push + CodeBuild local cache), or (b) a persistent remote BuildKit (`buildx create --driver remote` → buildkitd on EC2/Fargate) for a truly WARM cross-deploy cache. Pluggable third option: Depot.dev (managed remote builder). Recommend CodeBuild as the first AWS backend (managed, fits "in AWS if configured"); keep the seam open for remote-BuildKit/Depot.

Current build path: `provider/ecs/provider.py::_build_and_push_images` (serial loop, image grouping/owner-sibling dedup already handled) → `image/builder.py::ImageBuilder._run_build` (buildx cmd: `--load`, `--cache-from/--cache-to type=registry,...,mode=max`, watchdog for the mode=max hang) → `ImagePusher` (separate `docker push`). Good existing tests: tests/unit/test_image/{test_builder,test_buildkit_cache,test_builder_watchdog,test_pusher}.py.

Children .1–.6 (TDD). Do NOT regress the local path or the existing cache/watchdog behavior. Prefix rc-.
notes: ALL CHILDREN IMPLEMENTED + validated (2014 rc unit tests green). Local path: seam + parallel + cache-config + instrumentation. Remote: AwsCodeBuildBackend (build off-runner in AWS CodeBuild). Uncommitted feat/rc-remote-build-backend. REMAINING: (1) commit + PR; (2) provision IAM role + S3 bucket; (3) reviewed live e2e cutover (flip build.backend=aws-codebuild, watch one deploy, compare vs ~12min baseline). Follow-ups: S3 lifecycle expiry, CodeBuild LOCAL_DOCKER_LAYER_CACHE, in-buildspec parallelism.

title: [epic] rc.yml bootstrap: — committed GitHub-OIDC CI deploy-role stack (separate state)
description:
PROBLEM (from start-simpli, filed startsim-1zmk)
rc generates the workload stack from rc.yml into deploy/<project>/terraform/, which the
consuming repo gitignores + regenerates every run. The CI/bootstrap IAM — specifically the
GitHub OIDC role that CI assumes to trigger deploys — is NOT a per-service runtime resource.
It must be tracked, it has no rc representation today, so it lives out-of-band via the AWS CLI
and drifts. Concrete drift artifact: the 2026-06-16 hand-edit that added the "roll
foundry-tenant-* services" grant directly on the live deploy role.

REQUEST
A new top-level `bootstrap:` section in rc.yml so rc generates the deploy role into a
COMMITTED, non-gitignored stack with its OWN terraform state, idempotently, deriving its
permissions from the project/cluster config already present:

    bootstrap:
      github_oidc_deploy_role:
        github_repo: qosha1/start-simpli-api
        github_branch: main
        permissions:
          codebuild_project: ${project}-build
          ecr_namespace:     ${project}/*
          ecs_clusters:      [${cluster}, 'foundry-tenant-*']   # 2nd = StringLike (wildcard)
          pass_roles:        [${project}-task, ${project}-task-exec]

WHY THIS SHAPE
- codebuild_project -> codebuild:StartBuild/BatchGetBuilds on the build project ARN
- ecr_namespace     -> ecr:GetAuthorizationToken (Resource *) + push/pull on repos under namespace
- ecs_clusters      -> ecs service-deploy actions; exact cluster = exact service-ARN, wildcard
                       entry (foundry-tenant-*) = wildcard service-ARN (StringLike-by-ARN). The
                       wildcard entry IS the 2026-06-16 hand-edited "roll foundry tenants" grant.
- pass_roles        -> iam:PassRole on the task + task-exec roles, conditioned to ecs-tasks

ACCEPTANCE (epic-level)
1. rc emits a committed, self-contained bootstrap stack (own dir, own state key, own README).
2. Idempotent / no-clobber: re-emit is byte-identical; `rc bootstrap` never destroys; apply is
   gated behind an explicit flag.
3. Generated role matches the live one closely enough that `terraform import` of the live deploy
   role yields a no-op (or a reviewable, minimal) plan.
4. Documented in README + rc.yml schema docs + `rc bootstrap --help`.
5. Default path byte-identical: with NO `bootstrap:` key the existing golden fixture stays green.

CONTEXT
- Interim: start-simpli PR #28 ships a hand-written bootstrap/ stack. Once this lands, that stack
  migrates into the rc-generated one (import -> no-op is the migration gate).
- Verification of import->no-op against the LIVE start-simpli deploy role happens downstream in
  start-simpli-api during migration; rc's job here is faithful, deterministic, documented
  generation + configurability (role_name, create-vs-adopt OIDC provider) so the live role can be
  matched.

GOVERNING LAWS
- rc-general-cli-no-special-casing: generic capability, opt-in, additive, default path
  byte-identical. NO sentinal/start-simpli special-casing in code.
- rc-cli-change-process: PLAN -> TEST-FIRST -> BEADS -> ARCHITECT -> DOCS -> BUILD -> VALIDATE.
design:
ARCHITECTURE (grounded in the codebase)

Config (config/_schema_types.py + _schema_parser.py + v2_schema.py)
- New dataclasses: BootstrapConfig{ github_oidc_deploy_role, output_dir="bootstrap/terraform" }
  and GithubOidcDeployRole{ github_repo, github_branch="main", role_name=None,
  create_oidc_provider=False, permissions: dict }.
- New optional top-level RcConfigV2.bootstrap field; parsed only when raw.get("bootstrap").
- Follow existing convention: ${project}/${cluster} placeholders are stored LITERALLY at parse
  time (the schema layer does no interpolation today; output_dir already holds ${provider}).

Interpolation + policy derivation (new pkg remote_compose/bootstrap/, pure + unit-testable)
- build.interpolate(value, project, cluster): recursively replaces ${project}/${cluster} in
  str/list/dict. Validates no other ${...} rc-placeholder survives (terraform ${data...} refs are
  added AFTER interpolation, so the input must be clean).
- build.derive_statements(permissions): permission keys -> IAM statement dicts with stable SIDs:
    CodeBuildDeploy, EcrAuth (Resource "*"), EcrPushPull, EcsDeployServices (service+cluster ARNs,
    wildcards carried through from entries), EcsTaskDefinitions (Resource "*"), PassTaskRoles
    (iam:PassRole + Condition iam:PassedToService=ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com).
  Region/account are emitted as terraform refs ${data.aws_region.current.name} /
  ${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id} so EMIT NEEDS NO AWS CALLS (deterministic).

Emission (remote_compose/bootstrap/emit.py + templates/*.tf.j2, reuse terraform.emitter +
terraform.backend.render_backend_block)
- Templates: versions.tf.j2, backend.tf.j2, oidc.tf.j2 (data-source by default; resource when
  create_oidc_provider), deploy_role.tf.j2 (role + GitHub trust policy + inline permission policy),
  outputs.tf.j2. Plus a README.md + a .gitignore that ignores ONLY volatile artifacts (state is
  NEVER committed; the .tf files ARE — committed-ness comes from LOCATION outside the gitignored
  deploy/ tree, not from committing tfstate).
- Trust policy: Principal.Federated = OIDC provider ARN; Action sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity;
  Condition aud StringEquals sts.amazonaws.com; sub match repo:OWNER/REPO:ref:refs/heads/BRANCH
  (StringEquals exact branch; StringLike repo:OWNER/REPO:* when branch == "*").
- Separate state: build.derive_bootstrap_backend(workload_backend, project): reuse s3
  bucket/region/dynamodb_table/profile with key "<project>/bootstrap.tfstate"; local otherwise.
- role_name default "${project}-github-deploy"; overridable so it can match a live role name.
- create_oidc_provider False -> data "aws_iam_openid_connect_provider" by url; True -> resource.

CLI (remote_compose/cli_commands/bootstrap.py, registered in cli.py; click, like adopt.py)
- `rc bootstrap`: load v2 config, require bootstrap section (else clear error), resolve project +
  cluster (ecs_cfg.cluster or f"{project}-cluster"), emit to rc_yml.parent / output_dir, run
  TerraformRunner.init() + plan(); print plan. `--apply` (+ `--yes`) gates apply. NEVER destroy.
- Idempotent: re-running with no config change -> byte-identical emit -> no-op plan.

TESTING (tiers per CLAUDE.md)
- Unit: config parse/validate, interpolation, policy derivation, rendered HCL assertions, a golden
  fixture for a canonical bootstrap stack (tests/fixtures/golden/bootstrap_oidc/), idempotent
  re-emit byte-identical, default-path golden (ecs_minimal) UNCHANGED.
- Contract/CLI: CliRunner drives `rc bootstrap` with a fake/recording runner; assert emit dir +
  refusal without bootstrap section + no destroy.

RISKS / DECISIONS
- OIDC provider is account-global (one per account). CI already assumes it, so DEFAULT to a data
  source (adopt), opt-in to create — mirrors rc's adopt-or-create pattern (network.tf.j2).
- Literal import->no-op against the live role depends on the live role's exact SIDs/shape, which
  rc can't see from here; rc emits canonical SIDs + makes role_name configurable. Final no-op is
  the downstream start-simpli migration gate (records under the acceptance child).
acceptance_criteria: rc emits a committed self-contained bootstrap stack (own dir/state/README); re-emit byte-identical; rc bootstrap never destroys, apply gated; generated deploy role import->no-op against live (downstream gate); documented; default-path golden (ecs_minimal) stays byte-identical.

title: rc deploy (terraform path) force-rolls only image-group OWNERS, not siblings — workers run stale code after deploy
description:
The terraform-apply deploy path force-rolls only the build OWNER of each image
group, not the image-group SIBLINGS.

provider/ecs/provider.py deploy() (~line 1325):
    pushed = self._build_and_push_images(...)    # returns ONE owner per image group
    if pushed and not skip_force_roll:
        self._force_new_deployments(ctx, pushed)  # <-- owners only, no siblings

The Django pattern: django owns the shared image; celery-worker / celery-beat /
flower are SIBLINGS (same build identity, different command). _build_and_push_images
returns only owners, so the siblings are never force-rolled and keep running the
previous :latest after a deploy -> stale code in prod.

The --no-state path already fixed this (#8 / commit a4ea03c): it expands pushed
owners to ALL image-group members before rolling (provider.py ~1480-1486). That
expansion was never ported to the terraform-apply deploy(), so the two deploy
paths have drifted.

Impact: browser-mgr (pinned to current HEAD, deploys with plain `rc deploy` =
terraform path) — django's celery-* workers ran stale code after deploy. Sentinal
(debuggai-api) is UNAFFECTED because it deploys with `rc deploy --no-state`.

Related: browser-mgr-2u96 (deploy-complete-without-rolling pattern).
design:
Extract the owners->siblings expansion (currently inline in _deploy_no_state)
into ONE shared function so the two deploy paths can't drift again. A module-level
helper beside image_group_owners / _services_to_build:

    def roll_targets_for_pushed(services, pushed):
        owners = image_group_owners(services)
        pushed_owners = set(pushed)
        return sorted(n for n in services if owners.get(n, n) in pushed_owners)

Call it from BOTH:
  - deploy() : replace `self._force_new_deployments(ctx, pushed)` (~1325) with
    a roll over roll_targets_for_pushed(ctx.services, pushed).
  - _deploy_no_state() : replace the inline expansion (~1480-1486) with the helper.

Preserve existing behaviors (all covered by regression tests in GREEN):
  - --no-build branch (deploy, ~1299-1303) already rolls all services -> leave as is.
  - explicit --services filter: _build_and_push_images already maps a sibling filter
    to its owner, so pushed contains the owner and the helper rolls the whole group
    (matches --no-state semantics).
  - auto_roll=false owners are excluded from pushed (singletons owning their own
    group) so they stay un-rolled.
  - DeployResult.services should reflect the expanded roll_targets.
acceptance_criteria: Given a compose where several services share one build (django + celery-*), rc deploy (terraform path, no --services) force-rolls ALL of them, not just the owner. New unit test fails on current HEAD and passes after the fix. Regressions hold: --no-build rolls all; --services on a sibling rolls the whole group; auto_roll=false singleton stays un-rolled; _deploy_no_state unchanged (shares the helper); generated task defs byte-identical.
notes:
Fix implemented + PR #15 (branch fix/rc-wji.1-deploy-sibling-roll). Awaiting CI/merge; then rc-wji.1.4 (RC_REF bump).
MERGED to remote-compose main (PR #15) -> SHA e19e2e6.

title: rc deploy: don't force-roll unchanged/infrastructure services (Cloud Map DNS gap on stateful rolls)
description:
rc v2 'rc deploy' force-rolls EVERY service with a build context (provider.deploy -> _build_and_push_images returns all built services -> _force_new_deployments rolls them). For a single-task EFS service (e.g. postgres) rc rolls with min_healthy=0 (two tasks can't mount the same EFS dir), so EVERY deploy briefly deregisters it from Cloud Map -> dependents get OperationalError [Errno -2] 'Name or service not known' during the window.

LIVE INCIDENT (browser-mgr prod, 2026-06-11): celerybeat sync + django hit [Errno -2] resolving postgres.production.browser-mgr.local on every rc deploy. Worked around in browser-mgr CI by scoping the roll: 'rc deploy --services django,celeryworker,celerybeat,browserworker' (exclude postgres). That hand-maintained list is exactly the special-casing rc-general-cli-no-special-casing warns against — rc should handle this generally.

Options (decide in architect):
  (a) v2 'rc deploy' does NOT force-roll type=infrastructure services by default (postgres/redis); they roll only when explicitly named in --services. Most direct.
  (b) Honor --code-only in the v2 dispatcher (today it's v1-only; v2 silently ignores it) -> skip infrastructure.
  (c) Skip force-roll when the just-pushed image DIGEST == the running task's image digest (no-op roll skip) — generally avoids churn for any unchanged service, not just infra. Strongest but needs ECR/ECS digest compare in the deploy path.
Likely (a)+(c): infra never auto-rolls; everything else rolls only on real image change.
design: TDD per rc-cli-change-process. RED: provider-level test asserting _force_new_deployments / pushed set EXCLUDES a type=infrastructure service on a full deploy (and/or excludes a service whose pushed digest matches running). Mock the ECR/ECS calls via the existing deploy-path test seams (see test_skip_build.py / test_silent_build_skip.py). Then architect (a) vs (c), build, prove red->green + golden byte-identical. Relates to [[rc-kr7]] stateful guardrails (downtime-on-roll).
acceptance_criteria: A v2 rc deploy of an app change does NOT roll type=infrastructure single-task services; dependents see no Cloud Map DNS gap; explicit --services postgres still rolls it; default path unchanged for stacks without infra services. browser-mgr CI can drop the hand-maintained --services list.

title: Brownfield adoption: bind to existing IAM roles, SGs/rules, target groups, and arbitrary service names by ARN/name
description: rc was greenfield-first; adoption was grafted on mid-migration (existing ALB/CloudMap/EFS built as features during browser-mgr). Still NOT first-class: existing IAM roles, existing security-group rules, existing target groups, and arbitrary existing SERVICE NAMES. The entire D3 agony (adopt copilot cluster vs fresh cluster) existed only because rc assumes it owns naming and can't bind a resource by ARN/name. A tool whose headline use case is migrating live stacks must be adopt-first.
design: Extend the existing-ALB/EFS/CloudMap reference pattern uniformly to all resource kinds. rc adopt should introspect a live stack and emit refs + terraform imports (it only imported 4/6 ECR repos this time; SD services were hand-imported).
acceptance_criteria: rc.yml can reference existing IAM roles (task/exec), existing SGs + add rules, existing target groups, and existing/custom service names; rc adopt imports them; default create-new path byte-identical.

title: Field-level task-def ownership (replace all-or-nothing ignore_task_definition_changes)
description: To stop terraform stomping out-of-band edits we set ignore_changes=[container_definitions], which then SILENTLY swallows legit rc.yml changes (command/cpu/mem/env). That's why reconcile has to force command=/start-browserworker. rc either owns the whole container def or none of it. Add field-level ownership so rc can own command/cpu/mem while ignoring externally-managed fields (e.g. secrets/image tag), instead of the coarse global ignore.
design: Investigate terraform ignore_changes granularity for container_definitions (it's a single JSON blob — may need rc to manage discrete attrs or a merge strategy). Document the tension explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: rc.yml can declare which task-def fields rc owns vs ignores; a command change in rc.yml reaches the live task def without reconcile forcing it; default behavior documented + non-surprising.

title: SM-native per-service env (wire all keys from a Secrets Manager secret as valueFrom)
description: rc's env_file promotion only read the ~11-key LOCAL compose subset; browser-mgr prod needed ~61 keys living in SM (browser-mgr/prod-env-<svc>). reconcile_task_env.py re-wires every key as a valueFrom by hand. rc assumes compose env_file is the source of truth — for real apps it isn't. Add a way to point a service's env at an existing SM secret and have rc wire EVERY key (or a declared subset) as secrets[].valueFrom, per-service scoped.
design: Relates to mini-v2 note 'every task def gets ALL secrets across ALL services' — fix per-service scoping here. Support both 'wire all keys in secret' and explicit key list.
acceptance_criteria: rc.yml can reference an existing SM secret per service; provider wires each key as valueFrom on that service's task def only (per-service scoping); browser-mgr env reconcile step removed; default path byte-identical.

title: rc.yml app-IAM abstraction (per-service task-role policies/grants)

Add first-class per-service iam: in rc.yml: attach managed policy ARNs and/or declare inline statements (actions/resources/conditions). Provider renders aws_iam_role_policy / attachments onto the service task role.

title: rc CLI hardening: brownfield-migration weaknesses surfaced by browser-mgr cutover
description:
The Copilot->rc migration of browser-mgr (6-service ECS stack, adopt-in-place: existing cluster/EFS/ALB/CloudMap) exposed systemic gaps in rc. The most damning artifact is deploy/prod/reconcile_task_env.py — a ~200-line side-channel script that runs AFTER 'rc deploy' to do everything rc can't express (full env from SM, per-service command override, task-role IAM for EFS/RunTask/S3). Per the rc-general-cli-no-special-casing law, a per-stack reconcile script is precisely the special-casing rc must eliminate. THROUGHLINE: rc deploys infrastructure well but models the running APPLICATION thinly, and was built greenfield-first when the real job is brownfield consolidation.

The items in reconcile_task_env.py ARE this backlog. Each weakness below should become a general rc.yml capability so the next migration needs ZERO side-channel scripts.

Concrete trigger this session: SessionRecording uploads 403'd because rc created one shared task role with EFS+RunTask but NO S3 grant to the media bucket (Copilot supplied it via an AddonsStack S3AccessPolicy). rc has no app-IAM abstraction at all. Fixed live + codified in reconcile (browser-mgr commit 78ffe07) — but that fix living in reconcile instead of rc.yml is itself the bug.

What held up well (keep/extend): golden-fixture template architecture (provider templates + byte-identical default-path tests) made existing-ALB/CloudMap/EFS additive without regressing other stacks; terraform-state backend is the right default.
design: Follow rc-cli-change-process for every child: plan -> test-first (golden fixtures in tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/ + contract tests) -> beads -> architect (create-vs-adopt, schema) -> docs -> build -> validate. All new behavior ADDITIVE + opt-in; default path byte-identical (rc-general-cli-no-special-casing).
acceptance_criteria: All child issues resolved; a brownfield ECS stack (existing cluster/ALB/EFS/CloudMap/IAM) can be adopted and run correctly via rc.yml + general CLI alone, with no post-deploy reconcile script; default-path golden tests stay green.
notes:
TDD PROTOCOL (mandatory for every child, per rc-cli-change-process):
1. PROVE RED: write the failing test(s) FIRST under tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/ (or tests/contract/) that assert the new opt-in behavior. Run them; capture that they FAIL for the right reason (feature absent: missing resource/attr, StrictUndefined, or wrong output) — not an import/typo error. A red that fails for the wrong reason does not count.
2. ARCHITECT: design the rc.yml schema (opt-in key), the provider render, validation, and the create-vs-adopt decision — BEFORE touching implementation.
3. BUILD to GREEN: implement until the red tests pass.
4. PROVE RED->GREEN: re-run the exact tests from step 1 and show them flip red->green; AND run the full golden-fixture suite to prove the default path (no new config) stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL (no other fixture moved). Both halves required: new tests green + zero golden drift.
5. DOCS + VALIDATE: update rc.yml schema docs/README/help; run fast tier + relevant integration.
Do NOT regenerate golden fixtures to make tests pass without reviewing the diff (rc-cli-change-process).

title: rc adopt is broken: state_backend/adopt.py out of sync with v1_migrate API
description:
rc adopt fails immediately on any real stack. Found while adopting a live prod ECS stack (debuggai-api-prod) into terraform.

REPRO: rc -c rc.yml adopt against a v2 rc.yml -> TypeError.

ROOT CAUSE (remote_compose/state_backend/adopt.py::_discover_imports):
1. Calls discover.discover(stack, session=session) but the real signature is discover(rc_v1_yml_path: Path, aws_session=None, inventory_snapshot=None). Wrong: passes a V1Stack as the path arg, and 'session=' instead of 'aws_session='. -> 'TypeError: discover() got an unexpected keyword argument session'.
2. discover() RETURNS a tuple (V1Stack, ResourceInventory), not just an inventory. Code treats the return as inv.
3. Calls translate.imports_for(inv) — translate.py has NO imports_for function. The real API is per-resource translators translate_*_in_place(inv) -> (overrides, list[TerraformImportBlock], list[warnings]) (EFS/ALB/ACM/secrets/VPC/IAM/ECR/ECS cluster). TerraformImportBlock has .id (aws id) and .to (tf address).
4. discover() needs a v1-shaped rc.yml (raises on version: 2). adopt is fed a v2 rc.yml. _discover_imports builds a V1Stack by hand to dodge from_yaml, but then the discover() call is wrong anyway.

DEEPER ISSUE (scope, not just call-site): even after fixing the call site, the v1_migrate translators only import the SUBSET of stateful shared resources (EFS, ALB+listeners, ACM, SM secrets, VPC, IAM, ECR, ECS cluster). They do NOT cover per-service ECS services, task defs, target groups, listener RULES, Cloud Map services, or per-service ECR repos. The generated v2 module (rc plan emits 47 resources for debuggai-api-prod) has module addresses that must MATCH each TerraformImportBlock.to or terraform import fails / leaves drift. MIGRATION_RUNBOOK.md even documents 'Why we are NOT running terraform import today'. So adopt needs: (a) call-site fix, (b) a real import-set generator that walks the FULL generated module and maps every address to a live id, (c) a post-adopt 'rc plan must be ~0 drift' assertion, (d) tests with a recorded inventory.

IMPACT: rc adopt cannot bring any live stack under terraform mgmt. Blocks durable management of adopted/--no-state prod stacks (the whole point of the command). Live prod desiredCount/replicas stay API-only and resettable.

NON-DESTRUCTIVE NOTE: terraform import only writes state, so a fixed adopt is safe to iterate; the danger is applying with INCOMPLETE state (recreates live infra). Gate adopt on a clean plan before any apply.
close_reason: FIXED end-to-end. rc adopt now works: ran it against live debuggai-api-prod, imported 47/47 resources into s3 state. Two follow-up bugs the live run surfaced were fixed (PR #7, merged): (1) import-id formats — sd namespace NS_ID:VPC_ID, task def by ARN; (2) new opt-in provider_config.ecs.ignore_task_definition_changes for stacks whose container defs are owned out-of-band. Post-adopt rc plan: 0 add / 21 change (benign tf-only) / 0 destroy. PRs #6 + #7 merged.

title: rc: deploy into an EXISTING VPC (vpc_id + subnet_ids + security_group_ids)
description: Let provider_config.ecs declare an existing VPC instead of always creating one. Needed for tightly-meshed stacks (debugg-ai/sentinal: API + dynamic user-apps + browser-mgr share one VPC + SG and must talk freely). rc's own-VPC + peering breaks same-VPC SG-referencing + Cloud Map DNS. New keys: provider_config.ecs.vpc_id, public_subnet_ids[], private_subnet_ids[], security_group_ids[] (existing SGs ALSO attached to tasks so they join an existing mesh). When vpc_id is set: data-source the VPC/subnets, skip aws_vpc/igw/subnet/route_table creation; tasks get rc's tasks SG + the declared existing SGs. Default (no vpc_id) path stays byte-identical.
design:
ARCHITECTURE (general, additive, non-breaking — see [[rc-general-cli-no-special-casing]]).

CLI/config (all optional; absent => create VPC as today):
  provider_config.ecs:
    vpc_id: vpc-xxxx                  # adopt existing VPC
    public_subnet_ids: [s-a, s-b]     # >=2 AZs, PUBLIC (IGW route) — ALB + Fargate(assign_public_ip)
    private_subnet_ids: [s-c, s-d]    # optional; defaults to public_subnet_ids
    security_group_ids: [sg-x]        # optional; EXTRA SGs attached to every task (join existing mesh)

KEY DECISION — rendering aliases keep the DEFAULT path byte-identical (golden tests stay green; no breaking change). Emitter computes reference strings into context:
  vpc_id_ref           = create:'aws_vpc.main.id'              adopt:'data.aws_vpc.main.id'
  public_subnet_ids_ref= create:'aws_subnet.public[*].id'      adopt:'local.rc_public_subnet_ids'
  public_subnet_idx_ref= create:'aws_subnet.public[count.index].id' adopt:'local.rc_public_subnet_ids[count.index]'
  private_subnet_ids_ref=create:'aws_subnet.private[*].id'     adopt:'local.rc_private_subnet_ids'
Templates render {{ vpc_id_ref }} etc -> in create mode this is the ORIGINAL string => byte-identical output. network.tf.j2 wraps create resources in {% if existing_vpc %}data+locals{% else %}<verbatim original>{% endif %}. services.tf.j2 task security_groups = [tasks.id] + extra_security_group_ids.

EDGE CASES (document, do not over-enforce): existing public subnets need IGW route + map_public_ip (Fargate egress); rc creates its OWN task/ALB SGs in the existing VPC + the declared SGs are additive; NO igw/route-table created in adopt mode; Cloud Map namespace created in existing VPC (user avoids name collision); EFS mount targets in provided public subnets.
acceptance_criteria: (1) DEFAULT path: all existing golden fixtures BYTE-IDENTICAL (no regen). (2) ADOPT path: emitted tf has NO aws_vpc/aws_subnet/aws_internet_gateway/aws_route_table resources; has data.aws_vpc.main; ALB+tasks+EFS+cloudmap reference existing VPC/subnets; tasks carry extra SGs. (3) config validation: vpc_id without public_subnet_ids -> error; public_subnet_ids without vpc_id -> error. (4) fast tier (unit+contract) green.
notes: IMPLEMENTED + unit-validated 2026-05-31 on branch feat/existing-vpc-support. Emission (network adopt-or-create + rendering aliases), config-shape validation, AWS pre-flight, docs all done test-first. Default path byte-identical (golden green). title: rc: build shared image ONCE for multi-service apps (Django+celery), not per-ECR-repo
description: When N services share one build context+dockerfile (the standard Django pattern: django + celery-worker/beat/flower/browser all run the same image, differing only by command), rc currently builds+pushes that image to N SEPARATE ECR repos (debuggai-api/{django,celery-worker,celery-beat,...}). For a ~1.5-2GB image with no buildcache, that's N× the push time — observed ~50-75min for sentinal staging's first deploy, dominated by re-pushing the same Django image 4×. FIX: detect services sharing (build_context, dockerfile, build_args) → build+push ONCE to a single ECR repo → have the other services' task defs reference that same image URI with their own command override. Should cut multi-service deploy time ~N×. Found during sentinal staging deploy (sentinal-vmj6).
design:
ARCHITECTURE (general, additive). ROOT CAUSE: _build_and_push_images loops per-service; ECR stores layer blobs PER-REPO (no cross-repo dedup), so N services sharing one build => N full pushes of the same image (4x 4GB on Starlink = hours). The ONLY true fix is ONE repo per build.

IMAGE GROUP = (resolved build context, dockerfile, target, frozenset(build_args)). Services with the same identity share an image. Deterministic OWNER = min(service name) in the group.

EMISSION (provider.py services_view + services.tf.j2): each svc gains owns_image_repo (bool) + image_repo_tf_name (owner's tf_name). services.tf.j2: {% if svc.owns_image_repo %}aws_ecr_repository ...{% endif %}; task-def image = aws_ecr_repository.{{ svc.image_repo_tf_name }}.repository_url:latest. ecr_repositories output lists OWNERS only.

BUILD LOOP (_build_and_push_images): build+push ONCE per group (iterate owners); siblings skip (their task def already points at the owner image). buildcache ref keyed by the build identity/owner, not per-service.

ADDITIVE: a single-service-per-build app => each svc is its own owner => emission identical to today (golden stays byte-identical IF its services don't share a build — verify). Only multi-service shared-build stacks change (siblings stop getting their own repo). For an already-deployed shared-build stack, the sibling ECR repos become unreferenced (terraform destroys them) + sibling task-def image URIs change -> one-time roll; images now live in the owner repo.
acceptance_criteria: (1) services with identical build emit ONE aws_ecr_repository (owner); siblings' task-def image references the owner repo. (2) build loop builds+pushes once per group (N-service Django app = 1 django push, not N). (3) distinct-build / single-service apps: emission byte-identical (golden green). (4) unit tests: grouping, owner selection, emission (one repo + sibling ref), build-loop dedup. (5) fast tier green.
close_reason: Shared-image dedup complete + validated (unit + terraform-validate). One repo + one push per build group.

title: rc should set ECS healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds for services with health_check_path
description:
OBSERVED: deploying sentinal-test 2026-04-30, django service flapped repeatedly (3 deploy cycles, each task killed at ~90s) until I manually ran 'aws ecs update-service --health-check-grace-period-seconds 180'. Then it stabilized.

ROOT CAUSE: rc emits ECS service terraform with no health_check_grace_period_seconds, so AWS defaults it to 0. ALB target group starts health-checking immediately after task registration. Django services that run migrate + collectstatic + uvicorn boot take 30-60s to be ready. With 30s health interval × 3 unhealthy threshold = task gets killed at 90s — but only if first 3 checks all fail. With grace=0 and slow boot, EVERY task fails enough checks to be killed before uvicorn binds.

WHY THIS MATTERS: this turns 'first deploy works' into 'first deploy never converges' for any service whose start script does non-trivial work (migrate, collectstatic, npm build, etc.). The flap is silent — events show 'Health checks failed' but ECS doesn't say 'maybe your grace period is too short'.

FIX: provider/ecs/templates/services.tf.j2 should set health_check_grace_period_seconds when the service has a health_check_path. Default 60s (covers most fast-boot services); 120-180s for services with lifecycle.auto_on_deploy hooks (migrate). Make it configurable via services.<name>.health_check_grace_period.

VERIFY: after fix, deploy a stack with django + slow start script, watch ALB health — task should not be killed during first 3 health-check rounds.
notes: Implementation: provider/ecs/provider.py computes effective_grace (60s default, 180s when any auto_on_deploy lifecycle hook present, explicit value via services.<n>.health_check_grace_period wins). Template emits health_check_grace_period_seconds for public services only (AWS rejects the field without load_balancer block). 8 new tests in test_health_check_grace_period.py. Golden fixture regenerated. 1622 unit+contract tests pass.
close_reason: Shipped: rc emits health_check_grace_period_seconds=60 (180 with auto_on_deploy) on public services. Real-world repro from sentinal verification motivated this.

title: [BUG] rc exec / aws ecs execute-command silent hangs need heartbeat + better diagnostic
description:
User reported (start-simpli session 2026-04-30): 'rc exec hangs (matches the silent-hang bug fixed). Let me kill stale ones and call aws ecs execute-command directly.'

Multiple silent-wait stages in provider.exec:

1. The wait loop in provider.py:1687 polls list_tasks + describe_tasks for up to RC_EXEC_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S (default 300s) waiting for a RUNNING task with the ExecuteCommandAgent in RUNNING state. If neither happens, the loop is silent for 5 min then errors. The user has no way to know whether (a) ECS is slow, (b) tasks failed to start, or (c) something is broken — they just see hang.

2. _exec_capture spawns subprocess.run with timeout=600s. If the SSM session manager plugin hangs OR aws ecs execute-command hangs (network blip, broken SSM agent in container, broken SM perms partway through session), the user sees no output until 10-min timeout fires.

3. The session manager plugin process can pile up in zombie state when killed mid-session — the user noted multiple stale zsh wrappers + execute-command processes.

FIXES NEEDED:
  (a) Wrap the wait loop in a heartbeat (rc-60x pattern) so users see '... waiting for service X to be exec-ready (elapsed=Ns)' every 30s.
  (b) Wrap the subprocess.run in a heartbeat for the same reason.
  (c) Surface intermediate state during the wait — emit per-poll diagnostic when list_tasks returns empty vs returns tasks-but-agent-not-ready vs returns blocked-tasks.
  (d) On wait timeout, include the LAST diagnostic state as the error message (already partial via last_diag).

ACCEPTANCE: rc exec on a service whose task is still starting up emits visible progress every 30s; the user can tell if ECS is making progress vs stuck. On a real hang (SSM plugin blocked), the heartbeat shows elapsed time so the user can decide to abort.
close_reason: Shipped: heartbeat wrapping for both phases of provider.exec. (1) The 5-min wait loop that polls list_tasks + describe_tasks for ExecuteCommandAgent readiness now emits 'waiting for service X to be exec-ready (elapsed=Ns)' every 30s. title: [BUG] [P0 PROD] rc deploy --no-state silently no-ops the build phase — only force-rolls
description:
Discovered during start-simpli redeploy session 2026-04-30: 'rc deploy --no-state' completes in 39s with NO docker build/push activity. The user expected new images to be built and pushed but only update_service(forceNewDeployment=True) ran. ECS rolled to whatever images already existed in ECR with the :latest tag → no code changes deployed.

Trace from session log shows the dispatch path went straight to _force_new_deployments without invoking _build_and_push_images, OR _build_and_push_images returned [] from one of its silent-skip branches.

Hypotheses (need investigation):
  (a) skip_terraform=True path in _deploy_no_state has a bug that early-returns before build.
  (b) One of the per-service skip guards (build_context=None, no ECR repo discovery, etc.) hit silently.
  (c) cache_to=registry caused the buildkit hang we filed in rc-mtt — but in --no-state mode, with a session that completed in 39s, the build phase didn't even attempt.

The session also noted: 'both early-return paths emit messages we didn't see' — meaning the rc-8q4 visibility fixes are not catching this scenario.

ACCEPTANCE: rc deploy --no-state on a stack with build_context-having services rebuilds and pushes new images on every run (or emits a clear progress line stating WHY it skipped). Add an integration test against a v2 rc.yml + --no-state where the user can verify image digests change after the deploy.

Reproducer: see start-simpli session log captured 2026-04-30. ss-debuggai-django:110 task-def registered 2026-04-28 — meaning rc deploy --no-state on 2026-04-30 didn't bump the image OR register a new task-def revision.

This is more severe than rc-j04 (--dry-run silent real-deploy) because here the user EXPECTS a deploy and instead gets a no-op. Tasks roll to old code and the user thinks new code is live.
notes:

build_context isn't being populated when rc.yml's services don't

I tested the minimal repro of that exact pattern (rc.yml with services
declared but no build:; compose with build:context+dockerfile). Result:

Improvements shipped (commit pending):

title: [BUG] [P0 PROD] v0.2.0 SM-routing fix doesn't grant ecsTaskExecutionRole secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on new auto-secrets
description:
Discovered during start-simpli-api redeploy on rc v0.2.0 (post env-file-leak fix). New task defs reference compose env_file values via SM valueFrom, but ecsTaskExecutionRole only had GetSecretValue on the OLD rc.yml-declared secrets — not the new auto-named backend-envs-* SM secrets that v0.2.0 auto-promotes. New tasks failed to start with 'unable to retrieve secret from asm'. Old tasks kept serving (no downtime) but the deploy was stuck until manual IAM fix: attach inline policy granting GetSecretValue + DescribeSecret on <project>/* prefix.

FIX: provider/ecs/templates/iam.tf.j2 grants Secrets Manager perms based on the secrets[] in DeployContext. Verify it iterates v2_secrets_expanded (the post-_expand_env_file_auto list including the auto-discovered names) — sentinal-style auto-discovered SM secrets MUST be in the IAM grant. Likely a 1-line fix in the template + golden-fixture update.

ACCEPTANCE: rc up on a brand-new stack with compose env_file produces task defs that successfully pull all auto-promoted SM secrets without any manual IAM intervention. Real-AWS regression test against start-simpli-api or sentinal-core.
notes:
INVESTIGATION NOTES (2026-04-29):

The v0.2.0 IAM template (provider/ecs/templates/iam.tf.j2:51-72) DOES iterate
all_secret_arns which is computed from file_secrets + aws_sm_secrets in
provider.py:494-498. After v0.2.0's auto-discovery, file_secrets includes the
backend-envs-* auto-promoted entries. Full-terraform-path deploys SHOULD grant
GetSecretValue on every auto-discovered ARN.

The reported failure on start-simpli-api was during 'rc deploy --no-state'.
The --no-state code path (provider.py:_deploy_no_state) explicitly does NOT
manage IAM — it just rebuilds + pushes images + force-rolls services. So if
the existing ecsTaskExecutionRole was provisioned for the v1-era narrower
secret set, --no-state can't widen it.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (unverified):
  start-simpli-api was deployed before v0.2.0 with rc.yml-declared SM secrets
  only. When the v0.2.0 fix landed, they ran 'rc deploy --no-state' which
  rebuilt/pushed images but didn't re-emit terraform — so the new auto-
  discovered SM secrets were either pre-existing-from-some-previous-non-
  no-state-run, OR somehow got referenced by task defs in a path I can't
  see from the recap. Either way, --no-state didn't update IAM.

FIX OPTIONS (need user input on which is desired):
  (a) --no-state pre-flight: enumerate secret ARNs the existing latest task
      defs reference; call iam.simulate_principal_policy against the exec
      role; print missing perms + suggested inline policy JSON before
      force-roll.
  (b) post-rollout watcher: poll ECS service events for 60s after force-roll;
      grep for 'ResourceInitializationError' / 'unable to retrieve secret'
      and surface clearly with the offending ARN + role + suggested fix.
  (c) Document that --no-state mode requires the user to manage IAM
      themselves; do nothing in code.

(b) is highest leverage (catches every IAM/perms gap, not just SM). (a) is
more proactive. (c) is least work. Recommend (b) as the long-term fix +
also add a CHANGELOG note that v0.2.0 may require IAM grants on auto-
promoted secret ARNs for hybrid stacks.

Unclaiming for user direction.

Captures pre-roll events as baseline so stale events don't false-trigger. title: [BUG] docker buildx cache-to mode=max can hang indefinitely on slow uplink
description: [Sprint 1] Observed: 'cache-to type=registry,mode=max' uploaded ~2GB of layer cache to ECR for 30+ min then hung entirely with no progress for >2 hours. Killed manually. Fix: 5-min no-progress watchdog → kill + retry without cache-to + emit 'buildcache push hung; falling back to no-cache rebuild' warning. Expose --no-buildcache flag on rc up / rc deploy. Optionally drop default to mode=min. Acceptance: a build hung on cache-to push gets aborted within 5 min and rc emits a clear fallback message.
close_reason: Fixed in image/builder.py: ImageBuilder now uses Popen + line-streaming + no-progress watchdog when cache_to is set. Default RC_BUILD_NO_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S=300s; if buildkit goes silent for that long, kills the build + retries once without --cache-to + emits clear warning. New RC_DISABLE_BUILDCACHE=1 env var drops cache args entirely as escape hatch. Existing tests preserved (subprocess.run path unchanged for non-cache-to builds). New tests in tests/unit/test_image/test_builder_watchdog.py (3 cases). Full suite: 1538 passed.

title: [BUG] rc db push silently skips tables when pg_restore errors mid-restore
description: [Sprint 1] Observed during sentinal-core deploy: rc db push restored 164/165 tables; workflows_pagecapture was silently dropped because pg_restore hit an FK ordering error mid-restore. The 'rc db push: complete' line printed regardless. Different from rc-ln1 which exits non-zero on benign WARNINGS — this issue is real ERRORS being hidden. Fix: capture pg_restore stderr; grep for 'pg_restore: error'; report 'restored X/Y tables, Z errors' line; exit non-zero if any. Bonus: tee full pg_restore log to S3 for post-mortem. Acceptance: simulated FK-order pg_restore failure causes rc db push to report the missing table count and exit 1.

title: (EPIC) rc deploy DX — 8hr → 30min for typical first-deploy
description:
2026-04-29 sentinal-core deploy hit ~12 distinct rc UX/correctness issues that each cost 15-60 min. Most were silent failures or missing pre-flight checks. This epic covers the patterns so a typical first-deploy of a django+postgres+redis stack from a working compose file takes <30 min wall clock, not 8 hours. See child beads for the specific issues. rc-32x is part of this strategy (auto-inject CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS) — already filed, will be linked.

STRATEGY (4 sprints):
  Sprint 1 (Tier A — surface silent failures): 1-2 days
  Sprint 2 (Tier B — new rc fix subcommands): 3-4 days
  Sprint 3 (Tier C — pre-flight + heartbeat): 1 week
  Sprint 4 (Tier D — DX polish): 1-2 days

Cross-cutting principles:
  - Every silent failure becomes a visible warning OR hard error
  - Every long-running step emits progress every 30s
  - Every 'works locally / breaks ECS' pattern gets a plan-time warning + rc fix command suggestion
  - No new abstractions — mirror existing patterns

title: bare/wide except: pass swallows real errors in v2 deploy path
description: provider/ecs/provider.py:709, 795, 819, 844, 865, 1055, 1115 + cli_v2.py:721, 745, 844, 865 — 8+ instances of 'except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001' that don't re-raise or log. Examples: line 709 (buildcache auth failure -> warning + silent continue), line 1115 (terraform output pull -> pass, ingress_url stays None). Users see 'deploy succeeded' when it partially failed. Fix: use specific exception types (botocore.ClientError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired); for genuinely-recoverable cases (e.g. terraform state pull fails -> degrade to local state), log + return a degraded result object so callers know they're operating with reduced data. Source: 2026-04-28 v2 audit.

title: defensive .get() chains + silent None fallbacks in v2 paths
description: provider/ecs/provider.py (~91 uses) + cli_v2.py (~60 uses): patterns like '(ctx.provider_config or {}).get("ecs") or {}' silently mask missing config. When a required key is absent, .get() returns None and a downstream call raises TypeError at an unrelated line, making debugging painful. Examples: provider.py:145-146 assumes region exists before access; line 968 silently uses empty dict if provider_config is None. Fix: lean on existing typed dataclasses (RcConfigV2, DeployContext, ServiceSpec) + validate at parse time; for any remaining dynamic dicts, use explicit assertions at function entry: 'region = ecs_cfg.get("region"); assert region, "provider_config.ecs.region required"'. Source: 2026-04-28 v2 audit.

    ok: bool
    details: str = ""

class Phase(ABC):

class ValidatePhase(Phase):

class EmitV2TerraformPhase(Phase):
    def __init__(self, plan, output_dir: Path): ...

class ImportStatePhase(Phase):
    def __init__(self, plan, output_dir: Path,
                 sandbox_tfstate: Path | None,
                 terraform: TerraformRunner | None = None): ...

    # Runs terraform plan, parses for '- destroy' lines, aborts if found.
    # Then terraform apply against sandbox state only.

class ServicesCutoverPhase(Phase):

class DecommissionV1Phase(Phase):
    def __init__(self, plan, aws_session,
                 v1_rc_yml_path: Path,
                 archive_dir: Path): ...
