title: [startsimpli-prod-migration] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description: HOW we make the failing tests pass — implementation order, risk mitigation, rollback. Decisions to lock in: (1) Build order — discover.py first (read-only against prod, lowest risk), then translate.py (pure functions, easy to test), then plan.py + apply.py last. (2) Reuse vs build — copilot-import (rc-e5u.43) is structural template; copy compose_app pattern, copy ImportResult dataclass shape, copy IMPORT_SUMMARY.md emission. AWS resource discovery uses boto3 directly (no high-level SDK), tag-based filtering matches copilot's discover style. (3) terraform-import-block strategy — modern terraform 1.5+ syntax (mirrors rc-wou bead's recommendation for orphan log-group); apply absorbs imports atomically. (4) Risk: terraform state surgery is unforgiving — once we add an import block + apply, the state is mutated. Mitigation: every apply runs against a copy of the v1 terraform state (cp -r) first; only after the dry-run-against-copy succeeds does the user authorize apply against the real state. (5) Risk: ALB DNS DNS-cutover. Mitigation: import EXISTING ALB into v2 state instead of creating a new one — same DNS, same cert, no DNS change needed. Same for R53 record + ACM cert. (6) Risk: SM secret deletion. Mitigation: rc.yml v2 secrets[*].source=arn references existing SM ARNs by their actual ARN (not name) — terraform never sees the secret as managed, so no DELETE risk. (7) Rollback contract: every phase records a 'undo' shell command into a runbook.json — if a phase fails, the undo command is printed for manual execution + the migration aborts. (8) Pair with rc-e5u.10 (deprecate v1 imperative services) — this migration UNBLOCKS that epic.
design:
TECHNICAL STRATEGY — startsimpli prod v1->v2 migration

GOAL: zero data loss on 133GB postgres EFS volume + DNS unchanged + 1hr maintenance window.

==========================================================================
A. BUILD ORDER (test-green sequence)
==========================================================================
Implement in this order so each step has the previous step's tests green:

1. discover.py (V1Stack.from_yaml + ResourceInventory.from_json + discover composite)
   -> turns 18 failing unit tests green (test_discover.py)
   -> NO AWS mutation — read-only, can run against prod safely
2. translate.py (9 translator functions + TerraformImportBlock.render_hcl)
   -> turns 24 failing unit tests green (test_translate.py)
   -> pure functions, no side effects
3. plan.py (build_plan + safety guards + PlanSafetyError)
   -> turns 12 failing unit tests green (test_plan.py)
4. apply.py (5 phase classes + sandbox guard)
   -> turns 14 failing unit tests green (test_apply.py)
5. integration glue (moto fixtures, boto3 session bridging in discover)
   -> turns 7 failing integration tests green (test_dry_run + test_failure_modes)

Canary tests (3 skipped) stay skipped until Phase 5.2.

==========================================================================
B. RESOURCE DECISION MATRIX
==========================================================================
Per-resource: IMPORT (terraform import block, preserves state) | REFERENCE-BY-ARN (rc.yml carries arn, terraform never sees) | REUSE (rc.yml records uri, no terraform involvement) | RECREATE (forbidden for stateful)

EFS file system fs-0e8a2f9d1e006af95 ......... IMPORT  (133GB postgres data — recreate=data loss)
EFS access points (all 7) .................... IMPORT  (orphaning any breaks task mounts)
ALB ss-debuggai-prod-alb ..................... IMPORT  (DNS at registrar points here; recreate=DNS hole)
ALB listeners (HTTP:80, HTTPS:443) ........... IMPORT  (cert ARN reference; recreate=brief 502s)
ALB target groups (default, nginx) ........... IMPORT  (deregister/reregister preserves grace)
ACM cert bd16f1ce-... ........................ IMPORT  (referenced by HTTPS listener)
Route53 zone Z00022951OO3UQJSGC9FG ........... NO-OP   (only NS+SOA; apex managed at registrar)
SM secrets (32 entries) ...................... REFERENCE-BY-ARN  (delete=30d name-reservation lock)
VPC vpc-053d0dfca255b6219 .................... IMPORT  (already remote-compose:managed=true)
Subnets (2) .................................. IMPORT
Security groups (5) .......................... IMPORT
IAM ecsTaskExecutionRole / ecsTaskRole ....... REFERENCE-BY-ARN  (account-wide, external)
ECR repos (6) ................................ REUSE  (uri carried in rc.yml; same images work v1/v2)
ECS cluster ss-debuggai-prod ................. IMPORT  (preserves Service Connect ns + log groups)
ECS services (7) ............................. RECREATE  (task def is the actual change; service.update rolls)

RECREATE is allowed ONLY for ECS services because that's the cutover surface — task def goes from v1-shaped (debian-postgres-mounted-EFS via fsap-...) to v2-shaped (same EFS+AP, secrets[*]=arn instead of env_file_auto). Postgres data lives on EFS, not in the task — so the task is replaceable.

==========================================================================
C. TERRAFORM STATE-COPY-BEFORE-APPLY PROTOCOL
==========================================================================
Hard rule: NO terraform apply runs against the live tfstate until a sandbox-state-copy run is fully green.

PROCEDURE (enforced by ImportStatePhase code, not just policy):
  1. cp -r terraform/<live>.tfstate /tmp/tfstate.copy-$(date +%s)
  2. Pass copy path as ImportStatePhase.sandbox_tfstate=Path(...)
  3. ImportStatePhase runs:
     a. terraform init in output_dir
     b. terraform plan -state=<sandbox_tfstate>
     c. parse plan output: if any "- destroy" line → ABORT (PhaseResult.ok=False)
     d. terraform apply -state=<sandbox_tfstate> (sandbox-only)
     e. compare sandbox state vs original: import count must equal len(plan.terraform_imports)
  4. ONLY after sandbox green, operator runs the same with -state=<live>:
     - atomic state swap: cp live.tfstate live.tfstate.bak; cp sandbox.tfstate live.tfstate
     - this is the moment of mutation; everything before is idempotent

Code-level enforcement: ImportStatePhase raises SandboxStateGuardError if sandbox_tfstate=None or path missing. Tested in test_apply.test_refuses_without_sandbox_copy.

==========================================================================
D. PER-PHASE UNDO RUNBOOK
==========================================================================
Every phase records its undo command. On failure: print + abort.

Phase 1 ValidatePhase ............ READ-ONLY, no undo needed
Phase 2 EmitV2TerraformPhase ..... undo: rm -rf terraform/v2-generated/  (safe, no AWS state)
Phase 3 ImportStatePhase ......... undo: cp live.tfstate.bak live.tfstate  (revert atomic swap)
Phase 4 ServicesCutoverPhase ..... undo: aws ecs update-service --task-definition <prev_arn>  (per service, recorded)
Phase 5 DecommissionV1Phase ...... undo: mv archive/rc.yml.<ts> rc.yml  (file move, reversible)

Critical: NO phase calls delete_secret, delete_file_system, delete_load_balancer, or delete_certificate. Tripwire test in test_apply.test_no_aws_destroy_calls.

==========================================================================
E. MAINTENANCE WINDOW CUTOVER SEQUENCE (1hr budget)
==========================================================================
Pre-window (no downtime):
  - Phase 1 Validate (5min, read-only)
  - Phase 2 Emit v2 terraform (1min)
  - Phase 3 ImportState against sandbox copy (10min) — must be GREEN before window opens

Window opens (downtime starts):
  T+0   Phase 3 ImportState atomic swap + apply against live (5min)
  T+5   Phase 4 ServicesCutoverPhase: register new task defs (1min)
  T+6   Phase 4: update each of 7 services (rolling, ~5min each, sequential to keep blast radius small) -> 35min
  T+41  Health-check sweep: ALB target group healthy, /api/health/ 200, celery: healthy (5min)
  T+46  GO/NO-GO: psycopg2 SELECT canary row from prod postgres -> matches pre-migration value (2min)
  T+48  Phase 5 Decommission v1 rc.yml (archive, no AWS calls) (1min)
  T+49  Done. Window: 49min < 60min budget.

Rollback budget: 1hr separately. If GO/NO-GO fails at T+46:
  - aws ecs update-service --task-definition <v1_arn> for each of 7 services (parallel) -> 5min
  - cp live.tfstate.bak live.tfstate (atomic revert) -> 1s
  - DNS unchanged throughout (ALB import = no DNS swing)
  - Total rollback < 10min. Stack returns to v1 state.

==========================================================================
F. RISK SUMMARY
==========================================================================
1. EFS data loss .................. Mitigated by IMPORT (terraform never destroys imported resources unless explicitly removed from config). Sandbox-state-copy catches any 'destroy' line.
2. DNS hole ....................... Mitigated by ALB IMPORT — same DNS name, same listeners, same cert. No DNS change needed.
3. SM 30d name lock ............... Mitigated by source=arn (zero SM mutation).
4. Brief task restart on cutover .. Acceptable — 7 services * ~5min rolling = 35min, fits budget.
5. terraform plan misread ......... Mitigated by code-level destroy-line detection in ImportStatePhase. Test in test_apply.test_aborts_if_terraform_plan_shows_destroy.
6. Drift between discover and apply Mitigated by ValidatePhase re-discover + diff vs plan inventory. Test in test_apply.test_drift_detected.
7. Operator runs apply against live by mistake ... Mitigated by SandboxStateGuardError requiring explicit sandbox_tfstate path. Test in test_apply.test_refuses_without_sandbox_copy.

==========================================================================
G. UNBLOCKS

title: [startsimpli-prod-migration] 1.2 System Requirements
description: Translate user requirements into concrete technical constraints + tooling shape. Mirror the aws-copilot-import architecture (rc-e5u.43): a discover layer that reads source state, a translate layer with small per-resource transformers, a composer producing a MigrationPlan dataclass + summary, a CLI thin wrapper. Concrete shape: remote_compose/v1_migrate/{discover.py, translate.py, plan.py, apply.py, __init__.py} + tests/unit/test_v1_migrate/ + tests/fixtures/v1_migrate/ (committed v1 rc.yml + mocked boto3 inventory snapshots). Discover layer: parse v1 rc.yml + use boto3 to inventory LIVE AWS resources tagged with the v1 project_name (ECS cluster, services, task defs, EFS volumes, ALB, target groups, listeners, ACM cert, Route53 record, SM secrets, ECR repos, IAM execution role, security groups, VPC + subnets). Translate layer: per-resource transformers — translate_v1_to_v2_schema (rc.yml shape), translate_efs_in_place (terraform import block emission for the EFS file_system + access_points), translate_alb_in_place (target_group import), translate_acm_in_place (cert import), translate_secrets_keep_arn (use rc.yml secrets[*].source=arn pointing at existing SM ARNs instead of recreating via env_file_auto), translate_ecr_reuse (no-op — repo names match across v1/v2 by convention). Plan layer: produce MigrationPlan(phases=[validate, dry_run_emit_v2_terraform, import_state, dns_cutover, decommission_v1], terraform_import_directives=[...], runbook=str). Apply layer: --dry-run executes phases against a sandbox copy of state, --execute requires explicit confirmation per phase. Performance: must NOT lock prod for >5min during DNS cutover (TTL on api.startsimpli.com R53 record dictates window). Security: zero secrets-blob mutation — reuse existing SM ARNs verbatim. Integration: rc-e5u.43.10 (copilot e2e against multiple real apps) is the structural template. The rc-e5u.46.6 (rc-only acceptance for ephemeral) is what we're migrating TO; same v2 deploy code path, different INPUT shape.
acceptance_criteria: Notes field contains: complete tooling-module layout matching the architecture above; complete list of AWS resources to import vs recreate (with rationale per resource); explicit terraform-state-mutation plan; DNS cutover plan with TTL math; secrets-reuse plan (no SM mutation); rollback plan.

== Per-resource decision matrix ==

ECS cluster:                IMPORT (preserve so dependent services don't deregister)
ECS services (×7):          RECREATE under v2 management (services are wrappers; recreating

ECS task definitions (×7):  RECREATE (v2 emits new revisions; ECS handles atomically)

EFS access points (×7):     IMPORT (mount-point pointers; recreating breaks task-def refs
                            mid-deploy)
ALB:                        IMPORT (DNS aliased outside this account — recreate = outage)
ALB listeners (×2):         IMPORT (cert reference + redirect rule)
ALB target groups (×2):     IMPORT (service registrations)
ACM cert:                   IMPORT (already issued; recreate = DNS validation cycle)
Route53 api.startsimpli.com NO-OP (records live elsewhere; nothing to manage in v2)
SM secrets (×32):           REFERENCE BY ARN (secrets[*].source=arn in v2 rc.yml)
VPC + subnets + IGW + RTs:  IMPORT
Security groups (×5):       IMPORT

translate_efs_in_place(efs_inventory) -> (rc_yml_volumes, import_blocks)
translate_alb_in_place(alb_inv, listeners, target_groups) -> import_blocks

Each returns (overrides, terraform_imports, warnings) tuple matching

== terraform-state-mutation plan ==

1. Pre-flight: cp -r terraform/<v1>/ terraform/<v2-staging>/
2. Emit v2 terraform module into staging dir (provider.emit_terraform()).
3. Append `import { id=<arn>; to=<addr> }` blocks to staging *.tf files
   for every IMPORT resource above.
4. terraform plan in staging — MUST show 0 destroys, N adds, M imports.
   If plan shows a destroy on EFS/ALB/cert: ABORT.
5. User reviews plan + approves explicitly.
6. terraform apply in staging — state mutates with imports + adds.
7. Atomic swap: mv terraform/<v1>/terraform.tfstate terraform/<v1>.backup-<ts>/ &&
                mv terraform/<v2-staging>/terraform.tfstate terraform/<v1>/
8. terraform plan in real dir — must show 0 changes (drift=0).

== DNS cutover plan ==

NO DNS CHANGE.
- api.startsimpli.com is aliased at the registrar level (outside this
  AWS account) to the existing ALB DNS name.
- ALB import (not recreate) keeps the same DNS name.
- TTL math: irrelevant; no DNS swap.
- The api.startsimpli.com R53 zone in our account (Z00022951OO3UQJSGC9FG)
  has only NS+SOA — touch nothing.

== Secrets-reuse plan ==

ZERO SM mutation.
- 32 existing ss-debuggai-prod/<KEY> ARNs are referenced by their
  exact ARN in v2 rc.yml secrets:
    secrets:
      - name: USE_DOCKER
        source: arn
        arn: arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-west-2:033937118837:secret:ss-debuggai-prod/USE_DOCKER-YAXJLy
      ...
- provider.ecs translates each into task-def secrets[] with
  valueFrom: <arn> (no JSON-key:: suffix needed since these are
  per-key blobs).
- Existing values preserved in place; name reservation preserved;
  no 30d recovery risk.

== Rollback plan ==

Pre-cutover snapshot:
  cp -r terraform/<v1-stack> terraform/<v1>.backup-<timestamp>

Per-phase undo (recorded in runbook.json):
  ValidatePhase:        no-op (read-only).
  EmitV2TerraformPhase: rm -rf terraform/<v2-staging>.
  ImportStatePhase:     mv terraform/<v1>.backup-<ts>/* terraform/<v1>/.
  ServicesCutoverPhase: aws ecs update-service --task-definition <v1-arn>
                        per service (revert to old task def).
  DecommissionV1Phase:  N/A — only after a 7+ day soak.

Post-cutover smoke fail:
  - revert task defs via the cutover undo (ECS swaps back to v1 task def).
  - ALB/EFS/cert untouched (still pointing at same data).
  - Total time: <30 min worst case (state restore + 7 task-def reverts).

Time budget overall: planned 1hr maintenance window; rollback
budget separate 1hr window.

LOCKED 2026-04-27 by Quinn:

1. Downtime budget: <=1 hour maintenance window (announceable to customers).
2. DB strategy: IN-PLACE EFS preservation. 15 GB on EFS today; logical pg_dump/pg_restore would not fit in the 1hr budget. Tooling will use terraform 'import { id=...; to=... }' blocks to absorb the existing aws_efs_file_system + aws_efs_access_point resources into v2-managed state. NO data motion.

title: rc up --domain should auto-inject CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS / ALLOWED_HOSTS into django service env
description: Verified 2026-04-27 deploying start-simpli to https://startsimpli-sample.rctest.ezapps.ai: rc up --domain wires the ALB to the subdomain + ACM cert + R53 records correctly, but the deployed django returns CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED on the new origin. Reason: Django's CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS + ALLOWED_HOSTS settings need the subdomain in their lists, but rc has no awareness of those Django-specific knobs at deploy time. Fix: when --domain is set AND a service matches the django framework preset (rc-e5u.47), inject DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=<domain>,<aliases> + CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://<domain>,<aliases> into the service env (matching the framework preset's testing_defaults_env shape but driven by --domain not project-name-prefix). Same applies to Rails (RAILS_HOSTS) and Phoenix (PHX_HOST). Without this, every --domain deploy hits the CSRF wall and the user has to hand-edit settings or env files.
close_reason: Fixed via Framework.domain_env() + cli_v2.build_deploy_context injection. When rc.yml services.<svc>.domain is set AND the service's Dockerfile matches a framework preset (django/rails/phoenix), inject domain-aware env vars (DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS + CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, RAILS_HOSTS, PHX_HOST) UNDER the user's rc.yml.env so explicit overrides win. Tests in tests/unit/test_frameworks_domain_env.py (11 cases). Real-AWS validation today: sentinal-test.rctest.ezapps.ai admin login over HTTPS now works without manual settings.py CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS edit.

title: rc.yml services.<svc>.env override of SM-sourced key crashes ECS task-def
description: When env_file_auto routes a key to AWS Secrets Manager AND services.<svc>.env in rc.yml declares the same key with a plaintext override, ECS RegisterTaskDefinition rejects with 'The secret name must be unique and not shared with any new or existing environment variables set on the container, such as <KEY>'. Verified 2026-04-27 trying to override CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS for the startsimpli-sample.rctest.ezapps.ai deploy: env was already in SM via env_file_auto, rc.yml env override added it to environment[] without stripping from secrets[]. Workaround used: aws secretsmanager put-secret-value to update the SM blob in place + force-roll. Fix: cli_v2._service_env / build_deploy_context should detect overlap and strip the SM secrets[] entry for any key that has a corresponding rc.yml env override (rc.yml env wins). Acceptance: write a v2 rc.yml with env_file_auto + services.django.env containing a key that's also in the env_file; build_deploy_context emits a task def with that key only in environment[] (plaintext), not in secrets[].
acceptance_criteria: ECS RegisterTaskDefinition succeeds when env_file_auto and services.<svc>.env share a key; the plaintext env value wins and the SM secret entry is suppressed for that key only. Unit test in test_env_file_auto.py covers the overlap case.
close_reason: Fixed at provider.py:493 (per-service secret filter) + services.tf.j2 (template now reads svc.secrets not global secrets). When rc.yml services.<svc>.env declares a key that's also sourced from SM (env_file_auto / source: file), that service's task def now puts the key only in environment[]; the SM secret entry is suppressed for THAT service only (other services still get the full secrets list). Tests in tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_env_secret_collision.py: 2 cases — collision with override drops from secrets[] but preserves on services without override; no override means full secrets list emitted. 1485 unit+contract green (zero regressions).

title: (EPIC) Framework presets — generic framework detection + per-framework defaults
description: The .44 and .46 epics shipped Django-specific code paths: _looks_like_django_service heuristic, hardcoded migrate command, hardcoded DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=* env, hardcoded 'proxy_set_header Host localhost' rewrite for the --django nginx-conf flag, hardcoded celery-beat singleton patterns. This was the right pragmatic call to ship rc-only acceptance for start-simpli, but rc is a generic deploy tool — Rails, Phoenix, Elixir, Next.js, Go, FastAPI, NestJS users hit the same gotchas with framework-specific knobs. Refactor: introduce remote_compose/frameworks.py with a Framework dataclass (name, dockerfile_markers, migrate_command, host_strict_env_overrides, singleton_command_patterns, host_strict_validation_flag). Detect framework from Dockerfile + compose. Every Django-specific check becomes a framework-lookup against this registry. Built-ins for the rc-e5u.46 acceptance: django + rails + phoenix at minimum (for code-path proof) — others can be community-contributed dictionaries with no rc code change. Backward compat: rc.yml services[*].framework: django|rails|... overrides detection.
acceptance_criteria: A NON-Django stack (e.g., a Rails app's docker-compose with manage.py-equivalent + celery-equivalent) deploys via 'rc up' and gets correct migrate hook (rails db:migrate), correct env injection (RAILS_FORCE_SSL=false / etc.), correct nginx Host rewrite. ALL existing Django start-simpli acceptance (.46.6) STILL passes. The Django code paths in compose_warnings.py / init_from_compose.py / fix_nginx_conf.py / provider.ecs.provider.py reference frameworks.<framework_name> instead of inline string matching.
notes: Framework registry shipped: remote_compose/frameworks.py with Framework dataclass + DJANGO/RAILS/PHOENIX built-ins + detect_framework() + framework_by_name() + register_framework(). Refactored call sites: compose_warnings._looks_like_django_service is now a thin wrapper, init_from_compose uses framework.migrate_command + framework.testing_defaults_env (Django-shaped path is now framework-shaped path), detect_nginx_auto_fix_target filters by framework.host_header_rewrite. Built-in presets: django (manage.py + DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=* + Host: localhost rewrite), rails (Gemfile + RAILS_HOSTS=* + bundle exec rails db:migrate), phoenix (mix.exs + PHX_HOST=* + mix ecto.migrate). 23 new unit tests + all 1181 existing pass. Verified Django start-simpli scaffolding output unchanged — lifecycle.migrate hook + ALLOWED_HOSTS=* still emitted exactly as before.

title: e5u.46.10: celery-beat (and other singleton schedulers) need stateful=True even without volumes
description: Verified 2026-04-26 .46.6 run #7 against rc-test-startsimpli (project: start-simpli-api): everything else green — postgres/redis/django/nginx/celery-worker all healthy, ALB returns 200 on /api/v1/health/ with {status:healthy, database:healthy, redis:healthy, celery:healthy} — but celery-beat services in a flap loop ('5 tasks started' across the events list). Root cause: celery-beat is a SINGLETON scheduler. With default ECS deploymentConfiguration (min=100, max=200, rolling deploy), the new beat task starts BEFORE the old one is killed → both contend for the celerybeat-schedule lock file → both die → ECS replaces, repeat. Provider currently treats stateful=True only when svc has EFS-backed volumes (services.tf.j2:148). Need a SECOND signal: detect singleton-style commands. Heuristics: (a) command contains 'celery beat' / 'celerybeat' / 'celery -A * beat'; (b) service name ends in -beat / -scheduler / -singleton; (c) explicit rc.yml services[*].singleton: true field. Apply same min=0/max=100 + availability_zone_rebalancing=DISABLED treatment as stateful services. Pair with .45.11 — same root semantics (one instance at a time), same terraform fix.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh start-simpli deploy, celery-beat reaches running=1/1 and STAYS there (no flap) within the same window as the other services. /api/v1/health/ continues to report celery: healthy. e2e script's [3/7] healthy-services check passes for all 6 services. Verified by .46.6 run on real AWS.
close_reason: Shipped: provider/ecs/provider.py:_looks_like_singleton_scheduler detects -beat/-scheduler/-cron suffix + 'celery beat'/'celerybeat' command patterns. stateful = len(svc_mounts) > 0 OR singleton, which sets deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0 / maximum=100 / availability_zone_rebalancing=DISABLED. 14 tests in test_singleton_scheduler.py. Verified e2e against start-simpli celery-beat 2026-04-26 — boots cleanly under stop-then-start semantics, no flap loop.

title: e5u.46.7: rc up --domain — wire ALB to a custom subdomain in one flag
description: Verified context 2026-04-26: rc already supports services.<svc>.domain + .aliases + provider_config.ecs.route53_zone (used in the sentinal stack on rctest.ezapps.ai — ACM cert with SAN, Route 53 A records, DNS validation, all clean teardown). But for the rc-only acceptance flow, the user has to: (1) know about those rc.yml fields, (2) hand-edit the scaffolded rc.yml to add them, (3) ensure the parent zone is delegated to AWS already. For test stacks the friction is overkill. Add a single --domain flag to 'rc up' that auto-wires onto the scaffolded rc.yml's public service: domain: <FQDN>, aliases: [...] (from --alias multi-flag), provider_config.ecs.route53_zone: <derived> (drop leftmost label by default; --route53-zone for explicit override). Pre-flight check: 'aws route53 list-hosted-zones' must show the zone exists in the configured aws_profile + region (otherwise nothing to add records to). Pair with .44.21 (rc fix nginx-conf) so the generated nginx config trusts the configured domain in ALLOWED_HOSTS / Host header rewrites.

Single rc command, no /tmp file edits, no aws cli.

Pre-flight verifies Route 53 hosted zone exists; idempotent rc.yml patcher mutates services.<public>.domain + .aliases + provider_config.ecs.route53_zone. Drop-leftmost-label default zone derivation; --route53-zone overrides. 15 unit tests cover the surface.

title: e5u.46.5: celery workers reach steady state without manual reconciliation
description: Verified 2026-04-26 multiple times: celery-worker + celery-beat tasks fail on first deploy (django not yet ready / migrations not yet run / SM secrets not yet populated) and ECS exponential backoff stalls them in 'failed task' loops for 10+ minutes. Even after manual 'rc deploy --services celery-worker' the workers come up but report 'celery: no_workers' through django's health check. Two things going on: (1) ECS doesn't re-cycle stuck-on-failed-rev tasks promptly (covered by .44.24's --reconcile flag); (2) celery's connection to the broker takes longer than ECS's task-startup health check window. Add: (a) celery worker depends_on django service ready (or postgres+redis healthy at minimum) — emit ECS service-connect deps in terraform; (b) celery health check via 'celery -A config inspect ping' instead of relying on the ALB; (c) auto-trigger 'rc deploy --reconcile' as a fallback when 'rc deploy' detects partial failure on celery-* services. Pairs with .44.24.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh 'rc up --from-compose start-simpli/docker-compose.local.yml' deploy: within 5 minutes of the rc up exit, 'curl http://<ALB>/api/v1/health/' returns HTTP 200 with body containing 'celery: healthy' (not 'no_workers'). No manual rc deploy --reconcile or rc deploy --services celery-* needed.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-26 (unit-tested; real-AWS verification deferred to .46.6 which exercises the full pipeline). Diagnosis: cold-start failure mode where ALL services force-roll simultaneously. Workers race postgres/redis health + django migrations, fail to connect to broker, ECS exponential backoff stalls them at 0 running for 5-10+ minutes. Fix: ECSProvider._force_new_deployments now sorts services by type priority — infrastructure (0) → application (1) → worker (2) → proxy (3). Within each tier, alpha-sorted for stable / reproducible logs. Default ECS deploymentConfiguration (min=100/max=200) handles the rest of the convergence naturally — old tasks keep serving while new come up. The ordering primes infra first so postgres+redis are starting before django; django before workers; workers before nginx. Unknown service types treated as application (priority 1), defensive against future schema additions. _DEPLOY_ORDER constant on ECSProvider so it's discoverable + overridable. Tests: tests/unit/test_force_roll_order.py with 7 cases — pairwise tier ordering (infra-before-app, app-before-worker, worker-before-proxy), full start-simpli 6-service order verification, unknown-type default priority, alpha-sort within tier stability, unknown-service-in-pushed-list defensive handling. Full suite: 1114->1121 passed (+7), 4 skipped, no regressions. Real-AWS proof comes from .46.6's end-to-end script run. Files: remote_compose/provider/ecs/provider.py (_DEPLOY_ORDER class const + _force_new_deployments sort), tests/unit/test_force_roll_order.py (new).

title: e5u.46.3: scaffolder + auto-config — Django services get a lifecycle.migrate hook with auto_on_deploy
description: Verified 2026-04-26: start-simpli's start.sh runs migrations on container boot, but stale migrations / migration-ordering bugs (the contacts.0016 issue from earlier) cascade because MIGRATE happens INSIDE the django container's normal startup. When migrations fail, the django task exits 1 and ECS retries forever. The right pattern (already supported by rc, just not auto-emitted): lifecycle.migrate as a SEPARATE one-shot hook with auto_on_deploy=true so 'rc deploy' runs migrations via execute-command BEFORE the new task def goes live. Failure surfaces clearly + django container itself only does runtime work. The .44.10 scaffolder already detects Django via _looks_like_django_service; extend it to emit services.django.lifecycle.migrate with the standard 'python manage.py migrate --noinput' command + auto_on_deploy: true.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh 'rc init --from-compose' on a Django compose produces an rc.yml with services.django.lifecycle.migrate populated correctly. 'rc deploy' runs migrations via execute-command + reports success/failure clearly. The django task itself doesn't run migrations on container startup (no entrypoint coupling).
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-26. generate_v2_rc_yml now reuses compose_warnings._looks_like_django_service to detect Django services and emits services.<svc>.lifecycle.migrate = {command: [python, manage.py, migrate, --noinput], auto_on_deploy: true}. Default command chosen for universal compatibility (works with any venv layout, --noinput suppresses the data-loss confirmation prompt that would otherwise hang execute-command). Files changed: remote_compose/init_from_compose.py (import + DEFAULT_DJANGO_MIGRATE_COMMAND constant + lifecycle block in service-entry loop), tests/unit/test_init_from_compose.py (new TestLifecycleMigrate, 6 cases). Stretch goal (preserve user lifecycle on --force re-init) punted — generate_v2_rc_yml is a pure str→str function with no merge semantics; CLI-level merge is a separate concern out of this bead's scope.

title: e5u.46.1: services[*].dockerfile override in rc.yml — kill the /tmp compose dance
description: Verified 2026-04-26: rc.yml v2 reads compose_file verbatim. To deploy nginx with an ECS-aware Dockerfile (compose/ecs/nginx/Dockerfile) WITHOUT modifying the user's docker-compose.local.yml, I had to (a) copy local.yml to /tmp/docker-compose.ecs-test.yml, (b) sed-edit the nginx build.dockerfile path, (c) sed-rewrite every relative path to absolute (env_file, build context, volumes) because /tmp resolution broke them all. title: rc dev push chicken-and-egg: containers exit on empty EFS before push can land
description: Discovered during .45.12 real-AWS verification on rc-test-startsimpli. 'rc deploy --dev' swaps the django service onto an EFS-backed /app mount. EFS starts EMPTY. The django container entrypoint (/start -> manage.py runserver) immediately fails because manage.py is gone, exits with code 2, ECS replaces the task, the new task fails the same way, and after ~2 failures ECS throttles task placement. 'rc dev push' requires a RUNNING task to aws-ecs-execute-command into, so it cannot land any code. Design hole: dev mode assumes the container will tolerate an empty /app, but most real entrypoints can't. Fixes to consider: (a) seed EFS at deploy time via a one-shot task before the service starts, (b) inject a wait-for-first-push shim entrypoint in dev mode that keeps the container alive (e.g. tail -f /dev/null until manage.py exists), (c) make 'rc deploy --dev' upload the source as part of the deploy itself. Repro: rc.local.yml has django dev_volumes: [{name: src, source: ../Users/qosha/Repos/start-simpli/start-simpli-api/backend, mount: /app}], run rc deploy --dev --services django --no-build, ECS task starts and exits with EssentialContainerExited, runningCount stays 0 forever.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) rc deploy --dev seeds the EFS volume from the local source before the service starts, OR (b) dev mode injects a tolerant entrypoint that keeps the container alive until rc dev push lands files. End state: after rc up --dev, the django container is RUNNING (even before any rc dev push), so the rc dev push exec-command path can connect.

title: e5u.44.20: rc deploy must auto-push (or hard-warn) when SM secrets reference an empty blob
description: Verified 2026-04-26: switching compose_file from rc-test-startsimpli's original to a /tmp variant changed the env_file_auto secret name (basename fallback 'postgres' vs 'local-postgres'). Terraform created a new SM secret 'rc-test-startsimpli/postgres' with no values (placeholder only). 'rc deploy --services nginx' completed with exit 0 + 'Deploy complete', but ECS tasks all failed with 'retrieved secret from Secrets Manager did not contain json key POSTGRES_HOST' for ~10 minutes before I noticed. Two fixes: (a) detect at deploy-time that file-sourced secrets reference SM blobs with NO keys + auto-run secrets push (matches rc up's behavior), (b) emit a hard warning + non-zero exit when any secret is empty. Today's behavior — 'Deploy complete' followed by silent failure cascade — is the worst of both worlds. Pair with: also detect when SM secret name CHANGED between deploys (compose_file rename, secret rename) so the user knows that old SM secrets may be orphaned.

After fix: deploy either auto-runs secrets push for the new secret OR exits non-zero with 'secret X is empty in SM, run rc secrets push first'. Verified by: change one secret name in /tmp/rc.local.yml, run rc deploy, observe correct outcome.

title: e5u.45.11: ECS provider — availability_zone_rebalancing conflicts with deployment_minimum_healthy_percent <=100 on stateful services
description: Verified 2026-04-26 during .45.8 EFS provisioning on rc-test-startsimpli: the django service update for the new EFS-mounted task def failed with: 'InvalidParameterException: availability_zone_rebalancing does not support maximumPercent <= 100'. Per rc-e5u memory: provider auto-sets deploymentConfiguration.minimumHealthyPercent=0 / maximumPercent=100 for ANY service with EFS mounts (rolling deploys corrupt stateful EFS when two tasks briefly mount the same dir). Newer ECS API rejects this combination when availabilityZoneRebalancing is ENABLED (which is the new ECS default). Two compatible fixes: (a) set availabilityZoneRebalancing=DISABLED on services with stateful volumes, (b) bump maximumPercent to 200 for stateful services (allowed by AZ-rebalancing) and rely on deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0 alone for the rolling-deploy guard. (a) is more correct — AZ rebalancing actively spreads tasks which is opposite of what stateful workloads want. (b) is more permissive. File terraform aws_ecs_service resource has 'availability_zone_rebalancing' arg.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running 'rc deploy' against the rc-test-startsimpli stack with .45.8's dev_volumes does NOT raise InvalidParameterException; django service update succeeds + the new EFS-backed task def becomes ACTIVE. Test: 'rc -c /tmp/rc.local.yml deploy' completes without ECS API error and 'aws ecs describe-services --services django --query .deployments[0].rolloutState' returns COMPLETED.

Fix: services.tf.j2 emits availability_zone_rebalancing="DISABLED" inside the existing svc.stateful gate (alongside deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0 / maximum_percent=100). The svc.stateful flag in provider.py:emit_terraform already covers both volumes and dev_volumes (mounts list). Files: remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/services.tf.j2 (+8 lines), tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_efs_volumes.py (+33 lines new test), tests/fixtures/golden/ecs_minimal/services.tf (regenerated, +7 lines on db service). title: e5u.44.19: improve .44.18 warning — VPC resolver IP, FQDN, Host header
description: Verified 2026-04-26 against rc-test-startsimpli: the .44.18 nginx upstream-resolver detector emits an actionable warning, but the recommended fix recipe has 3 problems exposed during real deploy. (1) Resolver IP: warning recommends '169.254.169.253' which is the EC2-host metadata service IP — UNREACHABLE from a Fargate awsvpc task ENI. The actual reachable resolver is the VPC's own .2 address (vpc_cidr base + 2 = e.g. 10.42.0.2 for vpc 10.42.0.0/16). nginx config-load doesn't fail on the wrong IP (resolver directive is lazy) but every per-request lookup times out → 502 cascade. (2) Hostname form: nginx's resolver does NOT follow /etc/resolv.conf search domains. So 'set $u "django:8000"' issues a bare 'django' query → NXDOMAIN. The FQDN 'django.<project>.local:8000' works. (3) Host header: even when the proxy succeeds, Django's ALLOWED_HOSTS check rejects the ALB DNS → 400 SuspiciousOperation. Need a 'proxy_set_header Host localhost;' (or similar) for the django location. Fix: rewrite the warning text to derive the right resolver IP from rc.yml's vpc_cidr, use FQDN <service>.<project>.local:<port>, and mention the ALLOWED_HOSTS gotcha when the upstream service is named 'django' or has a Python framework (heuristic on Dockerfile).
acceptance_criteria: On the start-simpli stack, 'rc plan' for nginx prints a warning that recommends 'resolver 10.42.0.2 valid=10s ipv6=off;' (derived from provider_config.ecs.vpc_cidr) + 'set $u "django.rc-test-startsimpli.local:8000"' (FQDN) + a note about Host header / ALLOWED_HOSTS for django. A user following the recipe verbatim gets a working ECS nginx on first deploy, no second-loop debugging.

Warning text rewritten: (1) recommends 'resolver <vpc-base+2> valid=10s ipv6=off;' instead of the wrong 169.254.169.253 (with parenthetical 'the VPC's .2 address — Fargate tasks can't reach 169.254.169.253' to explicitly disabuse the user), (2) recommends 'set $u "<svc>.<project>.local:<port>"' (FQDN form — nginx's resolver does not follow /etc/resolv.conf search domain), (3) appends a Django gotcha line with 'proxy_set_header Host localhost' when the upstream service's Dockerfile looks Django-shaped. title: e5u.44.18: 'rc plan' warns when nginx.conf upstream uses bare hostname without resolver directive (ECS Cloud Map gotcha)
description: Verified 2026-04-26 on rc-test-startsimpli stack: nginx fails at startup with 'host not found in upstream "django:8000"' even though django IS registered in Cloud Map and DHCP search path is correct. Stock nginx resolves upstream{} hostnames ONCE at config-load. If lookup fails (timing window during task replacement) or succeeds-then-stales (next task gets a new IP), nginx is broken. Affects every as-front pattern (nginx public, django private via service-discovery). The compose dev pattern works because docker-compose's embedded DNS resolver is reachable + names are stable. Detect compose nginx services with build context, scan referenced .conf files for 'upstream NAME { server SVC:PORT;' patterns where SVC matches a compose service name, emit a warning during 'rc plan' instructing user to add: 'resolver 169.254.169.253 valid=10s; set $X ":$port"; proxy_pass http://$X;'. Stretch: scaffolder could rewrite nginx.conf with a sed pass when --fix-nginx is set.

title: e5u.45.2: BuildKit cache mount in init_from_compose Dockerfile guidance + scaffolder hints
description: Most rebuild time is 'pip install -r requirements/local.txt' (~3-5min on a fresh layer cache). With BuildKit cache mounts, that drops to <30s on cache hit. Two parts: (a) emit a docs section in the scaffolder's rc.yml output pointing at how to add 'RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install ...' to the Dockerfile; (b) ensure 'rc deploy' invokes 'docker buildx build --cache-from / --cache-to' against an ECR cache repo (one per project) so layer cache survives across machines and CI runs. Default cache repo: <project>-buildcache.

Verified by: timing both runs + 'docker history' on the resulting image showing identical layer SHAs except the final source layer.
notes: REAL-AWS VERIFICATION 2026-04-26 against rc-test-startsimpli (us-west-1, account 033937118837): cold deploy 99.3s (terraform applies new buildcache repo + first cache push); cache-hit deploy after 1-line manage.py touch: 17.8s — 5.6x speedup vs cold, 2.6x vs .45.1 baseline (47s). buildcache repo created (rc-test-startsimpli/buildcache) with django-cache tag populated. Reproducible via: 'echo "# touch" >> backend/manage.py && time .venv/bin/rc -c /tmp/rc.local.yml deploy --services django'.
close_reason:
VERIFIED 2026-04-26 (unit + emitted-tf only; real-AWS deferred — see below).

WHAT BUILT
- ImageBuilder: ImageBuildSpec gains cache_from/cache_to; when either is set the builder switches from 'docker build' to 'docker buildx build --load' and emits --cache-from type=registry,ref=<URL> / --cache-to type=registry,ref=<URL>,mode=max. mode=max is load-bearing — without it cache only exports the final stage and the pip-install layer rebuilds every time. --load brings the image into the local store so the subsequent docker push finds it. Classic 'docker build' path preserved when no cache args set (compat for installs without buildx).
- terraform (services.tf.j2 + outputs.tf.j2): when any service has a compose build: context, emit one shared aws_ecr_repository.buildcache (${var.project}/buildcache) plus an aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy expiring untagged layers after 7 days, and a buildcache_repository output. Pure-image stacks skip the resource entirely (gated on new has_build_context_service ctx flag).
- ECSProvider._build_and_push_images: reads buildcache_repository from outputs (None on older stacks → degrades to no-cache), pre-auths the cache registry via ECRAuthenticator (cached by host), then for each service with a build context computes <buildcache>:<svc>-cache and feeds it into both ImageBuildSpec.cache_from and cache_to. Auth failure on the cache registry is non-fatal: warn + fall back to no-cache builds.
- init_from_compose.py: scaffolder header now documents the BuildKit cache-mount pattern (RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install ... and the equivalent apt cache mounts), plus a one-liner that 'rc deploy' uses the shared ECR registry cache automatically. Did NOT touch the rc.yml body or rewrite Dockerfiles.

FILES CHANGED
- remote_compose/image/builder.py (+22 lines)
- remote_compose/provider/ecs/provider.py (+24 lines, _build_and_push_images + emit_terraform context)
- remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/services.tf.j2 (+34 lines, gated buildcache repo + lifecycle policy)
- remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/outputs.tf.j2 (+9 lines, gated buildcache_repository output)
- remote_compose/init_from_compose.py (+13 lines, header tip block)

TESTS
- New tests/unit/test_image/test_buildkit_cache.py (7 tests: classic-vs-buildx routing, cache-from/-to arg format, mode=max, --load, multi-flag combo).
- Extended tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_image_deploy.py with 4 tests: cache args wired when buildcache present, degrades when absent, terraform emits buildcache for build-context stacks, skips for pure-image stacks.
- Extended tests/unit/test_init_from_compose.py with 1 test: header mentions BuildKit cache mount tip.
- Suite: 945 passed, 4 skipped (baseline 926; +19 net — includes 12 new from this bead plus 7 that already existed in the workspace before my changes). Golden fixture untouched (canonical ctx has no build_context, so emits identically).

REAL-AWS VERIFICATION — DEFERRED
Did NOT run two consecutive 'rc deploy --services django' against rc-test-startsimpli to time cold-vs-warm cache (the bead's acceptance criterion). Reason per ticket context: parallel work is in flight on that exact stack right now (someone fixing the unrelated nginx 503), and a fresh 'rc deploy' would re-emit terraform (creating the new buildcache repo) and force a new task deployment, which could collide with the in-flight nginx fix or clobber the proxy work. Manual verification command for the user when the parallel work lands:
    cd <project> && rc deploy --services django   # cold: ~5min, populates buildcache:django-cache
    touch backend/manage.py                        # invalidate the source COPY only
    rc deploy --services django                   # warm: should be <30s, all pip layers cached
    docker history <api-repo>:latest              # all layer SHAs identical except final source COPY
Cache repo + lifecycle policy will be auto-created on first deploy (additive resource — no destroy/recreate of anything else).

KEY DECISIONS
- One shared cache repo per project, per-service tag, NOT one repo per service. Halves the lifecycle-policy footprint and matches the buildx convention.
- mode=max non-negotiable (intermediate-stage caching is the entire point).
- Cache repo gated on has_build_context_service to keep pure-image stacks zero-cost.
- Provider degrades to no-cache when buildcache_repository absent so old terraform state stays compatible (no forced re-init).
- Cache-registry auth failure is a warning, not a hard error — a flaky ECR token shouldn't block a deploy.

DEFERRED / NOT IN SCOPE
- Real-AWS timing run (above).
- DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 env injection — modern docker enables BuildKit by default and 'docker buildx' subcommand bypasses the toggle anyway.
- Rewriting user Dockerfiles to add cache mounts (per ticket: 'Don't try to rewrite Dockerfiles' — guidance in scaffolder header instead).
- rc-e5u.45.3 (--tag <existing> short-circuit) is the natural follow-up; not part of this bead.

title: (EPIC) Hot reload + fast iteration on deployed stacks
description: After ephemeral deploys (rc-e5u.44) the next friction is iteration: today a code change requires a full rebuild + ECR push + ECS redeploy that takes ~520s on a fresh stack and ~70-300s on a redeploy. Make the dev loop survive real iteration: edit local code, see it run in the cloud within seconds, repeat. Three approaches, ship in priority order. (A) Fast incremental redeploy — single-service builds with BuildKit cache, target ~30-60s. Already viable today as 'rc deploy --services <name>' but undocumented + uncached. (B) Sync into running container — 'rc sync <service>' rsync-style push via 'aws ecs execute-command' tar pipe + framework-specific reload signal (Django SIGHUP / gunicorn SIGUSR2 / touch wsgi.py). Target 5-15s. (C) EFS-backed bind mount — services[*].dev_volumes for true hot reload of source dirs, local-to-EFS sync via watcher. Target 1-3s + auto-reload. C is heavier infra (EFS cost, schema changes) and only justified for active dev sessions; A+B cover most use cases.
acceptance_criteria: On the deployed start-simpli stack from rc-e5u.44 verification: (A) edit a Django view, run 'rc deploy --service django', see the change reflected in <90s; (B) edit a Django view, run 'rc sync django', see the change reflected in <15s; (C) edit a Django view with 'rc up --dev' active, see the change reflected in <5s with no command needed. Each approach has a runnable verification command + working scaffolder defaults so users don't need to hand-write Dockerfiles or rc.yml fragments to get the loop.

title: e5u.44.11: 'rc up' one-shot — scaffold (if missing), provision, deploy, push secrets, print ALB URL

title: Gap: rolling deploys corrupt stateful EFS when 2 tasks mount it concurrently
description: Default aws_ecs_service deployment_configuration = min 100% / max 200% means ECS starts a replacement task BEFORE stopping the old one on forceNewDeployment. For a service with a writable EFS volume (postgres being the canonical case), both tasks mount the same data dir for ~seconds; the new task's initdb wipes postgres's live data and both crash. Observed in Mini v3 smoke: Task A initialized, 'rc secrets push' triggered forceNewDeployment, Task B's initdb removed contents, Task A panicked, subsequent restarts found partial state and refused. Fix: when a service has ANY EFS volume mount, emit 'deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0' and 'deployment_maximum_percent=100' so ECS stops the old task before starting the new one. Rolling remains the default for stateless services.
close_reason: EFS volumes now support per-service uid/gid/mode on access points (default 1000/1000/0755). postgres:16-alpine uid=70 wired and verified. Separately landed 'stateful' detection: any service with EFS volumes gets deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0/maximum_percent=100 so the replacement task waits for the primary to stop before mounting — caught while Mini v3 smoke corrupted postgres data under rolling deploy. End-to-end proof: Mini v3 deploy → migrate → superuser → admin login 302 → force postgres restart → admin login 302 again with the same credentials persisted in EFS. 6 new tests, suite 537 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Phase 3: Test design — pyramid, tiers, provider contract tests
description: Design the test strategy before any test code is written. Define the pyramid: (a) unit tests on pure logic (compose parsing, rc.yml v2 parsing, terraform HCL emission), (b) contract tests that run against every Provider implementation using FakeProvider first, (c) provider-specific integration tests (moto/localstack for ECS, kind for k8s), (d) optional E2E tests behind a flag. Decide tooling, fixtures, how to fake terraform apply without actually running terraform, and CI matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Test tier breakdown is documented with examples of what each tier covers. Tooling choices are named (pytest, moto, kind, testcontainers). Contract test approach is specified so a new provider can be added by implementing the interface and running the shared contract suite.
notes:
PHASE 3 TEST DESIGN

==============================================================
TEST PYRAMID
==============================================================

Tier 1 — UNIT TESTS  (fast, zero external deps, always run)
  Scope:
    - compose YAML parsing + validation
    - rc.yml v2 pydantic model + validation
    - v1 → v2 migration logic
    - terraform HCL template rendering (jinja2 → string assertions + `terraform validate`)
    - pure helper functions (resource auto-sizing, secret reference resolution, etc.)
  Tooling: pytest
  Runtime target: <10s total
  Runs: every commit

Tier 2 — PROVIDER CONTRACT TESTS  (shared across providers, parameterized)
  Scope: the Provider ABC semantics — every Provider implementation must pass
  Parameterization:
    - FakeProvider (always)
    - ECS (if extras installed + localstack available)
    - k8s (if kind + docker available)
  Runtime target: <60s against FakeProvider; provider runs gated by env
  Runs: every commit

Tier 3 — PROVIDER INTEGRATION TESTS  (provider-specific, actual terraform apply)
  ECS: actual terraform apply against LocalStack (community tier covers most; flag
       Pro-only ops explicitly). For ops LocalStack cannot simulate (e.g. Fargate
       ENI provisioning), fall back to HCL-validate-only tests + real-AWS E2E.
  k8s: actual terraform apply against kind cluster (pytest-kind or testcontainers).
  Tooling: pytest + LocalStack + kind + docker
  Runs: on PR merge to main + nightly

Tier 4 — E2E SMOKE  (behind `pytest -m e2e`)
  Scope: deploy a minimal 3-service app (web+db+cache) to real ECS and a real k8s
  cluster, hit its public endpoint with an HTTP request, assert 200.
  Tooling: rc CLI invoked via subprocess
  Runs: nightly + pre-release

==============================================================
FAKING TERRAFORM APPLY
==============================================================

- Tier 1–2: DO NOT run terraform apply. FakeProvider bypasses terraform entirely.
  For HCL correctness, render templates to strings and run `terraform validate` on
  the rendered module (fast, offline, no state).
- Tier 3: actual `terraform apply` against LocalStack / kind.
- tests/fixtures/terraform_runner.py exposes a recording runner (stubbable) used
  in Tier 1 tests that need to assert on the sequence of terraform commands
  without executing them.

==============================================================
CONTRACT TEST SUITE (shared, Tier 2)
==============================================================

tests/contract/test_provider_contract.py  (parameterized over providers)

  1. test_deploy_idempotent
       deploy(ctx); deploy(ctx) → second is no-op, same revision_id
  2. test_deploy_reconciles_partial_failure
       inject fault mid-deploy → retry converges to desired state
  3. test_redeploy_forces_new_revision
  4. test_status_reflects_live_state
       deploy, mutate out-of-band, status reports the mutation
  5. test_logs_returns_recent_output
       deploy an echo service, logs stream contains the echoed text
  6. test_exec_runs_and_returns_exit_code
  7. test_rollback_reverts_to_previous_revision
  8. test_destroy_removes_all_created_resources
       after destroy, status returns empty, terraform state is clean
  9. test_emit_terraform_is_standalone  (FR-7)
       emit to temp dir, run `terraform init && terraform validate` as a plain
       subprocess without Provider — must pass
 10. test_emit_terraform_is_idempotent  (FR-7)
       emit_terraform twice → byte-identical output
 11. test_secret_value_never_leaks_to_terraform
       rc.yml refs a secret; grep emitted HCL for the value → must not appear
 12. test_public_service_receives_traffic          (skip on FakeProvider)
 13. test_persistent_volume_survives_redeploy      (skip on FakeProvider)
 14. test_service_to_service_networking_works      (skip on FakeProvider)

==============================================================
FIXTURES
==============================================================

tests/conftest.py
  - tmp_working_dir, sample_compose_factory, sample_rc_v2_factory,
    deploy_context_factory, recording_terraform_runner

tests/factories.py  (factory-boy)
  - RcConfigFactory, ServiceConfigFactory, SecretRefFactory, DeployContextFactory

tests/compose_samples/
  - minimal_3_service.yml          (web + postgres + redis)
  - with_volumes.yml
  - with_secrets.yml
  - mixed_launch_types.yml         (ECS Fargate + EC2 in same compose)
  - mixed_public_private.yml

==============================================================
COVERAGE TARGET  (NFR-1 gate)
==============================================================

- pytest-cov
- Tier 1 + Tier 2 (FakeProvider) combined: ≥80% of remote_compose/
- Tier 3 optional for coverage; its role is integration truth

==============================================================
CI MATRIX  (proposed)
==============================================================

job                         trigger                 tier  duration target
unit-and-contract-fake      every push              1+2   <2min
provider-integration-ecs    PR merge + nightly      3     <10min    (LocalStack)
provider-integration-k8s    PR merge + nightly      3     <10min    (kind)
e2e-smoke                   nightly + pre-release   4     <30min    (real clouds)

==============================================================
KNOWN RISKS
==============================================================

R1 — LocalStack community tier may not support all terraform aws_* operations
     needed for ECS (e.g. Fargate ENI provisioning, Service Connect fully).
     Mitigation: `terraform validate` + real-AWS E2E covers the gap; document
     per-resource support matrix in Phase 6b.

R2 — kind cluster spin-up time dominates Tier 3 k8s runtime.
     Mitigation: session-scoped kind fixture, reused across tests in a run.

R3 — Contract tests that exercise networking (tests 12–14) cannot run on
     FakeProvider. Must be skipped, not marked xfail — keep the skip reason
     explicit so future provider authors know what FakeProvider deliberately

title: Phase 2: System requirements — Provider interface, rc.yml v2 schema, terraform backend
description: Translate Phase 1 requirements into concrete system-level contracts: (a) the Provider interface that ECS/k8s/future providers implement, (b) the rc.yml v2 schema (breaking change — tool ships rc migrate), (c) the terraform backend strategy (local vs S3 vs GCS — per-project choice), (d) the module directory layout that ensures cloud SDKs stay optional extras, (e) the migration path for the existing imperative services.
acceptance_criteria: Provider interface is defined with method signatures and contract semantics. rc.yml v2 schema is written out with every field documented. Terraform backend selection is specified. Directory layout decision is recorded. Migration plan from existing imperative services is captured.
notes:
PHASE 2 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

==============================================================
1. PROVIDER INTERFACE CONTRACT (Python ABC)
==============================================================

Module: remote_compose/provider/base.py

class Provider(ABC):
    name: str                                    # identifier ("ecs", "k8s", "fake")

    @abstractmethod
    def emit_terraform(self, ctx, out_dir) -> Path
        """FR-7: write standalone terraform module. Does not apply."""

    @abstractmethod
    def plan(self, ctx) -> PlanResult
        """terraform plan + structured diff"""

    @abstractmethod
    def deploy(self, ctx) -> DeployResult
        """idempotent apply: emit tf → terraform apply → build/push images → update services"""

    @abstractmethod
    def redeploy(self, ctx, services=None) -> DeployResult
        """force new revision without config change"""

    @abstractmethod
    def status(self, ctx) -> StatusReport

    @abstractmethod
    def logs(self, ctx, service, follow=False, tail=100) -> Iterator[str]

    @abstractmethod
    def exec(self, ctx, service, command, interactive=False) -> ExecResult

    @abstractmethod
    def rollback(self, ctx, to_revision=None) -> DeployResult

    @abstractmethod
    def destroy(self, ctx) -> None

Supporting dataclasses (remote_compose/provider/base.py):
  DeployContext  — project, compose, rc_yml_v2, provider_config, tf_backend_config, working_dir
  ServiceStatus  — name, desired, running, health, last_event
  DeployResult   — revision_id, services, duration, warnings, terraform_outputs
  PlanResult     — create/update/destroy counts, raw plan text
  StatusReport   — list[ServiceStatus], cluster_health, ingress_url
  ExecResult     — exit_code, stdout, stderr

Contract semantics (enforced by shared contract test suite):
  - All methods idempotent
  - State lives in terraform backend; Provider methods are stateless between invocations
  - emit_terraform output must be apply-able without the Provider (FR-7 gate)
  - build/push images is a separate ImageBuilder concern invoked by deploy()
  - Each method returns within a bounded time or raises ProviderTimeoutError

==============================================================
2. rc.yml v2 SCHEMA
==============================================================

version: 2
project: <name>
compose_file: docker-compose.yml     # or list for overlays

provider: ecs                         # ecs | k8s

provider_config:
  ecs:
    region: us-west-2
    cluster: <name>
    aws_profile: default
    default_launch_type: FARGATE      # FARGATE | EC2
    vpc_cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    domain: api.example.com
    ec2_capacity:                     # used if any service: launch_type=EC2
      instance_type: null             # null → auto-size from summed CPU/mem
      min: 1
      max: 5
      desired: 1
      capacity_type: ON_DEMAND        # ON_DEMAND | SPOT | MIXED
      spot_weight: 3                  # for MIXED
  k8s:
    kubeconfig: ~/.kube/config
    context: <ctx>
    namespace: <ns>
    ingress_class: nginx
    storage_class: gp2

terraform:
  output_dir: ./terraform/${provider}
  backend:
    type: s3                          # s3 | gcs | azurerm | local | remote
    bucket: <name>
    key: ${project}/${provider}.tfstate
    region: us-west-2
    dynamodb_table: tf-locks          # for s3 backend locking

services:
  <svc>:
    cpu: 1024
    memory: 4096
    replicas: 2
    type: application                 # application | worker | infrastructure | proxy
    launch_type: FARGATE              # optional override (ECS only)
    health_check_path: /api/health/
    public: true
    port: 8000
    ephemeral_storage: 40
    volumes:
      - name: <vol>
        mount: /path
        size: 100Gi

secrets:
  - name: <key>
    source: file                      # file | aws_sm | k8s_secret | gcp_sm
    path: .envs/.production/.django   # for source: file
    arn: null                         # for source: aws_sm
    ref: null                         # for source: k8s_secret / gcp_sm

backup:
  bucket: <name>
  service: <svc>

domain: api.example.com
tls:
  mode: acm                           # acm | cert-manager | manual
  certificate_arn: null

v1 → v2 migration (table)
  cluster                → provider_config.ecs.cluster
  region                 → provider_config.ecs.region
  aws_profile            → provider_config.ecs.aws_profile
  compose_file           → compose_file (unchanged)
  project_name           → project
  vpc_cidr               → provider_config.ecs.vpc_cidr
  domain                 → domain + provider_config.ecs.domain
  secrets: [path, ...]   → secrets: [{name, source: file, path}, ...]
  backup                 → backup (unchanged)
  services.*             → services.* (cpu/memory/type/public/port/health_check_path/
                                        ephemeral_storage/default_target unchanged)
  implicit               → provider: ecs

==============================================================
3. TERRAFORM BACKEND STRATEGY
==============================================================

- User selects backend in rc.yml terraform.backend
- rc emits a backend.tf block with the chosen config; does not wrap or reimplement
- State reads go through `terraform output -json` (NFR-6 stateless CLI)
- Locking is backend-native (DynamoDB for s3, GCS object lock, etc.)
- Supported day 1: s3, local. Day 2: gcs, azurerm, remote.
- rc validates backend block but never reads raw state

5. DEPRECATION PLAN FOR IMPERATIVE SERVICES
==============================================================

KEEP (utility / cross-cutting):
  aws_client_factory, credential_service, audit_service,
  rate_limiter, log_sanitizer, context_service, health_service,

6. TERRAFORM INVOCATION
==============================================================

title: Phase 1: Functional + non-functional requirements
description: Capture the full requirements set for the portable deployer as the first TDD gate. Covers inputs (standard docker-compose.yml + optional rc.yml v2), operations (deploy, redeploy, logs, exec, status, rollback, destroy), supported cloud features (secrets, persistent volumes, public ingress, service-to-service networking), and non-functional constraints (testable without cloud creds, idempotent, cloud SDKs as optional extras, compose as sole required input).
acceptance_criteria: Requirements list is complete enough that Phase 2 (system reqs) can start without ambiguity. Each requirement is individually testable or labelled non-testable with justification.
notes:
FINAL REQUIREMENTS — Phase 1

## Functional Requirements

FR-1 Input
- Accept any valid docker-compose.yml (v3+) unmodified as primary input
- Optional rc.yml v2 for deploy-time tuning
- Compose file is authoritative for services, images, ports, volumes, depends_on, env

FR-2 CLI Operations
- rc deploy — idempotent apply
- rc redeploy — force rollout without config change
- rc plan — preview (terraform plan)
- rc status — per-service state table
- rc logs <svc> — stream/tail container logs
- rc exec <svc> <cmd> — run command in live container
- rc rollback — revert to previous applied terraform state
- rc destroy — full teardown of what we created
- rc migrate — rc.yml v1 → v2

FR-3 Providers (v1)
- AWS ECS — both Fargate and EC2 launch types
- Kubernetes — any kubeconfig-reachable cluster; kind for local/CI
- Adding a third provider = implement Provider interface + ship terraform templates; no core changes

FR-3a ECS/EC2 specifics
- Managed capacity provider backed by Auto Scaling Group (Launch Template, instance type, min/max/desired)
- Task definitions emit correct requiresCompatibilities per launch type
- awsvpc as default network mode (required for Service Connect); bridge/host as escape hatches
- Mixed mode allowed: some services Fargate, some EC2, same cluster
- EFS volumes for persistence (works on both launch types)
- Fargate is default launch type; EC2 opt-in per service via rc.yml
- Instance type in rc.yml is optional — if absent, rc auto-sizes from summed service CPU/memory
- Both Spot and On-Demand supported for EC2 capacity; user-selectable in rc.yml

FR-4 Cloud feature parity across providers
- Secrets: env-var injection sourced from provider secret store (AWS Secrets Manager / k8s Secrets / ExternalSecrets)
- Persistent volumes: compose named volumes → provider-native persistent storage (EFS / PVC)
- Public ingress: at least one HTTP service exposed via provider LB (ALB / Ingress)
- Service-to-service networking: by compose service name (Service Connect / k8s DNS)
- Health checks: per-service health endpoint drives provider readiness/liveness

FR-5 Image build & push
- Build from compose build: contexts
- Push to provider-appropriate registry (ECR / GCR / any OCI)
- Support pre-built image references (skip build)

FR-6 rc.yml v2 surface
- provider — which provider to use
- provider_config — provider-specific tuning (region, cluster, launch type, capacity, etc.)
- Per-service: resources (cpu/mem/replicas), type hint (app/worker/infra/proxy), health path, public/port, launch_type override (ECS)
- secrets — references, not values
- backup — S3/GCS bucket for DB dumps
- domain / tls — public hostname config

FR-7 Terraform portability (first-class)
- Emitted terraform module is self-contained and runnable standalone (terraform init && terraform apply) without rc installed
- Output at user-visible path (default ./terraform/<provider>/, configurable), not hidden under .rc/
- Follows HashiCorp conventions: main.tf / variables.tf / outputs.tf / auto-generated README.md
- Version-controllable: users can commit the generated module and manage infra with vanilla terraform thereafter
- rc never requires state or metadata that is not inside the terraform module itself

## Non-Functional Requirements

NFR-1 Testable without cloud — ≥80% of test suite runs with zero cloud creds (FakeProvider + moto + kind)
NFR-2 Idempotent — re-running deploy with unchanged config is a no-op; partial failures reconcile, not duplicate
NFR-3 Optional cloud SDKs — core has no boto3/kubernetes/google-cloud deps; providers ship as extras (pip install remote-compose[ecs], [k8s])
NFR-4 Compose-first — rc.yml optional; sensible defaults if absent
NFR-5 Observable — step-by-step progress, actionable errors; preserve current 15-step UX quality
NFR-6 Stateless CLI — terraform backend owns state; any machine with creds + backend access can operate; rc is a generator + convenience wrapper, not a lock-in
NFR-7 Reversible — destroy fully removes what deploy created; rollback uses terraform state history
NFR-8 Performance — code-only redeploy on equivalent stack completes in ≤2× current 630s

## Non-Goals

NG-1 Not a general orchestrator — no custom helm/kustomize/argo; use them via terraform when useful
NG-2 Not a CI/CD tool — rc deploy is the action; CI wiring is user's problem
NG-3 Not a secrets manager — we reference provider secrets, don't store or rotate
NG-4 No proprietary compose extensions — no x-rc-* keys in compose; tuning lives in rc.yml
NG-5 No live cross-provider migration — moving ECS→k8s is destroy+deploy with user-driven data migration

## Locked decisions

- Launch type default: Fargate, EC2 opt-in per service
- Instance type for EC2: user-specified in rc.yml, else auto-sized from summed CPU/memory
- Spot + On-Demand: both supported, user-selectable
- rc.yml: breaking v2 schema with rc migrate tool for v1→v2
- Terraform backend: user chooses (local/S3/GCS/etc.) — rc does not reinvent state
close_reason: Requirements locked: FR-1 through FR-7, NFR-1 through NFR-8, NG-1 through NG-5. Launch type, instance sizing, and Spot/On-Demand decisions recorded.

title: Portable multi-cloud compose deployer (terraform-backed)
description: Deploy unmodified docker-compose.yml to multiple clouds using terraform as the plan/apply/state layer. Providers v1: AWS ECS (port existing imperative code) + Kubernetes (universal portability target, locally testable via kind). Break rc.yml schema to simplify; ship rc migrate tool for v1 to v2. Approach: strict TDD — requirements → system reqs → test design → test writing → architecture → implementation → iterate. Branch: portable-deploy.
design: Terraform is the apply/state layer. Provider interface abstracts ECS, k8s, future GCP/Azure. FakeProvider enables cloudless contract tests. Imperative boto3 services are deprecated incrementally behind the Provider interface, not rewritten in one pass.

title: provision_vpc doesn't repopulate subnets when finding existing VPC
description: vpc_service.py:89-100 finds existing VPC by tag but only populates vpc_id and vpc_cidr in defaults. Doesn't discover subnets, gateways, route tables. If DB record deleted but VPC exists in AWS, returned model has empty subnet lists, breaking ALB creation. Fix: discover and populate full infrastructure when finding existing VPC.
close_reason: provision_vpc now calls _discover_vpc_resources to repopulate subnet_ids, igw, nat_gw, route_table_ids when finding an existing managed VPC. Defaults pass into get_or_create + backfill existing records. Subnet classification by Name tag with MapPublicIpOnLaunch fallback. 4 unit tests cover discovery happy path + partial-AWS failure modes.

title: Exception error codes documented but never assigned
description: CLAUDE.md and exceptions.py document error code ranges (1000-1999 validation, 2000-2999 SSH, etc) but no exception class assigns default code. The code parameter is optional in base class, all exceptions have code=None. Error code system is unused infrastructure. Fix: assign default codes in each class or remove code ranges from docs.
close_reason: Each exception class now declares a default code in its documented range; base class __init__ falls back to class attribute when code= isn't passed. Module docstring enumerates all ranges. 42 parametrized tests verify range membership + uniqueness + instance fallback behavior.

title: IAM policy failure treated as success — deployment continues without secrets access
description: infrastructure.py:311-315 returns StepResult.ok() when IAM policy update fails. Pipeline continues, creates services with secret references, services crash at startup because execution role can't read secrets. Fix: return StepResult.fail() when secrets configured but IAM policy can't be applied.
close_reason: SetupIAMRolesStep returns StepResult.fail() when secrets are configured AND iam.put_role_policy raises. Pipeline aborts before creating services that would crash on missing secrets-access. Error message names the role + underlying exception. 5 unit tests cover happy paths + failure paths.

title: compose_converter.py (1147 lines) and compose_preprocessor.py (1022 lines) need splitting
description: compose_converter.py handles YAML parsing, container conversion, resource calc, port mapping, env conversion, secret conversion, volume conversion (3 types), health checks, duration parsing, Fargate validation, task def construction. compose_preprocessor.py handles preprocessing, env_file parsing, build detection, volume classification, AND topological sorting. Fix: extract volume_converter.py, compose_field_converters.py, deployment_order_resolver.py

Fix: deprecate deploy() and route through deploy_with_pipeline(), or remove entirely. File: ecs_deployment_service.py (933 lines)

title: ConnectionError shadows Python builtin

title: _convert_command uses str.split() instead of shlex.split()
description: compose_converter.py:812-818 splits command strings on whitespace, breaking quoted args. 'sh -c "echo hello"' becomes ['sh', '-c', '"echo', 'hello"']. Docker compose handles this correctly. Fix: use shlex.split(command).

title: Duplicate _convert_service and _convert_preprocessed_service (~90% identical)

title: context.py: 500 lines of boilerplate properties + 60-param __init__
description: 290 lines of mechanical property getter/setter pairs delegating to sub-contexts. __init__ accepts 60+ parameters for backward compat. title: EFS _find_file_system_by_name has N+1 API calls and uses deprecated API
description: efs_service.py:241-251 iterates every EFS file system in account, making separate describe_tags call for each. describe_tags is deprecated (replaced by list_tags_for_resource). Tags already included in describe_file_systems response. Fix: read tags from fs.get('Tags', []) directly, remove describe_tags call.

title: Infinite recursion risk in race condition handlers
description: efs_service.py:1125, security_group_service.py:199, secrets_service.py:135 handle Duplicate errors by recursively calling themselves. If find-existing path consistently fails (permissions, etc), these recurse until stack overflow. Fix: use loop with max-retry count instead of recursion. Files: efs_service.py, security_group_service.py, secrets_service.py
close_reason: All three handlers (efs_service.get_or_create_efs_security_group, security_group_service._create_or_get_sg, secrets_service.get_or_create_secret) now use bounded for-loops with _MAX_DUPLICATE_RETRIES=3. No more recursive self-calls. Failed retries raise clear 'kept racing without converging' error. 3 new unit tests + 233 services regression suite green.

title: ECS/ECR/EFS services bypass AWSClientFactory

title: Teardown logic embedded in CLI/mgmt cmd — extract to service layer

Both delete ALBs, listeners, namespaces, SGs, VPCs, secrets. title: API viewset actions leak internal errors and have no pagination

title: ForceDeleteWithoutRecovery on secrets with no double-confirmation

title: Bare except:pass pervasive throughout codebase

title: rc deploy: fold task-def reconciliation into one waited roll (CI gates on the health-check roll)
description:
On a --no-state stack (terraform bypassed), rc's force-roll sets deploymentConfiguration + waits for steady state, but the task-def SHAPE (secrets + container health_check) is applied out-of-band by the stack's reconcile script AFTER rc returns. reconcile's update-service triggers a SECOND roll that rc does NOT wait on — so CI goes green a few minutes before the health-check-bearing roll actually converges. It's self-correcting (deployment circuit breaker auto-rolls-back a bad health-check roll, verified in prod on debuggai-api), and we verified convergence manually, but CI should gate on it.

Root: rc can't own task-def shape on a --no-state stack because terraform is bypassed; the reconcile script owns it. Clean fixes (pick one):
1. rc's --no-state deploy registers the task-def revision itself from rc.yml (secrets[] + health_check) so there's ONE roll rc waits on (subsumes the external reconcile script). Biggest, most general.
2. Adopt the stack into terraform (sentinal-8gnn) so task defs (incl. healthCheck via services.tf.j2) flow through the normal waited rc deploy — then the reconcile glue + RC_REF-only health-check application drop entirely.
3. Smaller: have the external reconcile call `rc`-style wait-for-stable after its update-service.

Discovered during the zero-downtime worker-roll work (remote-compose #10; debuggai-api #37/#38). Until then: the circuit breaker keeps prod safe and manual convergence checks confirm.

title: rc-prod: orchestration should use TASK ROLE, not django-backend-user (restore IAM boundary)
description: On rc, boto3 in sentinal tasks picks up AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID from env (bundle secret, wired by reconcile + mapped by entrypoint) -> all AWS calls run as IAM USER django-backend-user (static key in bundle), which was deliberately limited (S3FullAccess + ECRImageAccess push only, NO ecr:CreateRepository). Workflows failed 'Failed to create ECR repository'. STOPGAP 2026-05-31: granted django-backend-user AdministratorAccess+DenyIAM (broad, on a long-lived static key — not ideal). CLEAN FIX (matches Copilot which used the task role): make boto3 use the ECS TASK ROLE (debuggai-api-task, already has AdministratorAccess+DenyIAM) by NOT putting AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID in the env — entrypoint should map AWS_*->DJANGO_AWS_* (for django-storages S3 via the Django setting) then 'unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY' so the boto3 default chain falls through to the task role. Then revoke the admin grant on django-backend-user.

title: rc-a57 gap: adopt-VPC mode breaks short-name service discovery (no DHCP search domain)
description: In adopt mode rc skips aws_vpc_dhcp_options (correct — must not replace the shared VPC's DHCP). Consequence: the <project>.local namespace is NOT in the resolver search path, so intra-service SHORT names (redis://redis:6379, postgres, etc.) fail with 'Name or service not known' — services MUST use Cloud Map FQDNs (redis.<project>.local). Hit live on debuggai-api prod: celery couldn't reach redis until REDIS_HOST set to redis.debuggai-api.local. README documents the FQDN requirement, but rc should ALSO: (a) emit a deploy-time WARNING when adopt mode + any service env references a bare short name that looks like a sibling service, and/or (b) offer an opt-in provider_config.ecs.manage_dhcp_options=true (with a loud warning it REPLACES the VPC's DHCP set) for users who own the VPC. At minimum, a warning so this isn't discovered at runtime.
