title: rc up flap-loop diagnosis: when ECS service deployment circuit-breaks/cycles, rc should surface task stop reasons + suggest fixes
description:
OBSERVED: 2026-04-30 sentinal verification. Multiple deploy cycles where rc up returned 'Stack is up' (exit 0) within 200-300s, but actually django was in a flap loop — every task killed within 90s because:
  - cycle 1: /app was empty (Dockerfile missing COPY ./backend /app) → 'python: can\'t open /app/manage.py'
  - cycle 2: uvicorn --reload caused intermittent connection refused
  - cycle 3: ALB grace period 0s killed tasks before uvicorn finished booting

Each was a different root cause that took 5-10 min of manual log/event spelunking to diagnose.

FEATURE: After force-roll, rc could poll for ~60-120s checking:
  - service.deployments[?status=='PRIMARY'].rolloutState
  - service.events for 'unhealthy' / 'stopped task' / 'CannotPullContainerError' / 'ResourceInitializationError'
  - the most recent stoppedTask's stoppedReason via describe-tasks
  - exit code 1 / SIGTERM-on-startup
  - log lines matching 'No such file or directory' / 'ImportError' / 'OperationalError' / 'connection refused'

If rolloutState=IN_PROGRESS for >60s with task-stop events, surface the diagnosis:
  '⚠ django service is flapping. Recent task stop reason: <X>. Possible fix: <Y>.'

This is the rc-8zz post-rollout watcher, but expanded — currently it watches for IAM/ECR/SM placement errors. Extend to runtime errors visible in container logs and ALB health-check failures.

VERIFY: simulate one of the three cycles above and confirm rc surfaces the right suggestion within 60s.
close_reason: Shipped: extended _watch_post_rollout_errors to count 'Health checks failed' / 'is unhealthy in target-group' events per service. 3+ in the watch window triggers a separate 'flap loop detected' diagnostic with three common causes (grace period too short, app crashing on startup, wrong containerPort) + a copy-pasteable aws logs tail command. 2 new tests covering the flap detection and the false-positive guard for normal rolling deploys (1 unhealthy event = drain, not flap).

title: rc up cache-hit silent: 'Deploy complete' when buildx cache hits 100% but image is stale
description:
OBSERVED: 2026-04-30 sentinal verification. After 'rc fix bake-bind-mount-source django' modified the Dockerfile, ran 'rc up' which printed 'Deploy complete duration: 211s'. But the django image's /app was empty when inspected via 'docker pull' + 'ls /app'. Looking at image history: NO 'COPY ./backend /app' layer — buildx had cache-hit a stage that never had it.

Specifically the symptom was: rc-fix added new COPY lines, but buildx's cache-from registry layer cache was stale. buildx silently ignored the new instructions because the cache key matched.

ACTUALLY — re-reading: the issue was that rc fix bake-bind-mount-source had NOT run yet at the prior deploy, so the OLD image had no COPY, AND buildx detected no input changes that would invalidate cache for the upper stages, AND… hmm, this might actually be a buildx bug, not rc.

But rc could detect this: after build, inspect the resulting image's layer history and confirm key COPY directives from the Dockerfile actually produced layers. If 'COPY ./backend /app' exists in the Dockerfile but no corresponding layer exists in the image, ERROR with: 'Buildx cache hit a stale layer; rebuild with --no-cache (or set RC_NO_CACHE=1).'

OR simpler: when rc fix * modifies a Dockerfile, automatically pass --no-cache to the next build. The fix changed the build inputs intentionally; cache invalidation is what the user expects.

SUGGEST: track 'last-modified' of Dockerfile paths, and if changed since last successful build, force --no-cache for that service.
close_reason: Shipped: defensive no-cache sentinel. Any rc fix subcommand (bake-bind-mount-source, django-tls, nginx-conf) drops .rc/no-cache-next-build via no_cache_state.mark_no_cache(). _build_and_push_images consumes the sentinel via consume_no_cache() and sets ImageBuildSpec.no_cache=True for every service. ImageBuilder honors no_cache by dropping cache_from + adding --no-cache flag. 9 new tests (no_cache_state + builder no_cache behavior). Sentinel auto-deletes after consume so subsequent builds use cache normally. 1665 unit/contract tests pass.

title: rc fix django-tls patch can be silently lost when source file changes between deploys
description:
OBSERVED: 2026-04-30 sentinal verification. Earlier in session ran 'rc fix django-tls' — patch landed in backend/config/settings/local.py with rc-j08 marker. Confirmed via image inspection. Then several rebuild cycles later, the patch was GONE from the disk file (likely git checkout/stash/pull cycle reset it). The next 'rc up' rebuilt without the patch and the deploy was fine on health but admin POST returned 403 again.

Re-running 'rc fix django-tls' restored it. Image rebuilt, validated end-to-end (HTTP 302).

FIX: when rc up is about to deploy a service that has a domain set (i.e. framework registry's domain_env auto-injection is going to put CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS / DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS into the env), rc should:
1. Detect that the framework is Django (already does this via FrameworkRegistry)
2. Look for the rc-j08 marker in the auto-detected settings module
3. If marker missing, emit a HARD WARNING: 'Service X is Django + has a domain set, but its settings module (path/to/local.py) does not contain the rc-j08 patch. /admin POST will return 403 even though CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS is injected. Run: rc fix django-tls'

Equivalent for Rails / Phoenix when those framework integrations land.

ALTERNATIVELY: make 'rc fix django-tls' write a shim file that re-checks/re-applies on every container start (idempotent at runtime, not build time). But that complicates the contract — the warning is the right move.

VERIFY: deploy a Django stack, manually 'git checkout backend/config/settings/local.py' to wipe the patch, run rc up — should fail loudly with the warning.
close_reason: Shipped: fix_django_tls.has_rc_j08_marker() helper + cli_v2 build_deploy_context drift check. When a Django service has svc.domain set (CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS injected by rc-32x), we now scan the auto-detected settings module for the rc-j08 marker. If absent, emit a stderr warning telling the user to run 'rc fix django-tls'. 9 new tests across 2 files. 1636 unit/contract tests pass.

title: rc should detect dev-mode commands (--reload, runserver, flask run --debug) and warn before deploy
description:
OBSERVED: 2026-04-30 sentinal verification. The deployed django container ran '/start' which exec'd 'uvicorn config.asgi:application --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002 --reload --reload-include …'. WatchFiles either flaked OR the supervisor briefly stopped accepting on 8002 during reloads. ALB saw connection refused/timeout, failed health checks, ECS killed every task. Stack flapped indefinitely.

This was the local-dev start script being shipped as-is to ECS (because rc reads compose's local.yml command field directly). rc has no awareness that '--reload' is dangerous in prod.

FIX in compose_warnings.py: detect_dev_mode_command() — given the ServiceSpec.command + entrypoint resolved at deploy time, scan for:
- 'uvicorn …--reload'
- 'gunicorn …--reload'
- 'manage.py runserver' (Django dev server, single-threaded)
- 'flask run …--debug'
- 'rails s …' without '-e production'
- 'next dev' (Next.js dev mode)
- 'npm run dev' / 'yarn dev'
- 'webpack-dev-server'

If detected, emit a warning during pre-flight: 'Service X command appears to be a dev-mode runner (--reload). This is unstable for ECS deploys (file-watcher flakes, slow restarts). Consider gating with an env var (e.g. UVICORN_RELOAD=0) or using a prod start script.'

Don't BLOCK — just warn loudly. Some users may genuinely want this for ephemeral dev stacks.

VERIFY: when this warning fires for sentinal's /start script, the user knows to set UVICORN_RELOAD=0 or override command.
close_reason: Shipped: detect_dev_mode_command in compose_warnings.py catches uvicorn --reload, gunicorn --reload, manage.py runserver, flask run --debug, npm run dev, yarn dev, next dev, webpack-dev-server, rails s without -e production. Wired into collect_compose_warnings so it surfaces during rc plan / rc up. 13 new tests. Caveat: only sees compose 'command:' directly; Dockerfile CMD-baked dev runners need image-side detection (followup).

title: rc fix bake-bind-mount-source can produce builds that fail when COPY targets are .dockerignored
description:
OBSERVED: 2026-04-30 sentinal verification. Ran 'rc fix bake-bind-mount-source django' which appended:
  COPY ./backend /app
  COPY ./test-fixtures /app/test-fixtures
  COPY ./scripts /app/scripts

Then 'rc up' failed with:
  ERROR: failed to compute cache key: failed to calculate checksum of ref … '/test-fixtures': not found

Root cause: my .dockerignore had 'test-fixtures' as an excluded top-level dir (a fix I'd made earlier to trim a 10GB build context). The fix ran successfully — but the resulting Dockerfile is structurally broken because Docker can't satisfy the COPY when its source is dockerignored.

FIX: rc fix bake-bind-mount-source should:
1. Read .dockerignore in the project_dir
2. For each COPY <host> <container> line it's about to add, check whether <host> matches a dockerignore pattern
3. If yes, either:
   a) Skip that COPY line (and tell the user the fix dropped it)
   b) Refuse to run and tell the user to remove the dockerignore entry first

OPTION (a) is friendlier; (b) is more rigorous. Pick (a), with a clear warning.

ALTERNATIVELY: rc up's pre-flight (rc-2v8 build context check) could parse the Dockerfile and validate every COPY source resolves under the build context after dockerignore is applied — would catch this AND any hand-written Dockerfile with the same bug.
close_reason: Shipped: fix_bake_bind now reads .dockerignore, skips COPY entries whose host source is excluded, surfaces them as result.skipped_dockerignored, and CLI prints a warning + 'remove dockerignore entry' hint. 4 new tests covering single-skip, prefix-match (parent OK when child ignored), no-dockerignore back-compat, and all-skipped path. 1626 unit/contract tests pass.

title: [FEATURE] rc fix django-tls — patch settings.py to consume CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS env var
description:
rc-32x already injects CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS / DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS into the django container env. But Django settings.py has to actually READ those env vars for them to take effect. Most Django apps' local.py (or production.py) hardcodes these settings rather than reading from env. The result: rc auto-injects, Django ignores, admin login still 403s 'Origin checking failed'.

Workaround used twice now (sentinal session 2026-04-29 + 2026-04-30): live-patch /app/config/settings/local.py inside the running container with:

  import os as _rc_os
  _rc_csrf = _rc_os.environ.get('CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS', '').strip()
  if _rc_csrf:
      CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = [o.strip() for o in _rc_csrf.split(',') if o.strip()]
  SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER = ('HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO', 'https')

uvicorn --reload picks it up. But the patch evaporates on next image rebuild.

PROPER FIX: new 'rc fix django-tls' subcommand that:
  1. Detects the active settings module (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE or default)
  2. Appends an env-reading block at end of that file (idempotent — skip if already present)
  3. Mirrors rc fix nginx-conf / rc fix bake-bind-mount-source patterns

Acceptance: 'rc fix django-tls' on a Django repo + 'rc deploy' produces a stack where /admin/ POST login works first time without manual settings.py edit.

Filed as part of rc-2j8 epic but separable. Closes the Sprint 2 coverage gap (rc-32x ships the env var; this fix-cmd makes Django consume it).

title: [BUG] bd bootstrap creates project-ID mismatch between metadata.json and dolt server
description: Discovered during start-simpli-api session AND this session (sentinal). After bd bootstrap or some sequence of bd operations, .beads/metadata.json's project_id diverges from the dolt server's database project_id, causing bd commands to fail with 'PROJECT IDENTITY MISMATCH'. Workaround used: hand-edit metadata.json to match dolt's project_id. Real fix: bd bootstrap should be atomic — write metadata.json AFTER dolt confirms the database is created with the same project_id. Cross-project / external bug, but worth filing here so it's tracked as friction. Acceptance: bd bootstrap on a fresh repo never produces an identity mismatch; bd doctor --fix can heal an existing mismatch by realigning metadata.json to dolt's actual project_id.

title: [FEATURE] Plan-time check: rc.yml services.<svc>.health_check_path matches a real endpoint
description: Discovered during start-simpli-api redeploy: rc.yml had services.django.health_check_path=/api/health/ but the real endpoint is /api/v1/health/. ALB health-checks would 404, causing tasks to be marked unhealthy + drained. Heuristic-only — won't catch all cases but cheap and helpful. Acceptance: rc plan against a stack where health_check_path doesn't appear in any urls.py emits 'WARN: health_check_path /api/health/ not found in any urls.py — ALB health checks may fail. Real endpoints found: /api/v1/health/'.

title: [BUG] terraform target-group dependency race when adding service.domain to existing stack
description: [Sprint 3] Observed: rc up after adding services.django.domain to rc.yml failed with 'ResourceInUse: Target group rc-test-sentinal-core-tg is currently in use by a listener'. terraform's plan tries to delete the old default TG before detaching it from the listener — circular dep. Workaround: rc destroy + rc up fresh. Real fix: emit terraform with lifecycle.create_before_destroy on TG resources (or explicit depends_on hints) so listener moves to new TG before old TG deletion. Acceptance: rc up after adding domain to existing stack succeeds without rc destroy.

Lets terraform create the new TG before deleting the old one when service.domain is added/removed/changed, avoiding 'Target group is currently in use by a listener' on existing-stack updates. Golden fixture regenerated. Full suite: 1572 passed.

title: [FEATURE] rc plan + rc up emit step-name + elapsed every 30s for long phases
description: [Sprint 3] Observed: rc plan went silent for 5 min during warning-collector hang; rc up went silent for 9 min during terraform apply, 4 min during _build_and_push_images, 5 min during force-roll waits. Hard to tell stuck vs progressing. Wire a heartbeat: every 30s during any blocking step (terraform init/apply, image build, secrets push, force-roll wait, warning collection), emit '[step <name>] elapsed=Ns' via self._emit. ECSProvider already has self._emit; add a heartbeat thread per long-running call. Acceptance: rc up never goes silent for >30s; rc plan never silent for >30s either.
close_reason: Shipped: remote_compose/heartbeat.py — context manager that emits '... <label> still running (elapsed=Ns)' every interval seconds via a daemon thread. Honors RC_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S env var. Wired into TerraformRunner.init/plan/apply/destroy AND the wait_for_steady_state loop in run_auto_on_deploy_hooks_for_path. Tests: tests/unit/test_heartbeat.py (5 cases). Full suite: 1572 passed. Sentinal pattern (9-min silent terraform apply, 5-min silent steady-state wait) now emits progress every 30s by default.

title: [FEATURE] Pre-flight warning when docker build context exceeds 1GB
description: [Sprint 3] Observed: sentinal repo is 11GB; backend/ alone is 6.8GB (5.8GB of which was backend/backend/media). First django build hung 25+ min uploading context to buildkit before adding .dockerignore exclusions. rc plan / rc up should: compute build context size via du -sk on resolved build_context per service. If >1GB: print warning naming heaviest top-level dirs + suggest .dockerignore additions. If >5GB: error unless --force-large-context. Acceptance: rc plan against a 6GB+ backend prints 'WARN: build context for django is 6.8GB. Top dirs: backend/backend/media (5.8GB), backend/venv (1.0GB). Add to .dockerignore.'
close_reason: Shipped: detect_large_build_context in compose_warnings.py. Computes per-service build-context size at plan time via os.scandir + os.walk (capped per subtree). >1GB → WARN; >5GB → ERROR. Names the heaviest top-level dirs in the message + suggests .dockerignore. Tests in tests/unit/test_compose_warnings_large_context.py (6 cases). Sentinal repro: backend/ at 6.8GB would now warn at plan time naming media (5.8GB) + venv (1GB) + suggesting .dockerignore — saves the 25-min context upload hang.

title: [BUG] rc fix nginx-conf hardcodes resolver IP from rc.yml.vpc_cidr at generation time
description: [Sprint 2] Observed: rc fix nginx-conf was run when rc.yml had vpc_cidr=10.42.0.0/16; generated compose/ecs/nginx/nginx.conf has 'resolver 10.42.0.2'. Later when vpc_cidr changed to 10.43.0.0/16 (different region), nginx.conf was stale → tasks would 502 on Cloud Map FQDN resolution. Fix options: (a) re-run rc fix nginx-conf on rc.yml change automatically; (b) emit nginx.conf with a placeholder + env-var substitution at container start; (c) plan-time validator that warns when nginx.conf resolver doesn't match current vpc_cidr. Acceptance: changing vpc_cidr in rc.yml + rc deploy emits a warning if existing nginx.conf has a stale resolver.
close_reason: Shipped: detect_stale_nginx_resolver_ip in compose_warnings.py. Plan-time scan of nginx config files for 'resolver <IP>' directives; warns when the IP doesn't match the IP derived from rc.yml.provider_config.ecs.vpc_cidr (network_base + 2). Suggests re-running rc fix nginx-conf. Tests in tests/unit/test_compose_warnings_stale_resolver.py (5 cases). Sentinal repro: a vpc_cidr change from 10.42 to 10.43 would now warn on plan instead of silently 502-ing in production.

title: [FEATURE] rc fix bake-bind-mount-source — patch Dockerfile for ECS deploys
description: [Sprint 2] Observed: docker-compose.yml has 'volumes: ./backend:/app' bind mount; the local-dev Dockerfile relies on this and doesn't COPY ./backend itself. ECS has no bind mounts → /app is empty → manage.py missing. rc plan already detects + warns about this but the fix is manual (cost 30 min in sentinal). New rc fix bake-bind-mount-source <service>: parses compose volumes, finds host:container source-dir mappings, appends 'COPY <host_path> <container_path>' to the matching Dockerfile (with a comment explaining local bind mount overrides at runtime). Mirror rc fix nginx-conf pattern. Acceptance: rc fix bake-bind-mount-source django adds COPY ./backend /app to compose/local/django/Dockerfile and rc deploy succeeds.
close_reason: Shipped: new 'rc fix bake-bind-mount-source <service>' subcommand. Parses compose volumes, finds source bind mounts (relative host paths, skips named volumes / system mounts / data volumes), appends COPY <host> <container> to the matching Dockerfile. Local docker-compose still bind-mounts at runtime so hot-reload keeps working. Tests in tests/unit/test_fix_bake_bind.py (10 cases). Implementation: remote_compose/fix_bake_bind.py + cli_commands/fix.py. Sentinal-shaped repro now: 'rc fix bake-bind-mount-source django' → image has /app/manage.py → ECS deploy works.

title: [FEATURE] rc plan / pre-deploy detects POSTGRES_HOST=localhost / 127.0.0.1 in env_file
description: [Sprint 1] Observed: .test/.postgres had POSTGRES_HOST=localhost (correct for docker-compose, wrong for ECS — postgres is a separate task at 'postgres' Cloud Map FQDN). Tasks failed with 'connection refused on localhost:5434'. Plan-time check: any env_file value pointing at localhost / 127.0.0.1 / host.docker.internal whose KEY names another compose service. Warn 'env_file X has POSTGRES_HOST=localhost but compose declares service postgres — use a .rc/.dev/.postgres override with POSTGRES_HOST=postgres'. Acceptance: rc plan against the sentinal repro emits this warning.
close_reason: Fixed in compose_warnings.py: new detect_localhost_host_in_env_file detector + wired into collect_compose_warnings. Catches the sentinal pattern: env_file declares POSTGRES_HOST=localhost (or 127.0.0.1, host.docker.internal) when a compose service of that name exists. Suggests the correct Cloud Map service name. Tests in tests/unit/test_compose_warnings_localhost_env.py (7 cases).

title: build_deploy_context() service-construction loop is 90+ lines with nested branches; bail-on-first-error
description: cli_v2.py:471-585 builds service registry: outer loop over deploy_names, inner branching for rc.yml-vs-compose-only, nested volume + dev_volume loops, lifecycle merge calls. High cognitive complexity. A missing service name silently skips volumes; an env_file parse error is swallowed (lines 479-481). Fix: extract into ServiceResolver class with build_from_rc_yml() / build_from_compose_only() methods; separate VolumeResolver. Return result objects so errors are collected + reported together (not bail-on-first).

title: v2 schema parse errors lack file path + line number context
description: config/v2_schema.py: when parse_v2(raw) fails the error message likely lacks YAML line numbers. Users see 'schema validation failed' with no idea which rc.yml line is wrong. Fix: wrap schema validation; on failure, re-raise with enriched context (file path, YAML line via ruamel.yaml line tracking, field name, expected type). Add a 'did you mean?' suggestion for common typos (compose_file vs compose-file, etc.).

title: ServiceSpec.env / build_args / volumes are untyped dicts; render-time errors should be construction-time
description: ServiceSpec stores env: dict[str,str], build_args: dict[str,str], volumes: list[dict[str,str]] — untyped. Volume mounts require string keys 'name', 'mount', 'uid' etc.; typos silently fail at terraform-render time, far from where the bad value was set. RcConfigV2 next door is a typed dataclass. Fix: introduce dataclasses for VolumeMount (name, mount_path, uid, gid, mode), EnvVar, BuildArg with explicit fields + validation. Render-time errors become construction-time errors caught at the CLI boundary.

title: env_file_auto suppression set computed in cli_v2 but provider doesn't see it
description: cli_v2.py:441-443 calls _expand_env_file_auto() to build suppressed_env_keys (prevents env vars from the secret file landing in task-def environment[]). The provider's emit_terraform handles secrets independently. Two parallel logics → divergence risk. Fix: add suppressed_keys: set[str] to DeployContext, populate in build_deploy_context, consume in provider so both code paths agree on what's suppressed. Source: 2026-04-28 v2 audit.

title: Singleton-scheduler heuristic duplicated between cli_v2 and provider.py
description: cli_v2.py:469-523 imports + reapplies _looks_like_singleton_scheduler() from provider.py to auto-promote compose named-volume mounts to EFS. provider.emit_terraform() reapplies the same heuristic at provider.py:88-106. Same logic runs twice; bug fix needs edits in 2 places. Fix: move heuristic to provider/ecs/heuristics.py, import in both call sites. Mark compose-side auto-promotion in ServiceSpec so provider can skip re-checking. Source: 2026-04-28 v2 audit.

title: dispatch_if_v2() command-router conflates dispatch with command bodies
description: cli_v2.py:902-1040 — 140-line function routes to v2 if config is v2, then handles per-command logic inline (deploy: ttl + dev_mode + services_filter; destroy: destroy_args; status; plan: collect warnings). Each branch is 30+ lines. Adding a command requires editing this monolith. Fix: command registry pattern. COMMAND_HANDLERS = {'deploy': DispatchDeploy(), 'destroy': DispatchDestroy(), ...}; each handler owns argument validation + output. Dispatcher becomes: 'handler = COMMAND_HANDLERS.get(command); handler.dispatch(ctx, v2, kwargs) if handler else False'. Lets new commands ship without touching dispatch logic.

title: cli_v2.py is 1084 lines mixing 5 concerns; split into a package
description: cli_v2.py contains: (1) YAML parsing (load_rc_yml), (2) compose-file parsing + env expansion (_parse_compose_services, _expand_compose_vars), (3) ServiceSpec construction (build_deploy_context, ~115 lines), (4) provider dispatch (dispatch_if_v2, ~140 lines), (5) lifecycle hook polling (_run_auto_on_deploy_hooks). Concerns leak across each other; circular-import risk (cli_commands → cli_v2 → services). Hard to unit-test dispatch without spinning AWS clients. Fix: split into cli_v2/ package with parsing.py, context.py, dispatch.py, hooks.py. Move AWS-touching code (session_factory) into aws_integration.py so dispatch logic is testable with fakes.

title: Provider.deploy() does too much: 6 phases mashed into one 40-line method
description: provider/ecs/provider.py:611-649 — deploy() chains: (1) emit terraform, (2) init runner, (3) reconcile orphan logs, (4) apply terraform, (5) build/push images, (6) force new deployments. No abstraction layer separates phases; failure modes require digging through one method to figure out which phase blew up. Fix: extract each phase into named private methods (_emit, _apply, _push_images, _reconcile_and_deploy, _force_deployments). Return a progress object so callers can handle partial failures + report which phase succeeded/failed. Makes the orchestrator testable in isolation.

title: [bug] test_compose_import_e2e uses system python3 instead of sys.executable
description: tests/integration/test_compose_import_e2e.py:109 hardcodes 'python3' for subprocess.run, which fails on systems where the system python3 doesn't have project deps (e.g. click) installed. Should use sys.executable instead. Pre-existing — surfaced during rc-31f Phase 5.1 validation. Not v1_migrate-related.

The hard parts: (a) terraform-state-copy-before-apply guard — apply.py must cp -r the v1 stack's tfstate to a sandbox dir + run import + apply against the copy, only proceeding to the real state on user confirmation. (b) DB-integrity sandbox test — provision a real (small) postgres on the sandbox region, write canary rows pre-migration, verify post-migration. (c) Failure-injection paths — boto3 stubs that raise the right exceptions trigger the right user-facing error messages without leaving partial state behind. Wire any rc bugs surfaced during integration testing back as separate beads (don't fix in-line — log + move on, they'll show up in 5.1 / 6.1 phases).

title: rc db push --filter 'TABLE_NAME LIMIT N' for sub-section sampling
description: Discovered 2026-04-27 building sample DB for start-simpli. The user's ask was 'trim tables with over 1000 rows' — Django dumpdata path (build_sample_fixture command) handles that via ORM, but the simpler pg_dump→rc-db-push path dumps EVERYTHING (423 MB for the start-simpli local DB) regardless of size. Add: rc db dump-local --max-rows-per-table 1000 --keep-all-tables 'users,teams,...' that produces a smaller dump by inserting per-table 'COPY (SELECT ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT N) ...' clauses. Or wrap pg_dump's '--data-only --table' loop. Acceptance: rc db dump-local --max-rows-per-table 1000 produces a dump where psql output 'SELECT count(*) FROM <big-table>' returns ≤ 1000 after restore.

title: docker image rebuild doesn't invalidate Python pyc — runserver may serve stale code
description: Verified 2026-04-27 with start-simpli django: edited config/settings/local.py, ran rc deploy --services django (which rebuilt the image + force-rolled). Even after the new task was running, Django settings showed the OLD list values until I explicitly cleared __pycache__ inside the container and forced another restart. Hypothesis: the Docker layer cache replayed an existing layer that contained pre-compiled .pyc files alongside the .py — the .pyc bytecode got served instead of recompiling from the new .py. Fix options: (a) the Dockerfile should add a 'find /app -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +' step before EXPOSE; (b) start-simpli's /start entrypoint should clear pyc on boot; (c) image build pipeline should set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 in development images. Affects any framework where compiled bytecode lives next to source.

title: SM secret blob keys not in original env_file aren't pulled into task def
description: Verified 2026-04-27: I added DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS to the SM blob via aws secretsmanager put-secret-value, but the deployed django container's env had DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=empty. Reason: env_file_auto reads the env_file at deploy time and emits secrets[] entries in the task def for KEYS PRESENT IN THE FILE. Adding a key to the SM blob later doesn't retroactively add a secrets[] entry — the key is in SM but no task-def reference pulls it. Fix: rc could detect orphan SM keys (in SM blob but not referenced by any task def) and warn during rc deploy. Or: support a 'extra-env-from-sm' rc.yml block that lets users explicitly map SM keys to task-def env without needing the env_file. Workaround we used: also add the key to rc.yml services.<svc>.env (which goes to plaintext environment[]).

title: terraform init / docker push retry-on-transient-network in rc deploy
description: Verified 2026-04-27 mid-session: 'terraform init' twice failed with 'context deadline exceeded' to registry.terraform.io (retry was instant-success), and 'docker push' to ECR failed once with 'write: broken pipe' through the Docker Desktop HTTP proxy. Both transient. Currently rc raises immediately, user has to manually re-run. Fix: wrap runner.init() and pusher.push() in a bounded retry loop (3 attempts, exponential backoff 5s/15s/45s, only retry on connection-shaped errors — context deadline / broken pipe / connection reset / temporary DNS — never on auth / quota errors). Surface each retry as a one-line progress log.

title: orphan log-group reconcile: prefer terraform 1.5+ import {} blocks over CLI import
description: Current orphan-log-group reconcile (rc-e5u.46.9 + boto3-delete fallback) uses 'terraform import' CLI which validates the WHOLE module before importing. With --domain, the cert-validation for_each on managed-resource attributes triggers 'Invalid for_each argument' — import fails, fallback boto3 deletes the log group, apply recreates fresh. Works but discards the orphan's accumulated metric history. Modern terraform (1.5+) has 'import { id = ...; to = ... }' blocks evaluated DURING apply — they don't suffer the import-CLI's strict validation. Refactor: emit an import block in cluster.tf.j2 conditionally when boto3 detects the orphan. Apply absorbs it cleanly without delete-recreate, preserving history. Behind a flag so existing fallback path stays for terraform < 1.5.

title: provider.exec waits for execute-command-enabled task, not just any RUNNING task
description: Verified 2026-04-27: after a force-roll, two task sets briefly co-exist — old (DEREGISTERING, exec disabled) + new (RUNNING, exec enabled). provider.exec selects the first RUNNING task it finds; can land on the old one. Result: 'aws ecs execute-command failed because execute command was not enabled when the task was run'. Current poll loop (rc-e5u.46.6) waits for ExecuteCommandAgent in RUNNING state but seems to still pick stale tasks during fast force-roll cycles. Fix: also filter tasks by enableExecuteCommand=true via ecs.describe_tasks() return shape, AND prefer tasks whose taskDefinitionArn matches the SERVICE's CURRENT taskDefinition (latest revision). Add a unit test that mocks 2 RUNNING tasks (old has exec=false, new has exec=true) and asserts provider.exec picks the new one.

title: rc deploy should accept --domain late-binding to add a subdomain to an existing stack
description: Verified 2026-04-27: rc up --domain works on first deploy. But when a user wants to ADD a domain later (or change it), they have to either rc destroy + rc up --domain again, or hand-edit /tmp/rc.local.yml then rc deploy. Both are clunky. Add --domain / --alias / --route53-zone flags to rc deploy with the same behavior: pre-flight zone check, idempotent rc.yml patch via _patch_rc_yml_domain, then proceed with deploy. Acceptance: rc deploy --domain X on an already-deployed stack adds X to the ACM cert SANs + R53 records + listener-rule routing without rebuilding the stack.

title: rc up should detect Django settings module that hardcodes ALLOWED_HOSTS / CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS and warn
description: Verified 2026-04-27: start-simpli deploys with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.local, where local.py HARDCODES ALLOWED_HOSTS = [...] and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = [...] as Python literals. Setting env vars (via SM) is a no-op because the module never reads from os.environ. Fix needed in start-simpli was a 1-line patch to extend the lists from env. rc could detect this at deploy time: scan the active settings module for top-level lists named ALLOWED_HOSTS / CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, and if --domain is set + the module doesn't reference os.environ.get for those names, emit a warning during rc up. Lower-effort alternative: extend the framework registry's testing_defaults_marker_keys to include 'CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS_FROM_ENV' or similar sentinel; if absent, warn. Distinct from rc-32x — that's about INJECTION; this is about DETECTION.

title: build_sample_fixture loaddata vs Django post_save signals — IntegrityError on auto-created rows
description: Verified 2026-04-27 with start-simpli: the fixture lists a Team explicitly, but the Company that team references has a post_save signal that AUTO-CREATES a default Team. During loaddata, the Company inserts first, signal fires, default Team appears, then loaddata's explicit Team for the same (company_id, slug=default) hits the unique-constraint error. The fix has two angles: (a) extend build_sample_fixture's --exclude defaults to omit signal-managed models (Teams, Organizations, Companies created via post_save on User signup, etc.); OR (b) add a --disable-signals mode that wraps loaddata in signal_disconnect / reconnect using Django's signal API so the fixture wins. (b) is more general but invasive (signals encode REAL business logic — disabling them might leave half-set state). Acceptance: a Django app with post_save signals creating default rows can round-trip dumpdata→loaddata without IntegrityError.

title: rc db push exits 1 on benign pg_restore warnings
description: Verified 2026-04-27 pushing the start-simpli local dump (423 MB) into deployed postgres: pg_restore completes with 'errors ignored on restore: 4' (typical FK constraint / extension-already-installed warnings), but rc db push emits 'restore exited 1' and the surrounding command exits non-zero. Real-world: the data IS restored cleanly; the 4 'errors' are warnings pg_restore prints when it skips already-existing objects (e.g. PostgreSQL extension that the schema-only dump can't recreate). Fix: distinguish pg_restore's exit codes — exit 0 = clean, exit 1 with only constraint/extension warnings = restore succeeded with caveats (treat as success + emit summary), exit 1 with row-load failures = real error. Surface the 4 warning lines in the rc output so users can audit but don't fail on them.

title: rc lifecycle loaddata preset for Django framework registry
description: The framework preset (rc-e5u.47/.35.7) declares migrate, createsuperuser, shell, dbshell, collectstatic for Django. Missing: loaddata for fixture seeding. Add to remote_compose/frameworks.py DJANGO.lifecycle_hooks: 'loaddata': ('python', 'manage.py', 'loaddata', '${LOADDATA_FIXTURE_PATH:-fixtures/sample.json}'). Pair with rc-e5u.36 (rc db push). Useful for: rc lifecycle loaddata django after a fresh deploy to seed test data. Rails analog: 'seed': ('bundle', 'exec', 'rails', 'db:seed') is already there — the symmetry suggests Django should expose loaddata too.

title: rc deploy: lifecycle hooks defer until secrets+force-roll, matching rc up flow (rc-3q9 extension)
description: rc-3q9 fixed the issue for rc up by adding defer_lifecycle_hooks=True. But rc deploy (without --from-compose / not via rc up) still runs hooks during dispatch_if_v2 deploy step — before _auto_push_empty_secrets_if_any has finished and force-roll has converged. Verified 2026-04-27 with rc deploy on start-simpli: 'migrate on django... FAILED (exit 254)' fired because the hook hit a still-stale task. Fix: rc deploy command should also pass defer_lifecycle_hooks=True and call run_auto_on_deploy_hooks_for_path AFTER its own work completes. Same UX pattern as rc up. Acceptance: rc deploy on a fresh stack emits 'migrate on django... ok' instead of FAILED, with no manual rerun needed.

title: backup.bucket existing-S3-bucket should auto-import like orphan log-group
description: Verified 2026-04-27 trying to add backup.bucket to rc.yml after the deploy was up: terraform tries to create the bucket fresh, fails with BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou. Same shape as the orphan-log-group .46.9 case — AWS has the resource, terraform doesn't, apply blows up. Fix: provider should auto-import an existing bucket whose name matches backup.bucket (after verifying via boto3 head_bucket that we own it), OR fall back to a delete+recreate policy when the bucket is empty. Distinct from log-group case because S3 deletion is destructive (data loss) — auto-import is the only safe path here.

title: e5u.46.12 [bug] auto_on_deploy migrate hook runs before container has real secrets — exits 254
description: Verified during .46.6 e2e run #2 (2026-04-26): rc up against start-simpli emits 'FAILED (exit 254)' for the django.migrate auto_on_deploy hook. Root cause: the lifecycle hook runs DURING dispatch_if_v2 deploy step, AFTER _auto_push_empty_secrets_if_any but BEFORE rc up's outer _secrets_push_v2(rollout=True). On a fresh deploy, the django task is still running with placeholder secrets when the hook fires, so 'python manage.py migrate' fails with exit 254 (likely DB connection refused / wrong creds). Workaround: the start-simpli django container's /start script also runs migrations, so the eventual force-roll picks them up — but the FAILED message in 'rc up' output is misleading and sets up alarm fatigue. Fix: move _run_auto_on_deploy_hooks to AFTER the outer _secrets_push_v2 + force-roll completes (so tasks have real env), OR delay the hook with a wait-for-task-ready that includes a brief Postgres connectivity probe. Pair: lifecycle.migrate auto_on_deploy currently overlaps with start-simpli's container-side /start migrations — once .46.12 ships, the hook becomes the canonical migration path and /start should defer to it via a flag.
acceptance_criteria: rc up against start-simpli emits 'migrate on django... done.' instead of 'FAILED (exit 254)' on a fresh deploy. The hook's stdout shows 'No migrations to apply' (or fresh migrations applied) instead of a Postgres connection error.
close_reason: Hook deferral shipped: dispatch_if_v2 takes defer_lifecycle_hooks=True; rc up uses it + runs hooks via run_auto_on_deploy_hooks_for_path AFTER _secrets_push_v2. Helper polls ECS for deployment stability (single PRIMARY deployment + rolloutState=COMPLETED) before exec'ing, so hooks always land on the latest task def. 7 tests + 77 in adjacent suites green.

title: e5u.46.11: auto-provision compose named volumes when target service is stateful/singleton
description: Verified 2026-04-26 .46.6 run #7+: celery-beat fails to start with '_gdbm.error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: /celery-beat/celerybeat-schedule'. Compose declares 'volumes: - celery-beat-schedule:/celery-beat' (named external volume). On ECS, rc doesn't materialize compose named volumes (.44.7 detector warns about this). Without the directory, celery-beat (now correctly singleton-stateful per .46.10) still fails on startup. Stack reaches 5/6 green; celery-worker reports healthy via ALB so all CELERY tasks WOULD work — beat just can't schedule them. The fix: when a compose service has a named-volume mount + the service is stateful (volumes already wired) or singleton (.46.10) — auto-emit an EFS file system + access point + mount it at the declared compose path. Ephemeral by default (force_destroy=true) since these are typically scratch state for the scheduler. User can opt out via compose.exclude or by pre-declaring services.<svc>.volumes in rc.yml. Pair with .44.7 — that warning becomes 'consider auto-provisioning' once .46.11 ships.

title: e5u.44.22: env_file_auto secret name should preserve path context, not fall back to basename when env_file is outside compose dir
description: Verified 2026-04-26: cli_v2._auto_secret_name_for() falls back to env_file's basename when the path can't be made relative to the compose dir (i.e. env_file is OUTSIDE compose_path.parent).
