title: Expand e2e coverage: secrets, stateful EFS, rollback
description: Grow e2e beyond the single full-lifecycle test to cover the secrets workflow (mini-v2), stateful EFS (mini-v3), and rollback chains — the paths most likely to break silently in real AWS.

title: rc up uses rc.yml by default even when other rc.*.yml configs exist — should surface alternatives
description:
OBSERVED: 2026-04-30 sentinal had both rc.yml (us-west-2, stale) and rc.core.yml (us-west-1, the actual live config). I ran 'rc up' (no -c flag) — it picked rc.yml and started creating resources in us-west-2 against a non-existent VPC. Fast-failed in ~60s with 'VPC vpc-... has no internet gateway' but the user could lose tens of minutes if the stale config happens to point at a half-existing region.

FIX: when 'rc up' (or any rc command) runs without -c and finds multiple rc.*.yml files in the working dir:
- If exactly one has a matching terraform state dir under terraform/ECS-*/, that's the active one — emit info '(using rc.core.yml; other configs found: rc.yml)'.
- If multiple have state dirs, REFUSE to run and list them: 'Multiple rc configs found with active state. Specify with -c: [rc.yml, rc.core.yml]'.
- If none have state dirs, fall back to current behavior (rc.yml default).

ALTERNATIVELY: if rc.yml's project name and provider_config doesn't match what's actually deployed (probe AWS for cluster existence), tell the user.

LOWER URGENCY because the failure mode is loud (terraform errors out fast). But the false-start is ugly when iterating.
close_reason: Shipped: cli._warn_on_rc_yml_ambiguity scans cwd for rc.yml + rc.*.yml siblings and emits a stderr nudge listing them when 2+ exist and no -c flag was passed. Doesn't block — just makes the implicit choice visible. 5 new tests.

title: [FEATURE] rc psql / rc dbshell — managed psql against the deployed postgres
description: [Sprint 4] Observed: shelled into postgres via aws ecs execute-command + psql repeatedly to drop/recreate DB, debug queries. Output kept getting mangled by less paging (added -P pager=off manually). New rc psql wrapper: finds postgres task; execs in with PAGER=cat + psql -P pager=off; supports -c for one-liners + interactive mode. Mirrors rc exec but for the DB. Acceptance: rc psql -c 'select count(*) from django_migrations' returns clean text without pager artifacts.
close_reason: Shipped: rc db psql subcommand. Auto-discovers postgres task from rc.yml.cluster, reads POSTGRES_USER/DB/PORT from the running task def env, builds aws ecs execute-command with PAGER=cat + psql -P pager=off so output isn't mangled by less. Supports -c <SQL> for one-shot + interactive shell mode. Tests: tests/unit/test_db_psql.py (5 cases). Resolves the 'aws ecs execute-command + psql' boilerplate I had to remember manually during the sentinal debug session.

title: up.py compose_path_for_autofix silently None when rc.yml's compose_file is stale
description: cli_commands/up.py:141-149 reads rc_raw_existing.get('compose_file'), checks .exists(); if missing, compose_path_for_autofix stays None silently. The user gets no warning that rc up won't auto-generate the nginx config because the compose_file pointer is stale. Fix: emit a click.echo warning when the existing rc.yml's compose_file is missing — point at the bad path, suggest --from-compose to refresh.

title: network.tf.j2 hardcodes private-subnet offset cidrsubnet(...,count.index+10)
description: network.tf.j2:46 — private subnets allocated at offset +10 in cidrsubnet(). For tight VPC CIDRs (e.g. 10.0.0.0/18 = 64 subnets), the +10 offset is rigid. Fix: derive from VPC size (so a /18 doesn't blow up) or expose subnet_allocation_strategy in provider config. Document the existing collision-avoidance rationale.

title: frameworks.py: register_framework() exists but no path for users to register from rc.yml
description: frameworks.py:192 has register_framework() but it's never called from user code. Registry is module-level (DJANGO/RAILS/PHOENIX). Users wanting a FastAPI/Starlette/Express preset must PR the repo. Fix: support 'services.<svc>.framework: custom-fastapi' in rc.yml plus a project-local hook (e.g. rc.yml field framework_modules: [./my_frameworks.py]) that's loaded + registered at startup. Document in README.

title: Provider.status() does N+1 ECS API calls (describe_task_definition per service)
description: provider.py:1043-1058: for each service we call describe_task_definition() to detect stale revisions. 10-service stack = 11 API calls. Fix: list_task_definitions(familyPrefix=family) gives revision numbers in one call. Cache family_latest if status is called frequently. Affects rc status latency on larger stacks; not urgent at single-digit scale.

title: compose_warnings.py 640 LOC: 6 detectors + scattered helpers + duplicated _resolver_ip_for
description: compose_warnings.py has 6 independent detectors (bind_mounts, external_volumes, bad_hosts, multi_port_alb, nginx_upstream_resolver, django_allowed_hosts), each with its own scanning logic + shared helpers (_resolve_build_context, _looks_like_django_service, _resolver_ip_for). _resolver_ip_for is also duplicated in fix_nginx_conf.py. Scanning limits scattered (_MAX_FILES_PER_CONTEXT, _MAX_FILE_BYTES). Fix: ComposeScanner base class with scan(compose, compose_path) -> list[Warning]; each detector is a ScannerPlugin subclass. Consolidate scanning limits into ScanConfig dataclass. Move _resolver_ip_for to shared utils.

title: init_from_compose.py 900 LOC of heuristics ordered by call graph, not by concern
description: init_from_compose.py contains: service-type inference, CPU/memory defaults, public-service selection, framework detection, ALLOWED_HOSTS injection. Each heuristic is a pure function (testable) but the module's function ordering follows the call graph, not the concern. Touching CPU defaults requires 50+ lines of context. Fix: namespace into classes — class ServiceTypeInference, class ResourceSizing, class PublicServiceSelection. Each owns its concern + can be unit-tested in isolation. Document decision trees in docstrings.

title: Provider.exec()/exec_capture undocumented dependencies on SSM agent + role perms
description: provider/ecs/provider.py:1181-1445 — exec methods create ECS execute-command sessions via boto3 without documenting the prerequisites (task with ssm-agent enabled, task role with ecs:execute-command + ssm:StartSession). Failure surfaces as 'operation timed out' or generic access denied, no breadcrumb. Fix: docstring spelling out the requirements; catch common errors and suggest the missing perms in the error message.

title: Lifecycle hook polling timeout/interval only configurable via env vars (RC_HOOK_WAIT_*)
description: cli_v2.py:852-897 polls ECS deployments with RC_HOOK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S (default 300s) and RC_HOOK_WAIT_INTERVAL_S (default 10s) env vars. No CLI flag. Polling logic also duplicates describe_services + state-checking from provider.status(). Fix: --hook-timeout and --hook-poll-interval flags with env-var fallback. Extract polling into a shared ECSWaiter class in provider so status() reuses the same code path.

title: "rc-test-" project marker hardcoded in provider for terraform tagging
description: provider/ecs/provider.py:580 — 'is_rc_test': ctx.project.startswith('rc-test-') is configuration baked into code. Teams with different test-prefix conventions (e.g. -test suffix, _test_ infix) have no override. Fix: provider_config.ecs.test_project_pattern (regex), default '^rc-test-'. Pass to terraform as a variable.

title: capacity.tf.j2 hardcodes ASG target_capacity=80, scaling_step=10
description: capacity.tf.j2:137-139 hardcodes EC2 ASG managed scaling: target_capacity=80, maximum_scaling_step_size=10. No override path in rc.yml. A user wanting 50% utilization or single-instance scaling must edit terraform directly. Fix: add provider_config.ecs.ec2_capacity.{target_capacity,scaling_step_size} with defaults; thread through to template variables.

title: VPC CIDR default '10.0.0.0/16' duplicated across 3 modules
description: provider/ecs/provider.py:152, compose_warnings.py:382 (_VPC_CIDR_DEFAULT), fix_nginx_conf.py:45 — each defines '10.0.0.0/16' independently. Changing the default needs edits in 3 places. Fix: define VPC_CIDR_DEFAULT in a shared constants module (suggest remote_compose/config/defaults.py or top-level remote_compose/defaults.py) and import everywhere. Probably ~10-line PR.
close_reason: Created remote_compose/defaults.py with VPC_CIDR_DEFAULT='10.0.0.0/16'. Updated 5 v2 callsites to import it: provider/ecs/provider.py:152, compose_warnings.py:382, fix_nginx_conf.py:45, compose_import.py:96, cli_commands/fix.py:120. Left v1 paths (services/, management/, models/, migrations/) untouched — that's the deprecated path. Left init.py's example-rc.yml template literal since users edit the example by hand. 1485 unit+contract tests green.

title: ECRAuthenticator timeout + docker_bin not configurable; error mode brittle
description: provider/ecs/ecr_auth.py:20,44 — docker_bin defaults to 'docker' (PATH search), timeout=60 baked in. Errors on login failure surface stderr[:200] as exception message — brittle and the error UX is poor. Fix: accept docker_bin + login_timeout_s as init parameters; catch TimeoutExpired and CalledProcessError separately so we can give actionable hints ("docker login timed out — check credentials/network").

title: domain.tf.j2 hardcodes ttl=60 for cert validation; service_discovery.tf.j2 ttl=10
description: domain.tf.j2:45 hardcodes 'ttl = 60' on Route 53 cert validation records; service_discovery.tf.j2:32 hardcodes 'ttl = 10' for Cloud Map. No way to override. Fix: extract to template variables ttl_cert_validation + ttl_service_discovery; pass from provider config with defaults. Useful when validation latency is a concern or for teams with stricter DNS TTL policies.

title: rc auto-detect framework settings module that's not env-var-friendly
description: Generalisation of rc-21m (which is Django-specific). When deploying any framework via rc that has a 'local' / 'dev' settings module (config.settings.local, config/environments/development.exs, config/environments.test.rb, etc.), those modules typically hardcode dev-only values for hostnames / origins / debug flags. Deploying that module to a remote stack with rc up --domain leaves the deployed app rejecting the new domain. The framework registry (rc-e5u.47) already knows django/rails/phoenix; extend it with 'host_validation_settings_path' (e.g. config/settings/local.py for Django) so rc up --domain can run a quick scan + emit a warning if the file hardcodes hostnames + doesn't read from env.

title: rc up / rc deploy could warn when stack TTL is unset on a long-lived deploy
description: Verified through this session: deployed start-simpli without --ttl on initial pass; stack lived for 12+ hours burning AWS spend before being noticed and reaped. rc could detect long-running ephemeral-shaped stacks and warn: at rc status / rc list time, surface 'NOTE: stack <project> has been running 12h with no TTL — consider rc destroy or attach a TTL via rc up --ttl 4h'. Threshold could be configurable in ~/.config/remote-compose/policy.toml (default 6h). Distinct from rc reap (which only acts on TTL'd stacks). Acceptance: 'rc list' shows long-running untagged stacks with a 'consider tearing down' hint after the 6h mark.

title: big fixture files in git: warn / suggest .gitattributes for diff suppression
description: Verified 2026-04-27: backend/fixtures/sample.json from build_sample_fixture is 5+ MB JSON, generated. Each regen produces a >100k-line diff in git. Suggestions for the docs / scaffolder: (a) auto-add .gitattributes entry: 'fixtures/sample.json -diff -merge linguist-generated=true' so PR diffs collapse it; (b) consider git-lfs for repos that regenerate often; (c) build_sample_fixture's --output default could land outside the repo (e.g. /tmp/sample-<timestamp>.json) with a flag to opt into committing. None of these are the right default for everyone — surface the trade-off in the command's help text + ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: rc commands force PYTHONUNBUFFERED so tee/pipe captures progress in real time
description: Verified 2026-04-27 capturing rc up output via tee: rc was silent for ~10 minutes during terraform apply / docker push because Python block-buffers stdout (4 KiB chunks) when piped. Manifested as misleading 'is rc hung?' moments + Monitor command grep filters seeing nothing until the buffer flushed at end-of-step. Fix: in remote_compose/cli.py main entry (or .venv/bin/rc shebang), set PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 / sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True) so progress output appears as it's emitted. Also consider replacing print() calls with click.echo(...) which respects flushing.

title: copilot.8: addons CFN templates — detect, list, document not-yet-handled
description: copilot/<svc>/addons/*.yml define extra CFN resources (RDS instances, S3 buckets, DynamoDB, etc.). Out of scope for first cut. Detect their presence and emit a clear human-readable summary at the end of import: 'Found 3 addon templates; manual translation required: <list>'. Each addon type gets a stub bead the user can pick up (RDS → 'set up your own RDS, point DATABASE_URL at it'; S3 → 'use rc.yml backup.bucket OR add to terraform/'). Test asserts the summary is emitted with a fixture containing addons.
close_reason: Addons surfaced in IMPORT_SUMMARY.md with per-AWS-resource-type guidance (10 common types). CLI prints addon count. CFN-tolerant YAML loader handles !Ref/!Sub/etc. Sentinal corpus IAM addon test verifies end-to-end. 19 new tests + full copilot suite 123/123 green.

title: autoimport.5: P3 backlog — celerybrowser/eval-app/docs prod Dockerfiles + non-standard port mappings
description: celerybrowser exposes 7788/5901-5903/9222 (VNC + chrome remote debug); ECS task net mode SG rules need to handle these. eval-app + docs only have local Dockerfiles; need prod Dockerfile. These are sentinal-side changes, not portable-deploy provider changes. Document as a follow-up the sentinal team can pick up.
close_reason: P3 backlog — these are SENTINAL-side changes (Dockerfiles, port mappings) not rc provider changes. Tracked for the sentinal team, not blocking rc. The auto-import path itself doesn't need them: cli_v2.build_deploy_context honors compose.exclude/include cleanly.

title: multidomain.6: P3 backlog — celerybrowser, eval-app, docs production Dockerfiles
description: Followups not blocking the core multi-domain feature. (a) celerybrowser needs ports 7788/5901-5903/9222 — non-standard port mapping; investigate ECS task net mode SG rules. (b) eval-app: production-ready Dockerfile + decide what subdomain. (c) docs: only has compose/local/docs/Dockerfile target=dev; needs a prod Dockerfile build target.

title: Gap: _zone_from_domain's 2-label heuristic is wrong for nested subdomains
description: Provider's _zone_from_domain('migration-test.api.startsimpli.com') returns 'startsimpli.com' — assumes the R53 zone is always the apex. Real accounts often delegate subdomain zones (e.g. api.startsimpli.com), leaving the parent undelegated. The data.aws_route53_zone lookup then fails at apply. Fix (landed): provider_config.ecs.route53_zone explicit override bypasses the heuristic. Smarter future fix: list zones via boto3 at emit time and pick the longest-suffix match of the target domain.

title: Gap: all secrets attach to every service (no per-service scope)
description: Provider currently does 'for svc_view in services_view: svc_view[secrets] = secrets_view' so every service task def gets ALL secret entries — e.g. postgres container receives DJANGO_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD + SECRET_KEY + REDIS_URL etc. that it has no use for. Correctness is fine but wastes env-var slots (ECS caps 100/container) and leaks unnecessary values to workloads that shouldn't see them. Fix: allow rc.yml v2 secrets to optionally scope to a list of service names, defaulting to all if unspecified.

title: Gap: rc destroy leaves orphan container-insights log group
description: ECS auto-creates /aws/ecs/containerinsights/<cluster>/performance when Container Insights is enabled. Terraform doesn't manage it, so 'rc destroy' cleanly removes everything else but leaves this log group behind. Fix: either import/manage it as an aws_cloudwatch_log_group resource in cluster.tf.j2, or add a post-destroy cleanup hook. Found during Mini v0 cleanup verification.

title: Gap: aws_service_discovery_service.failure_threshold deprecation
description: terraform validate emits 7 deprecation warnings — 'failure_threshold = 1' is no longer supported by AWS and will be removed in a future terraform-aws-provider major version. Template: remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/service_discovery.tf.j2. Fix: drop the failure_threshold line from health_check_config {}. Non-blocking for Mini v0 but will break on provider major bump.

title: Phase 6b.16: Postgres-on-EFS access point uid mismatch
description: EFS access points enforce posix_user=1000:1000 (per our template). postgres:16-alpine container runs initdb which tries chown on the data directory; fails with 'Operation not permitted' because the container user (postgres, typically uid 999 or 70) can't change ownership on a 1000:1000 mount. Fix options: (a) parameterize access point posix_user per service via rc.yml; (b) drop access points for EFS and use raw mount with iam auth; (c) ship a postgres base image that matches uid 1000. For now demo works around by not using EFS for the db service; production guidance should recommend RDS for postgres instead of ECS-on-EFS.
acceptance_criteria: A demo or integration test deploys an ECS+EFS postgres service and initdb completes. Access point uid is either documented as parameterizable or replaced with a mount strategy that lets postgres chown.
close_reason: EFS volumes now support per-service uid/gid/mode on access points (default 1000/1000/0755). postgres:16-alpine uid=70 wired and verified. Separately landed 'stateful' detection: any service with EFS volumes gets deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0/maximum_percent=100 so the replacement task waits for the primary to stop before mounting — caught while Mini v3 smoke corrupted postgres data under rolling deploy. End-to-end proof: Mini v3 deploy → migrate → superuser → admin login 302 → force postgres restart → admin login 302 again with the same credentials persisted in EFS. 6 new tests, suite 537 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Phase 6b.6: Register 'ecs' provider and enroll in contract suite

  tests/contract/conftest.py
    - _provider_selected() default changed: returns ["fake"] by default
      (previously returned all registered, which would break in any env
      without real terraform + real AWS).
    - RC_CONTRACT_PROVIDERS=<csv|all> env var opts into real providers.
    - minimal_ctx fixture now asks for the `provider` param and picks
      per-provider minimal config from _PROVIDER_DEFAULT_CONFIG. Contract
      tests stay provider-agnostic; providers that need specific config
      (region, cluster) get sensible defaults injected here.

Verification
  pytest tests/contract/                            → 13 passed, 4 skipped
                                                       (FakeProvider only, unchanged)
  RC_CONTRACT_PROVIDERS=ecs pytest tests/contract/ \

          secret_value_never_leaks"
                                                     → 3 passed

                                                       (baseline unchanged)

Contract-gate status

  ⚠️ deploy/destroy/status/etc. contract tests need real terraform + AWS

Contract fixture now injects provider-specific minimal config. 3 emit-only contract tests pass against ECS in sandbox; lifecycle tests need real terraform (CI/laptop).

title: Phase 6b.5: ECS provider — custom domain + ACM + Route 53
description: When rc.yml v2 domain is set, provision ACM certificate (DNS-validated via Route 53), wire ALB 443 listener + redirect from 80, create A-record alias to ALB.
acceptance_criteria: api.example.com pointed at a Route 53 hosted zone + rc.yml domain: api.example.com → HTTPS endpoint serving valid certificate after deploy.

Templates

close_reason: Custom domain + ACM (DNS-validated) + Route 53 A-record. ALB gets 443 listener with TLS 1.3 security policy; 80 redirects to 443 when domain set. Manual TLS mode accepts pre-existing certificate_arn. 16 new tests pass; 440 total.

title: Phase 6b.4: ECS provider — secrets integration (file + aws_sm)
description: Route rc.yml v2 secrets through ECS task definitions without leaking values. File-source secrets materialize as aws_secretsmanager_secret + aws_secretsmanager_secret_version + task definition secrets[] block. aws_sm-source secrets reference existing ARNs.
acceptance_criteria: Secret values never appear in emitted HCL or in terraform state plaintext (verified by sentinel test); task definitions have correct secrets[] with valueFrom pointing at the right ARN.
notes:
PHASE 6b.4 DELIVERY — Secrets integration (file + aws_sm)

Contract
  source: file  — terraform creates an empty aws_secretsmanager_secret with
                  a placeholder secret_version. lifecycle.ignore_changes =
                  [secret_string] so subsequent applies don't overwrite the
                  real value uploaded by `rc secrets push` (legacy command,
                  unchanged). Secret ARN is referenced by task definitions
                  and the task execution IAM policy.
  source: aws_sm — no terraform resource created. Existing ARN is referenced
                   directly in task defs + IAM policy.
  source: k8s_secret / gcp_sm — silently skipped on the ECS provider. Other
                                 providers consume these.
  Unknown source → ProviderConfigError with the bad source name.

Env var naming
  Default: secret.name sanitized → uppercase (django → DJANGO,
           my-db-password → MY_DB_PASSWORD). Explicit override (env_name
           field) is a future extension.

Hard invariant
  Secret VALUES never appear in terraform HCL or terraform state. Enforced
  by contract-suite sentinel test plus a provider-level sentinel test
  (test_sentinel_never_appears_in_any_hcl).

New / updated files
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/secrets.tf.j2  — NEW, renders only
    when has_file_secrets. Placeholder + ignore_changes.
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/iam.tf.j2      — UPDATED, conditional
    task_execution_secrets policy listing every referenced secret ARN.
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/services.tf.j2 — UPDATED, conditional
    containerDefinitions.secrets[] with name + valueFrom per secret.
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/provider.py              — UPDATED, builds
    file_secrets / aws_sm_secrets / secrets_view / all_secret_arns context;
    _env_name_for_secret helper added.
  tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_secrets.py         — NEW, 16 tests.

Verification receipts
  pytest tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_secrets.py
    → 16 passed in 0.80s
  pytest tests/
    → 424 passed, 9 skipped in 7.48s  (baseline 408/9)
  ⚠️ Real AWS secret read-after-apply: still sandbox-blocked.
close_reason: Secrets integration done. file-source creates placeholder aws_secretsmanager_secret with ignore_changes lifecycle (value uploaded by rc secrets push). aws_sm-source references existing ARN. Task def containerDefinitions.secrets[] + IAM policy both wired. Sentinel confirms values never enter HCL. 16 new tests pass; 424 total.

title: Phase 6b.3: ECS provider — EFS persistent volumes
description: Extend ECSProvider with EFS volume support for compose named volumes with persistence requirements. Adds: aws_efs_file_system, aws_efs_mount_target, aws_efs_access_point per volume; task definition volumes+mountPoints wiring.
acceptance_criteria: with_volumes.yml fixture deploys, volume survives task replacement (verified via rc deploy + rc destroy sequence on real AWS).
notes:
PHASE 6b.3 DELIVERY — EFS persistent volumes

Templates
  efs.tf.j2    NEW  — renders ONLY when any service has volumes[].
                      Emits: EFS security group (2049 from tasks SG),
                      aws_efs_file_system per named volume (encrypted,
                      generalPurpose, bursting), aws_efs_mount_target per
                      (volume × private_subnet), aws_efs_access_point per
                      (service × volume) pair with POSIX uid/gid 1000 and
                      per-service root directory.
  services.tf.j2 UPDATED — task def adds volume{} and containerDefinitions
                      mountPoints[] blocks when service has mounts.
                      transit_encryption = ENABLED; access point enforces
                      root directory isolation.

Provider
  provider.py — parse ServiceSpec.volumes list; each entry {name, mount}
                is validated (both required) and produces (a) a deduped
                EFS file system entry, (b) a per-(service, volume) access
                point entry, (c) a per-service mount view attached to the
                service view for services.tf.j2 consumption.

Tests (tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_efs_volumes.py)  13 new
  - efs.tf empty when no volumes; services.tf has no volume block
  - Single volume: file_system + mount_target + access_point + SG shape
  - Task def wiring: volume block, mountPoints, transit_encryption,
    correct file_system/access_point IDs referenced
  - Shared volume: two services mount the same name → one file_system,

  - Multiple volumes per service: two named volumes in one task def
  - Validation: missing name or mount raises ProviderConfigError

Reality-check receipts
  python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_efs_volumes.py -v
    → 13 passed in 0.64s
  python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/
    → 79 passed in 1.90s  (66 prior + 13 new)
  python3 -m pytest tests/
    → 408 passed, 9 skipped in 6.91s  (baseline was 395/9)
  ⚠️ Real AWS: same constraint — sandbox SIGKILL blocks real terraform.

     rc-e5u.17 contract-suite enrollment + LocalStack/real AWS CI.
close_reason: EFS persistent volumes done. One aws_efs_file_system per named volume (deduped), mount_target per AZ, access_point per (service, volume) pair with POSIX user/group and per-service root directory, SG allowing 2049 from tasks SG. Task def volume+mountPoints wiring. 13 new unit tests pass; 408 total.

title: Phase 6b.2: ECS provider — EC2 launch type + ASG capacity provider
description: Extend ECSProvider with EC2 launch type support. Adds: aws_launch_template, aws_autoscaling_group, aws_ecs_capacity_provider, EC2-specific task definition compatibility, instance auto-sizing from summed CPU/memory when rc.yml instance_type is null, ON_DEMAND/SPOT/MIXED capacity selection.
acceptance_criteria: Mixed-mode compose (some services Fargate, some EC2) deploys successfully. Auto-sizing test passes (summed 6144 CPU + 12GB mem → t3.xlarge or similar).
notes:
PHASE 6b.2 DELIVERY — EC2 launch type + ASG capacity provider

New files
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/autosize.py
    Heuristic: pick smallest t3-family shape that fits the largest single
    EC2 task; size ASG min/desired/max by summed demand × 1.2 headroom.
    Custom ladders supported (users can pass m5/m6i/c7g shapes).

  remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/capacity.tf.j2
    Renders ONLY when at least one service has launch_type=EC2.
    Emits: SSM-latest ECS AMI lookup, EC2 instance IAM role + instance
    profile, EC2-instances security group, aws_launch_template with
    /etc/ecs/ecs.config user_data, aws_autoscaling_group (simple

Template updates

    MIXED on-demand-base-percentage.

New tests
  tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_autosize.py        12 tests
    Instance-choice ladder climb, summed-demand ASG sizing, custom ladder,
    ladder exhaustion raises.
  tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_ec2_launch.py      17 tests
    Fargate-only (capacity.tf empty, cluster excludes EC2 CP),
    EC2-only (capacity_provider_strategy, EC2 compat, cluster includes CP),
    Mixed-mode (both service shapes in same module, default_launch_type
    resolution, per-service override),
    Capacity type (ON_DEMAND simple LT, SPOT + MIXED mixed_instances_policy),
    Auto-sizing (explicit instance_type wins, auto-size when absent),
    Default-launch-type validation.

Verification receipts
  python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/
    → 66 passed in 1.89s  (was 37, added 29)
  python3 -m pytest tests/
    → 395 passed, 9 skipped in 10.58s  (baseline 366/9)

  End-to-end smoke: DeployContext with mixed services (web Fargate public,
  api Fargate, worker EC2 replicas=2), capacity_type=SPOT → emitted module:
    capacity.tf    3693 bytes   instance_type = "t3.medium"
                                desired_capacity = 3
                                mixed_instances_policy + capacity-optimized
    services.tf    4420 bytes   web/api: launch_type = "FARGATE"
                                worker:  capacity_provider_strategy with

Acceptance check (Phase 6b.2)
  ✓ Mixed-mode compose (Fargate + EC2 in same file) produces valid HCL

title: Phase 7: Iterate — deprecate imperative services, add third provider
description: Once ECS + k8s providers are stable and tested, deprecate the imperative boto3 services (aws_service, vpc_service, alb_service, security_group_service, ecs_deployment_service, etc.) by marking them as internal-only and removing their direct CLI entry points. description: Pattern 'os.path.normpath(service.build_info.context):service.build_info.dockerfile' computed in steps/build.py:30-45, steps/multi_service.py:117-133, and compose_converter.py:301-303. If format changes, all three must update. Fix: add get_build_key() method to BuildInfo dataclass.

title: AWSClientFactory singleton not safe for multi-tenant Django; 12 convenience methods add no value
description:
aws_client_factory.py:377-401 - Global singleton with double-checked locking. In multi-tenant Django where different requests use different AWS credentials, all tenants share the same factory instance and its default_region.

aws_client_factory.py:188-274 - 12 convenience methods (get_ecs_client, get_ecr_client, etc.) are all single-line wrappers around get_client(). 90 lines of code with zero additional logic. Callers can just use factory.get_client('ecs', ...).

ecr_service.py:590-615 - get_account_id() duplicates STS call already in factory's validate_credentials().
close_reason: Factory cleanup complete

title: Minor code quality: inline imports, silent parse defaults, model validation gaps, ECSService name collision
description:
Scattered minor issues:
- ecs_service.py, ecs_deployment_service.py, alb_service.py, service_connect_service.py: 'import json', 'import time', 'from botocore...' inside method bodies instead of module top
- compose_converter.py:731-738, 884: _parse_memory and _parse_duration silently return defaults (512, 30) on unrecognized formats with no warning
- ecs.py:374-385: No model validation ensuring min_count <= desired_count <= max_count
- ecs.py:299: to_aws_format silently falls back to ['FARGATE'] when requires_compatibilities is empty list
- models/ECSService vs services/ECSService name collision forces alias gymnastics everywhere
- infrastructure.py:64-66: VPCInfrastructure.all_subnet_ids can crash if JSON fields contain None
- efs_service.py:522: Uses MD5 for client token (not security-critical but triggers scanners, use sha256)
- exceptions.py: Error code ranges documented in comments but never enforced (code parameter always defaults to None)
- pipeline steps store mutable instance state (_created_access_points, _created_services) that accumulates across reuse
- image_build_service.py:633: ECR URI pattern uses hyphen separator while pipeline uses slash — different repos for same service
- infrastructure.py:188-218: ProvisionALBStep uses click.echo directly instead of pipeline event system
close_reason: All minor code quality fixes applied

title: Tracking models: ResourceMetric has 3 copy-pasted factory methods; BuildRecord.mark_skipped abuses error_message field; no data retention
description:
tracking.py:572-653 - record_ecs_metric, record_efs_metric, record_cluster_metric are copy-pasted with only FK difference. Consolidate into _record_metric(target_type, target, ...).

tracking.py:244 - mark_skipped re-purposes error_message for skip reason (comment says 'Re-use field for skip reason'). Use metadata JSONField or add skip_reason field.

tracking.py - ResourceMetric has no data retention strategy. Time-series table grows unboundedly. Need cleanup job or documented retention policy.

tracking.py:112-115 - BuildRecord.build_log is unbounded TextField. Docker build logs can be megabytes. Consider truncation on save or offload to object storage.
close_reason: Tracking model cleanup complete

description:
tests/fixtures/start_simpli_compose.yml and start_simpli_service_config.yml are named and structured for one specific project. Rename to generic names (multi_service_compose.yml, etc.) and replace startsimpli-specific values.

Compose fixture has inline password-like values (POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secretpassword, DJANGO_SECRET_KEY: test-secret-key) — replace with obviously-fake tokens.

Cluster fixture duplicated between test_compose_converter_per_service.py:64-75 and test_infrastructure_services.py:43-53. make_preprocessed helper duplicated between test_deployment_order.py:44 and test_compose_converter_per_service.py:27. Move shared fixtures to conftest.py.
close_reason: Test fixture cleanup complete

title: describe_tasks does not batch — will fail for >100 task ARNs
description: ecs_service.py:829-849 passes all task ARNs to describe_tasks. AWS API accepts max 100 per call. >100 ARNs will cause rejection. Fix: chunk task_arns into batches of 100.

title: _wait_for_alb_active has no failure state detection
description: alb_service.py:454-483 only checks for 'active' state. Does not detect 'failed' or 'provisioning_failed' states. If ALB enters terminal failure, waits full timeout with generic message instead of actual failure reason. Fix: detect failure states and raise with specific error.

title: tracking.py 619 lines (3 models) + ecs models 917 lines (5 models) — borderline
description: tracking.py has BuildRecord (247), DeploymentEvent (190), ResourceMetric (182). ecs.py has ECSCluster (152), ECSTaskDefinition (160), ECSService (292), ECRRepository (105), EFSFileSystem (188). Not critical but navigation harder. Consider splitting ECR/EFS into own files.

title: poll_until raises generic TimeoutError instead of custom exception
description: utils/polling.py:31 raises builtin TimeoutError. Rest of codebase uses ECSDeploymentTimeoutError, DeploymentTimeoutError, SSHTimeoutError. Callers must catch both. Fix: accept timeout_exception_class parameter defaulting to TimeoutError.

title: AuditLog doesn't extend TimestampedModel + duplicate index on aws_instance_id
description: 1) audit.py:9 AuditLog extends models.Model directly, every other model uses TimestampedModel. 2) targets.py:58 has db_index=True on aws_instance_id AND line 103 includes it in Meta.indexes — duplicate index wastes storage. 3) Only ECR/EFS models have __repr__, rest rely on __str__. Fix: extend TimestampedModel, remove duplicate index, add __repr__.

title: No cleanup on partial VPC provisioning failure
description: vpc_service.py:102-241 if provision_vpc fails midway (NAT Gateway creation fails), already-created VPC/subnets/IGW are orphaned. ClientError handler at line 237 does not attempt cleanup. Fix: add try/except calling teardown_vpc on failure, or log which resources were created.

title: VPC subnet CIDRs hardcoded to 10.0.x.x, won't work with different VPC CIDR
description: vpc_service.py:29-32 hardcodes PUBLIC_SUBNET_1_CIDR='10.0.1.0/24' etc. If different VPC CIDR passed to provision_vpc, subnets may not be within VPC range. Fix: derive subnet CIDRs from vpc_cidr using ipaddress.ip_network.

title: Pipeline __init__.py re-exports everything — slow startup
description: deployment_pipeline/__init__.py imports all step classes and all context classes. Importing PipelineContext triggers loading every step module, which triggers lazy imports of all services. Fix: keep __init__.py minimal (core classes only), let consumers import steps from .steps explicitly.

title: RecordDeploymentFailureStep defined but never used in any pipeline
description: finalization.py:107-139 defines RecordDeploymentFailureStep, exported in __all__, but not included in any of the four PipelineBuilder definitions. InitializeDeploymentStep.cleanup() handles failure recording instead. Fix: integrate into pipeline failure path or remove.

title: deploy --services uses comma-separated string instead of Click multiple
description: cli.py:597 uses click.option with manual comma splitting. Click supports multiple=True which is more idiomatic: --services web --services worker. Integrates with completion and help.
